The centralized-dependent governance model means Frax DAO retains the keys to custodian approvals, which is the one thread connecting this otherwise institutional-grade product to its wilder ancestry.

usyc-hashnote.title: Billions Without a Swap Pool
usyc-hashnote.text: Hashnote's USYC has swelled to $2.66B in tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} backing — the largest such product by circulation — with zero DEX pools and a deliberate institutional-only profile. Hashnote's USYC has swelled to $2.66 billion — the largest tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} product by circulation — while maintaining exactly zero DEX pools and deployment on just two chains. The B- safety grade at 69 on a product backed entirely by T-bills and reverse repos continues to puzzle until you realize the score is penalizing everything the product deliberately doesn't do: decentralize, provide on-chain liquidity, or publish proof of reserves beyond its own API price feed. Supply grew 17% month-over-month from $2.27B, suggesting institutional demand that doesn't need or want DEX exit routes. At 3.19% APY via NAV appreciation (net of a 50% performance fee) on a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} token, USYC is functionally a Bermuda-licensed {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} that happens to be an ERC-20 and a BEP-20 with {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} as its only transparency layer. The Circle branding now appearing on its DefiLlama listing hints at strategic alignment that could eventually reshape how this product reaches the market.

eurr-stablr.title: Malta's Euro Bet
eurr-stablr.text: EURR is StablR's Malta MFSA MiCA euro stablecoin with Grant Thornton {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} — distinguished mostly by Tether's strategic backing. StablR's EURR is backed 100% by fiat euro at European financial institutions under a Malta MFSA EMI license with MiCA compliance and Grant Thornton attestations — the same regulatory infrastructure as its dollar sibling USDR, with Tether's strategic investment providing both capital and the awkward question of whether a Tether-backed entity can win institutional trust in a market built on regulatory purity. Ethereum-only deployment with institutional-regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} gives EURR clean infrastructure, but the euro stablecoin market remains a fraction of the dollar market, and competition from Circle's EURC, SocGen's EURCV, and Banking Circle's EURI means EURR must differentiate on something beyond compliance alone. The Tether connection is both asset and liability — distribution relationships and brand recognition offset by the regulatory scrutiny that follows Tether everywhere. Whether Malta's MFSA license carries the same weight as France's ACPR or the Netherlands' DNB in the MiCA credibility hierarchy remains the competitive question.

usdr-stablr.title: MiCA Compliant, Market Indifferent
usdr-stablr.text: StablR's USDR is Malta MFSA EMI-licensed under MiCA with 100% cash and short-term EU government bond reserves audited by Grant Thornton -- credentialing without adoption at $6M supply. StablR's USDR holds a Malta MFSA EMI license under MiCA with 100% reserves in cash and short-term government bonds audited by Grant Thornton -- a regulatory stack including formal {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} that checks every European compliance box while the market barely notices at $6 million in supply. The WATCH stress band at 17 and 26 depeg events including a brutal 1,058-basis-point downside deviation reveal a single Ethereum pool with $1 million in TVL struggling to maintain any semblance of peg discipline. The liquidity score of 19 with perfect concentration in one pool means any meaningful exit runs through StablR's own issuer API {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route rather than on-chain. Europe's MiCA framework was supposed to be the catalyst for regulated stablecoins, and USDR has the credentials to benefit -- but credentialing and adoption remain stubbornly separate problems at this scale.

usdo-openeden.title: Treasury Yield, Repackaged
usdo-openeden.text: OpenEden's USDO is a rebasing {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}}-backed stablecoin distributing yield daily, with Bermuda DABA licensing and Chainlink PoR -- elegant for retail but awkward for DeFi. OpenEden's USDO is a rebasing stablecoin fixed at $1 that distributes T-bill yield daily by increasing holder balances -- backed 70% by OpenEden's own TBILL tokens, 15% by BlackRock BUIDL, 5% by Franklin Templeton BENJI, and 10% in USDC as a cash buffer. The Bermuda BMA DABA license and Chainlink Proof of Reserves provide regulatory and transparency layers that most rebasing stablecoins lack, with on-chain {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} of the underlying {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} basket, though the peg score of 81 and 44 depeg events -- including one that spiked nearly 17,000 basis points above peg -- reveal the mechanical challenge of maintaining a $1 price on a token whose supply changes daily. The backstop scores a modest 52 with capacity issues, reflecting the illiquidity gap between holding tokenized treasuries and providing instant dollar {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}}. Deployed across four chains, USDO is elegant for retail but awkward for DeFi protocols that don't handle rebasing tokens -- hence the cUSDO wrapper for composability.

usda-anzens.title: Cardano's Lonely Dollar
usda-anzens.text: Cardano's only MSB-licensed dollar with clean BitGo-custodied reserves and the worst peg record on Pharos, dragged by absent DeFi depth. Anzens USDA offers the cleanest reserve on Cardano -- 60% USD cash, 40% U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills, all {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}-managed by BitGo Trust under a FinCEN MSB license -- and the messiest peg record on the entire dashboard: 605 depeg events with deviations hitting -1704 bps on the downside and +2558 bps on the upside. The problem isn't the backing; it's the chain. A single DEX pool with $424K in TVL and Cardano-only deployment mean there is no meaningful arbitrage infrastructure to enforce the peg, producing a C safety grade at 56 despite reserves that would earn a much higher mark on any chain with real DeFi depth. Supply has shrunk 11% week-over-week to $9.5M, and the only exit is KYC-verified bank transfers through Anzens for {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} with multi-day settlement. USDA is proof that sound reserves are necessary but nowhere near sufficient -- you also need a market that can actually trade the thing.

usdf-falcon.title: Ethena's Wilder Cousin
usdf-falcon.text: Falcon's USDf cranks the {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} dial: 15% in altcoin shorts on CEXes alongside BTC/ETH hedges, with $1.79B supply persistently trading below peg and a narrow whitelisted exit. Falcon Finance takes the {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} playbook and cranks the risk dial: 45% BTC shorts, 30% stablecoins, 5% ETH shorts, 5% tokenized Treasuries, and the part that separates it from Ethena -- 15% in altcoins like DOGE, FET, TRX, and TON, each hedged with {{term:perpetual}}perp{{/term}} shorts on centralized exchanges where liquidity can vanish in a single cascade. At $1.79 billion in supply (up 2.6% weekly) with a B- safety grade at 68, Falcon has grown into a top-tier stablecoin by AUM while carrying exotic collateral quality and DEWS at 27 in the Watch band -- the only billion-dollar stablecoin persistently trading below peg at $0.998. The 5.7% sUSDf yield attracts capital, but the whitelisted-onchain {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop scores just 65 with only 3.3% immediate capacity, meaning the exit door is narrow relative to the room's occupancy. Real-time reserve transparency via ht.digital is a genuine differentiator, though 37 depeg events and a worst deviation of -265 bps suggest the altcoin hedging strategy occasionally stumbles where BTC-only approaches wouldn't.

europ-schuman.title: Credentials Without Scale
europ-schuman.text: EUROP is Schuman Financial's ACPR-licensed euro stablecoin backed by euro cash at EU banks — credentials in abundance, market share negligible. Schuman Financial stacks every credential the euro stablecoin market demands — ACPR EMI license from France, KPMG {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, 98% of reserves in euro cash at Societe Generale and peer EU banks, a 2% buffer beyond par — and still sits at barely 8.6M EUR circulating, roughly the size of a mid-tier DeFi protocol's {{term:treasury}}treasury{{/term}}. The B grade at 73 places EUROP in the same safety tier as EURC and Eurite, which is precisely the problem: when three euro stablecoins score identically on safety but differ by orders of magnitude in scale, the credentials become table stakes rather than differentiators. DEWS Watch at 20 and 28 depeg events with a worst drawdown of 229 bps reflect the thin-market volatility endemic to sub-$10M stablecoins, not structural instability. The five-chain deployment including XRPL and Plasma is an unusual distribution bet — reaching beyond EVM chains where the established euro competitors have not yet planted flags.

brz-transfero.title: Pegged to Volatility Itself
brz-transfero.text: BRZ is Transfero's centralized Brazilian real stablecoin, redeemable 1:1 by KYC'd users against BRL cash held in regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at a Brazilian institution — its depeg history is FX volatility, not reserve failure. BRZ's 184 depeg events -- including swings of nearly 10,000 basis points below peg and 7,800 above -- are not evidence of product failure but of what happens when you peg a token to the Brazilian real and price it against dollar-denominated markets. The D safety grade at 48 is largely a function of FX-driven peg volatility rather than reserve inadequacy, since BRZ is backed 100% by BRL cash at a Central Bank of Brazil-authorized institution with Swiss VQF registration. The practical exit story is grim: under $200K in effective DEX TVL across 14 pools, a 1% {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fee through Transfero's offchain issuer path, and a liquidity score of 21 mean any position of size is essentially trapped until someone wants to buy it on the secondary market. Deployed across 14 chains with nearly 300 million reais in circulation, BRZ serves a genuine need in Latin America's largest crypto market -- but the DEWS Watch band at 29 and razor-thin liquidity are a standing reminder that non-USD stablecoins carry risks no reserve structure can hedge away.

rlusd-ripple.title: The Institutional On-Ramp
rlusd-ripple.text:
Ripple's NYDFS-supervised dollar has grown to $1.4B with a pristine T-bill/MMF/cash reserve, but DEX liquidity is concentrated and supply flows look lumpy — a settlement token, not a DeFi primitive.

Ripple's RLUSD has grown to $1.4B in circulation on just two chains, backed by a pristine 100% very-low-risk reserve split across {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, government {{term:money-market-fund}}money market funds{{/term}}, and cash under NYDFS supervision with BPM LLP {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}. The B+ report card at 75 and CALM stress band reflect the structural strength you'd expect, but the 54 depeg events -- including a 636 bps upward spike during early price discovery -- are a reminder that even well-collateralized tokens need time to build secondary market depth. DEX liquidity of $96M across only 4 pools (HHI 0.89) is heavily concentrated, which is consistent with RLUSD's design as a payments corridor token rather than a DeFi primitive. Supply dipped 8.5% from last month's $1.55B, suggesting institutional flows are lumpy rather than sticky -- the kind of pattern you see when a token is being used for settlement and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rather than held as a reserve asset.

feusd-felix.title: Liquity Fork on Hyperliquid
feusd-felix.text: feUSD is a Liquity-v2-fork {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dollar on Hyperliquid, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} by HYPE ecosystem tokens — concentrated chain risk, sturdy redemption mechanics. Felix Protocol cloned Liquity V2 onto Hyperliquid's unproven L1 and loaded the CDPs with 60% HYPE ecosystem tokens — an asset class Pharos rates very-high risk — alongside bridged BTC, ETH, and SOL. The result is a $75M stablecoin with 339 depeg events and a worst deviation of 473 bps positive, currently trading at $0.994. The 93-rated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop is genuinely strong for a DeFi-native coin, with zero-fee atomic collateral redemption and an interest-rate-sorted queue. But the B safety grade tells the real story: when your primary collateral is the native token of the chain you live on, a single ecosystem shock hits both your backing and your exit {{term:liquidation}}liquidity simultaneously{{/term}}. Fifteen DEX pools rated fallback-class with 0.27 HHI concentration means getting out fast is not a given.

dusd-standx.title: The Quiet Basis Trader
dusd-standx.text: DUSD is StandX's delta-neutral synthetic dollar; Ethena-style basis trade through Ceffu custody, no token, no published proof of reserves. StandX runs the Ethena playbook through Ceffu {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} with one critical difference: no governance token, no points program, no yield sharing — just a $99M {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} stablecoin where 95% of reserves are active spot-long/perp-short positions on BTC, ETH, SOL, and BNB with a 5% stability buffer. The D grade at 49 is the honest assessment: CEX custody, exotic collateral, no published proof of reserves, and a {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop scoring 57 via an issuer API with same-day settlement and only 5% immediate capacity. The peg record is actually clean — just 7 depeg events with the worst at 181 bps above peg — which suggests the Goldman Sachs and Binance Futures alumni running the desk know what they are doing, provided the infrastructure beneath them holds. DEWS Calm at 12 and stable supply near $99M say the market trusts the trade for now, but trust and verification are different things entirely. This is a {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} expressed through CEX {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} futures.

eurcv-societe-generale-forge.title: SocGen’s Blockchain Experiment
eurcv-societe-generale-forge.text: EURCV is SG-FORGE's MiCA EUR stablecoin; reserves held in EUR cash at SocGen itself, top institutional safety with thin DEX liquidity. EUR CoinVertible is issued by SG-FORGE, the digital asset arm of a systemically important European bank, with reserves held 100% in euro cash at Société Générale itself — institutional-top {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} that earns the highest marks available in both resilience and dependency risk. The B safety grade makes EURCV one of the highest-rated euro stablecoins on Pharos, held back primarily by the expected F in decentralization — an inevitable trade-off when a 160-year-old bank decides to issue tokens on public blockchains. The DEWS stress reading is among the lowest on the entire dashboard, suggesting the product is operationally serene despite the thin DEX liquidity that plagues most euro stablecoins. Deployed across Ethereum, XRPL, Stellar, and Solana with MiCA EMI licensing from France’s ACPR, whether EURCV is the future of tokenized money or a corporate innovation lab’s pet project depends on whether SocGen commits distribution resources that match its regulatory credentials. Direct 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through SG-FORGE.

yusd-aegis.title: Funding Rate Roulette
yusd-aegis.text:
A delta-neutral BTC-collateralized synthetic dollar with best-in-class proof-of-reserves but a D grade — yield is funding-rate roulette priced into the score.

Aegis YUSD is a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} stablecoin built entirely on BTC — spot long at Fireblocks, Copper, and Ceffu under institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} hedged by COIN-M {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} shorts — which means the D grade at 46 is the market's verdict on using an active {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} position as collateral. The 28 depeg events with a worst of -977 bps and +1705 bps tell the story of a token whose peg stability is a function of {{term:funding-rate}}funding-rate{{/term}} economics and exchange availability, not reserve quality. Real-time proof-of-reserves through Accountable is genuinely best-in-class transparency — you can watch the positions live, which is more than Ethena offers — but transparency doesn't reduce the underlying risk of CEX custody concentration. The 3.78% APY on a D-rated token produces a yield-to-risk ratio of 0.066, which is the market correctly pricing in the scenario where negative funding rates eat the insurance fund faster than it refills.

reusd-resupply.title: Leverage All the Way Down
reusd-resupply.text:
A CDP coin minted against Curve Lend and Fraxlend vault shares — recursive yield wrapped in a token, with a 1% redemption-fee floor.

Resupply's reUSD wraps Curve Lend and Fraxlend vault shares into a dollar token whose collateral is itself earning yield on other stablecoins -- turtles of leverage atop a 1% {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fee floor sourced from a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} architecture. The C report card at 59 and 703 depeg events tell the tale of exotic collateral doing exotic things, though supply has stabilized around $35M after a slight contraction from last week's $37M. DEX liquidity is concentrated (HHI 0.59) across just 6 pools with an effective TVL of only $825K, meaning any serious exit would blow through the order book. The DEWS Watch band at 24 and a yield-to-risk ratio under 0.02 suggest the market correctly prices reUSD as a recursive instrument rather than a stable store of value -- you hold this to farm, not to park.

tbill-openeden.title: T-Bills With a Token Wrapper
tbill-openeden.text: a tokenized BVI Treasury fund managed by BNY Investment Management, KYC-gated and trading at NAV above $1 with zero secondary liquidity. OpenEden's TBILL holds $135M in short-dated {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills as a tokenized {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} managed by BNY Investment Management with institutional-top {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, trading at $1.14 as accumulated NAV appreciation pushes the token further above its original dollar price. The B+ report card at 75 with zero depeg events and zero DEX pools is the signature of a KYC-gated {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} fund structure that functions as intended: professional investors get 3.3% APY on-chain, and everyone else can look but not touch. Supply surged 67% from last month's $81M but pulled back from last week's $148M peak, showing the kind of institutional rebalancing flows that drive tokenized treasury products. The complete absence of secondary market liquidity is a feature, not a bug -- TBILL redeems through the issuer at a 5 bps fee with multi-day settlement under {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}-backed reporting, which is exactly how a regulated BVI fund should work.

a7a5-old-vector.title: The Sanctioned Dollar's Mirror
a7a5-old-vector.text: A7A5 is a centralized ruble stablecoin from Old Vector LLC, backed 1:1 by RUB deposits at sanctioned Russian state bank Promsvyazbank. A7A5 is a ruble-pegged stablecoin backed 100% by deposits at Promsvyazbank — a Russian state-owned bank under Western sanctions — which is why Pharos classifies its {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} as institutional-sanctioned and its reserve risk as very-high despite the collateral being plain fiat currency. Issued by Old Vector LLC under a Kyrgyz VASP license with quarterly audits from an independent Kyrgyz firm, the regulatory architecture is technically compliant with its home jurisdiction while being functionally untouchable by Western financial infrastructure. Since 2026-02-09 the issuer has passed through nearly all of the reserve yield to holders as additional A7A5 at the CBR key rate minus one percentage point — a step up from the previous 50% split that makes A7A5 one of the few {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} stablecoins whose holders directly capture a sanctioned bank's deposit rate. Whether A7A5 represents financial innovation for an isolated economy or sanctions evasion with a token wrapper depends entirely on whose compliance framework you're applying.

usd1-world-liberty-financial.title: The Presidential Stablecoin
usd1-world-liberty-financial.text: a Trump-affiliated dollar issued by BitGo Trust with very-low-risk T-bill reserves, structurally conventional but politically polarized. World Liberty Financial's USD1 arrived with the Trump family brand and proved that political controversy does not prevent a stablecoin from functioning: 100% very-low-risk reserves in {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills, {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} positions, and cash, custodied by BitGo under a South Dakota trust charter with regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and recurring {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. The irony is structural -- USD1 is, by the numbers, a perfectly conventional stablecoin with impeccable reserves and a near-perfect peg score, indistinguishable from any Paxos or Circle product except for the name on the letterhead. Supply has contracted by double digits recently, suggesting that the initial burst of politically motivated minting is unwinding as holders discover that USD1 earns no yield, has thinner DEX liquidity than competitors half its size, and offers issuer-only {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rather than an on-chain rail. Whether the brand is an asset or a liability depends on which side of the political aisle you mint from, but the B safety grade suggests the product itself is unremarkable in the best possible way.

usdx-hex-trust.title: Institutional Backing, Amateur Plumbing
usdx-hex-trust.text: Hex Trust's USDX has 80% T-bills and 20% cash at tier-1 banks, but a single DEX pool with $836 effective TVL means the peg trades at 28 cents on the dollar without anyone arbitraging it back. Hex Trust's USDX has 80% T-bills and 20% cash at global tier-1 banks under a Hong Kong TCSP license, which makes its D safety grade a case study in how clean reserves mean nothing without functional market infrastructure. Supply sits at $42.6M across three chains (Ethereum, Flare, Songbird), but the single DEX pool holding $200K with $836 in effective TVL is not a liquidity profile — it's a rounding error. The 838 depeg events and a worst deviation of 7,191 basis points tell the story of a stablecoin that periodically trades at 28 cents on the dollar despite holding T-bills at par. DEWS has pulled back from Warning to Watch at 26, but that improvement just means the bleeding slowed, not that it stopped. {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} from a Hong Kong TCSP-licensed {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} provider and 270+ institutional clients haven't translated into the on-chain arbitrage loops that keep prices honest, and same-day issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} cannot substitute for the missing secondary market — leaving USDX as expensive proof that custodial credibility and stablecoin stability are entirely different problems.

pusd-plume.title: USDC With a Detour
pusd-plume.text:
A USDC wrapper that routes through a Nucleus BoringVault with OFAC checks — extra trust layers on top of an asset that was already perfectly functional.

Plume's pUSD takes USDC, routes it through a Nucleus BoringVault with OFAC compliance checks, and issues a wrapped token on Ethereum and Plume Chain -- adding smart contract risk, {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} abstraction, and a new trust layer to an asset that was already perfectly functional. The C safety grade at 59 with zero-fee same-day {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and CALM DEWS at 2 suggest the wrapper works as designed, but 15 depeg events including a catastrophic 4,049-basis-point negative deviation reveal at least one moment when it emphatically did not. Supply has drifted down 9% month-over-month to $6.1M with $258K in effective DEX liquidity, raising the question of whether the RWAfi ecosystem narrative generates enough demand to justify the wrapper's existence. pUSD is a solution in search of a problem that Plume hasn't yet proven it has.

bold-liquity.title: Immutable Code, Perfect Scores
bold-liquity.text: BOLD is Liquity V2's decentralized dollar stablecoin, minted from immutable {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} vaults against WETH, wstETH, and rETH only — no governance keys, no admin functions, no RWA exposure. Liquity V2's BOLD is the highest-rated DeFi stablecoin on the dashboard, earning an A+ at 94 -- with a safety grade history that confirms this is structural, not a fluke. Backed by wstETH, WETH, and rETH in immutable contracts with no governance keys, no admin functions, and no RWA exposure, BOLD achieves what most decentralized stablecoins only aspire to: genuine peg stability alongside genuine decentralization, with just 6 depeg events recorded and none exceeding 134 basis points. The 90-rated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop with permissionless atomic collateral redemption at 50 bps provides the hardest peg floor in DeFi, while user-set interest rates and the Stability Pool yield mechanism (currently ~3.6% via Yearn's yBOLD) create self-correcting incentives that have kept BOLD remarkably close to par. Supply is growing modestly across seven chains, but the total remains small relative to the design's ambition -- proof that the market still prices convenience and composability above architectural purity.

avusd-avant.title: Avalanche's Quiet Contender
avusd-avant.text: avUSD is Avant's centralized dollar stablecoin, redeemable 1:1 for USDC and deployed into actively managed {{term:delta-neutral}}market-neutral{{/term}} strategies for yield — avUSD itself does not accrue yield, the staked savUSD does. Avant's avUSD is a USDC-backed base token for the Avant protocol, with deposited USDC routed into 0xPartners-managed market-neutral strategies and protected by a loss-absorption reserve. The token itself does not accrue yield: users stake avUSD into the separately tracked savUSD senior tranche when they want yield exposure, while avUSD remains the redeemable receipt for USDC exits at a 5-basis-point fee and one-to-seven-day settlement window. The institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and BVI domicile mean trust runs through Avant's operational integrity rather than a regulatory framework, which is why the backstop {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} remains queue-based rather than a hard on-chain par floor. Five recorded depegs, including one at 321 basis points below peg, show the market can still stress the wrapper even when the current peg score is high.

ylds-figure.title: The SEC-Registered Yield Coin
ylds-figure.text:
The only stablecoin registered under the 1933 and 1940 Acts — SOFR-minus-50bps via a face-amount certificate, with full KYC and zero DeFi composability as the price of legitimacy.

YLDS is that rarest of crypto products: a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing stablecoin{{/term}} registered under the Securities Act of 1933 and the Investment Company Act of 1940, paying SOFR minus 50 basis points through a fixed face-amount certificate structure that the SEC has explicitly blessed. The reserves are 86% overnight {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} repos and 13% {{term:money-market-fund}}money market funds{{/term}} at UMB Bank, KPMG-audited, with institutional-top custody — a {{term:rwa}}real-world-asset{{/term}} reserve stack so conservative it makes Circle look adventurous. Deployed on Solana and Provenance rather than Ethereum, YLDS targets a distribution path through Figure's existing lending platform rather than DeFi composability. The trade-off is clear: full SEC registration means mandatory KYC, restricted transferability, and zero DeFi integration, but for institutions that need a yield product whose legal status doesn't require a creative memo from outside counsel, YLDS is the only game in town.

usdq-quantoz.title: The Dutch Compliance Standard
usdq-quantoz.text: Quantoz's USDQ is DNB-supervised under MiCAR at 102% overcollateralization with EU/US sovereign bonds and Tier-1 bank deposits -- perfect peg score, modest distribution. Quantoz's USDQ holds the distinction of being supervised by De Nederlandsche Bank under MiCAR with reserves maintained at 102% overcollateralization -- 69% in Netherlands, German, and U.S. government bonds with 31% in cash at Tier 1 European banks, all held in segregated bankruptcy-remote accounts with institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. A perfect peg score of 100 with zero depeg events and zero {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fees makes USDQ the cleanest-performing USD stablecoin outside the top ten by every stability metric Pharos tracks. Deployed across Ethereum, Polygon, XRPL, and Algorand, the distribution is modest but the regulatory positioning is unmatched: DNB supervision, MiCAR compliance, regulatory {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, and a Visa principal membership for stablecoin-linked debit cards turn compliance into competitive advantage. Whether the Dutch compliance premium translates into adoption at scale depends on whether European crypto users value regulatory certainty enough to choose USDQ over the familiar convenience of USDC.

usdn-noble.title: Cosmos Dollar, Shrinking
usdn-noble.text: Noble's USDN is an IBC-native rebasing dollar backed 100% by {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} via M0, but supply has nearly halved in a month -- solid fundamentals, vanishing demand. Noble Dollar has shed nearly half its supply in a month, dropping from $25 million to $13.4 million, a trajectory that undercuts the bullish thesis for an IBC-native rebasing stablecoin backed 100% by {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} in bankruptcy-remote SPVs via M0. The B safety grade at 70 reflects solid fundamentals -- only 2 depeg events, CALM stress, real-time reserve verification through M0's dashboard with on-chain {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} -- but $26,000 in DEX TVL across a single pool with perfect concentration is barely a rounding error. The rebasing mechanism that passes T-bill yield directly to holders is an elegant design that should theoretically drive adoption, yet the supply contraction suggests Cosmos ecosystem demand alone cannot sustain it. Noble's proven IBC infrastructure has moved billions in USDC transfers, but USDN needs a reason for those dollars to stay as USDN rather than passing through.

usdu-unitas.title: The JLP Hedge Fund
usdu-unitas.text: Unitas's USDu routes 80% of USDC deposits into Jupiter LP tokens hedged by CEX perpetual shorts through Copper and Ceffu, a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} dressed up as a stablecoin. Unitas routes 80% of USDC deposits into Jupiter LP tokens — a basket of BTC, ETH, SOL, and USDC earning Jupiter Perps trading fees — while hedging the spot exposure with CEX {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} shorts through Copper and Ceffu off-exchange {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} settlement. The remaining 20% sits as margin for the short positions, making the entire reserve an active trading strategy with exotic collateral quality classification and zero idle assets. Singapore-domiciled with Accountable providing real-time zero-knowledge solvency proofs, USDu's transparency is a genuine upgrade over the 'trust us' school of yield products. Deployed on BSC and Solana with a peg score of 99 and only six depeg events, the machinery works — but the 80% dependency on USDC means every dollar of backing passes through Circle before reaching Jupiter's perps market, adding a layer of counterparty risk the hedge fund framing might obscure.

mnee-mnee.title: BSV Refugee, T-Bill Convert
mnee-mnee.text: Fiat-backed USD stablecoin with pristine T-bill plus cash reserves and Wolf and Company attestations, dragged down to a B- by Antigua licensing, institutional-unregulated custody, and near-zero on-chain liquidity. MNEE wraps 85% short-dated {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}} and 15% cash into a clean reserve profile attested by Wolf and Company -- the kind of composition that earns an A+ dependency score and a peg score of 97. The B- safety grade at 69 is a product of infrastructure, not reserves: Antigua FSRC licensing, institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and a single Ethereum deployment with effectively $17K in usable DEX liquidity leave holders dependent on issuer-API {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} as the only credible exit. Sixteen depeg events including a 601-basis-point plunge expose what happens when a $101M stablecoin has no on-chain arbitrage infrastructure to defend parity. MNEE proved a fiat-backed coin can have pristine reserves and still score like a mid-tier product when the plumbing around it is this thin.

usdg-paxos.title: Paxos's Singapore Sequel
usdg-paxos.text: Paxos's USDG is the Singapore sequel under MAS supervision, with all-very-low-risk reserves at DBS and Standard Chartered and a dual-jurisdiction MiCA EU issuance no competitor matches. After Binance's BUSD died under regulatory fire, Paxos relocated its stablecoin ambitions to Singapore, where USDG now sits under a MAS Major Payment Institution license with reserves split between DBS Bank and Standard Chartered -- institutional-top {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} that matches Circle and exceeds Tether. The all-very-low-risk reserve composition and A+ resilience grade make USDG structurally one of the safest stablecoins in existence, which makes the lowest peg score among rated top-ten coins a curious anomaly -- a brief tracking history with early growing pains rather than structural fragility. The zero-fee {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and additional EU issuance via a MiCA-compliant Finnish entity give USDG a dual-jurisdiction strategy that no competitor currently matches. The catch is on-chain presence: concentrated on just a few chains with modest DEX depth, USDG's institutional pedigree still outpaces its DeFi footprint.

xsgd-straitsx.title: Southeast Asia's FX Shortcut
xsgd-straitsx.text:
A MAS-licensed SGD stablecoin with DBS/StanChart reserves and twice-monthly attestations, earning a B+ on real Southeast Asian payment-corridor adoption.

XSGD is the rare non-USD stablecoin that exists for a reason beyond novelty — SGD-denominated on-chain liquidity for Southeast Asian payment flows where routing through dollar pairs adds pointless FX friction. The B+ at 76 is earned: MAS Major Payment Institution license, 100% reserves at DBS and Standard Chartered under regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and twice-monthly independent {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} to ISCA standards. Twenty-five depeg events with a worst of -733 bps and +1265 bps look alarming until you account for the inherent pricing challenges of a SGD token valued against USD-denominated oracles on thin non-USD pairs. The $1.76M DEX TVL across 24 pools with an impressively low 0.129 HHI shows genuine liquidity diversification, and the Grab partnership and OKX Pay integration push XSGD into real payment corridors where most stablecoins only write blog posts about going.

xusd-straitsx.title: Good Bones, No Tenants
xusd-straitsx.text:
Same MAS framework as XSGD, but $225K DEX liquidity in a single pool against $50M supply makes XUSD institutional plumbing without an on-chain audience.

StraitsX's XUSD inherits the same MAS framework, DBS/StanChart/UOB {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and institutional-top infrastructure as its XSGD sibling, with twice-monthly {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} reports, yet the B+ at 75 masks a liquidity crisis: $225K in DEX TVL with a 0.971 HHI means one pool holds essentially everything, and the 123 depeg events confirm what thin markets produce. The $50M circulating supply is respectable for a Singapore-issued dollar stablecoin, but it lives almost entirely off-chain — the on-chain footprint on Ethereum and BSC is a ghost town. XUSD's zero DEWS stress score and solid redemption backstop at 65 confirm the institutional plumbing works fine; the problem is that nobody building in DeFi has a reason to choose it over USDC. The value proposition is regional FX corridors and StraitsX's banking relationships, not DEX composability — a perfectly valid business, just not one that shows up in on-chain metrics.

vgbp-vnx.title: The Loneliest Pound
vgbp-vnx.text: VNX's VGBP is on-chain British sterling on Base and Celo at 172K GBP circulating — a proof of concept that GBP can exist on-chain at all, under FMA TVTG licensing. VGBP occupies one of the emptiest niches in stablecoins: on-chain British sterling, where the competition is essentially nobody. At 172K GBP circulating on Base and Celo with $33K in DEX TVL, this is less a stablecoin and more a proof of concept that GBP can exist on-chain at all. The AREVA-audited GBP cash reserves at Swiss and Liechtenstein banks under FMA TVTG licensing provide more {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} infrastructure and formal {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} than the token's market presence would seem to justify, and same-day issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} adds a clean exit path nobody is using. DEWS Watch band at 18 flags thin-market fragility rather than reserve concern. The UK's stablecoin regulatory framework remains the wildcard — if it invites high-street banks to issue tokenized sterling, VGBP's first-mover advantage evaporates overnight. Until then, VNX holds the field by default in a market nobody has shown up to contest.

cusd-cap.title: The Stablecoin Basket Case
cusd-cap.text: cUSD is Cap's diversified basket of regulated stablecoins and tokenized T-bill funds; clever distribution if everything works, shared contagion if one fails. Cap's cUSD is a basket wrapper backed by 35% USDC, 25% USDT, 20% BlackRock's BUIDL, 10% WisdomTree's WTGXX, and 10% PayPal's PYUSD — five institutional-grade stablecoins blended into a single token with a maximum 40% concentration cap per asset. The dynamic-fee vault mechanism adjusts minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} costs in real-time to prevent full utilization, ensuring atomic redemptions remain available, while EigenLayer AVS provides the economic security layer. Redemptions return a proportional basket of all underlying assets rather than a single stablecoin, which socializes any individual reserve depeg across all redeemers — clever risk distribution if everything works, shared contagion if one component fails. Deployed on Ethereum and MegaETH with wrapper-classified governance, cUSD is less an independent stablecoin and more a diversification instrument for holders who want institutional {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} exposure without choosing sides. The BUIDL and WTGXX slices are tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market funds{{/term}}.

msusd-main-street.title: USDC Base, Strategy Token Above
msusd-main-street.text: Main Street's USDC-backed dollar layer mintable and redeemable 1:1 by verified users; strategy risk lives in the separate msY staking token, not here. Main Street USD is the liquid stablecoin in Main Street's two-token design: unstaked msUSD is described by the issuer as 1:1 backed by USDC and directly mintable or redeemable by verified users via {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} flows. The options-box strategy risk belongs to the separate msY staking token, where users opt into NAV-accreting {{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}} after depositing msUSD. That distinction matters for Pharos scoring because msUSD should be modeled as a USDC-backed redemption asset, while msY carries the strategy exposure.

iusd-infinifi.title: Credit Fund in Token Clothing
iusd-infinifi.text: USDC-collateralized dollar with duration-matched private credit deployment; ~20% liquid reserves, 30-day unwind windows, queued redemptions under stress. InfiniFi's iUSD deploys USDC reserves into institutional private credit -- Fasanara, FalconX, Sentora, Maple -- with a liquid DeFi buffer on Spark, Fluid, and Aave to service redemptions, paying 5.78% APY through its siUSD savings wrapper. The structural tension is immediate: only 19.6% of reserves are available for instant withdrawal, meaning four-fifths of the backing is locked in credit strategies with 30-day unwind windows. Supply has contracted sharply from $173M to $109M in a single month, a 37% drawdown that tests whether the fractional liquid reserve model actually works under redemption pressure. The WATCH-band DEWS score of 18 and B safety grade at 70 reflect this managed stress -- the yield-to-risk ratio of 0.12 is competitive, but you're earning credit fund returns and bearing credit fund risks through a stablecoin interface. No depeg events recorded yet, which either means the queue system is working exactly as designed or that the real stress test hasn't arrived. Functionally siUSD is a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper over private-credit {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} positions, with the buffer-driven {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} queue acting as the gate when liquid reserves run thin.

pht-pht.title: Peso Stablecoin Pioneer
pht-pht.text:
A MakerDAO-fork Philippine peso CDP coin backed by apcxUSDT — a custodial USDT wrapper that adds a layer between holders and Tether.

PHT is a Philippine peso-pegged stablecoin built on a MakerDAO MCD fork, backed 100% by apcxUSDT (a 1:1 custodial USDT wrapper) in {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} vaults with Chainlink oracle price feeds and LayerZero OFT {{term:bridge}}bridging{{/term}}. The reserve is technically high-risk not because USDT is unstable but because the apcxUSDT wrapper adds a custodial layer between PHT holders and the underlying Tether. CoinGecko and DefiLlama now show live Ethereum, Polygon, and Tron coverage, so Pharos models it as a multichain local-currency stablecoin while keeping {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} coverage conservative.

hyusd-hylo.title: Staked SOL, Stable Dollar
hyusd-hylo.text: Solana LST-backed dollar with xSOL absorbing SOL volatility; oracle-free, admin-free, only three depeg events on record. Hylo's hyUSD converts Solana staking yield into dollar stability through a dual-token design where xSOL absorbs SOL's volatility so hyUSD doesn't have to -- backed entirely by a basket of liquid staking tokens (mSOL, JitoSOL, bSOL, JupSOL) at 150%+ overcollateralization with no upstream stablecoin dependencies. The B safety grade at 70 with only three depeg events (worst: -171 bps) is a quietly remarkable result for a stablecoin whose entire backing is volatile crypto. DAO governance and the absence of admin keys earn genuine decentralization marks, a rarity among crypto-backed competitors. The WATCH-band DEWS at 19 and a slight monthly supply contraction from $17M to $15.5M suggest Hylo is in a consolidation phase rather than a growth one, while $3.1M in DEX TVL across six pools provides adequate but not deep exit liquidity for the current supply. Oracle-free and admin-free is an elegant thesis -- the question is whether the Solana LST ecosystem remains healthy enough to keep the collateral basket liquid. Mechanically this is a dual-token {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with explicit {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} and xSOL absorbing {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} burden ahead of hyUSD holders.

meusd-mezo.title: Bitcoin Maxis Get CDPs
meusd-mezo.text: Liquity-style BTC-backed CDP stablecoin on Mezo's Bitcoin L2, with sound redemption mechanics capped by an unproven-chain penalty; persistent above-peg drift from defensive overcollateralization. Mezo's meUSD applies Liquity-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics to Bitcoin collateral -- 110% minimum ratio, permissionless {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at 75 bps, atomic settlement -- across wrapped BTC variants on a Bitcoin L2 that Pharos classifies as unproven. The C+ grade at 63 with an 87-rated backstop tells a split story: the redemption architecture is sound, but the unproven chain penalty caps the ceiling on what is otherwise a competently designed system. At $18.9M circulating with 184 depeg events and a worst positive deviation of +504 bps, meUSD exhibits the above-peg drift typical of BTC-backed CDPs -- borrowers overcollateralize defensively when Bitcoin volatility spikes, pushing the token above par. DEWS reads a calm 13 and supply has been flat for months, suggesting meUSD has found its equilibrium as a niche product for BTC holders who want dollar-denominated leverage without selling their stack. The two-chain deployment across Ethereum and Mezo is pragmatic, though $4.9M in DEX liquidity spread across seven pools remains thin for any serious exit scenario.

usdu-usdu-finance.title: Undercollateralized by Design
usdu-usdu-finance.text: USDU Finance is an intentionally undercollateralized stablecoin at roughly 43% backing, minted through DAO-approved adapters into Curve, TermMax, and Morpho vault positions for professional risk-takers. USDU Finance is refreshingly honest about what it is: an intentionally undercollateralized stablecoin at roughly 43% backing, minted through DAO-approved adapters connected to Curve, TermMax, and Morpho vault positions, designed explicitly for professional market participants who can price the risk. The C safety grade at 55 with $31,000 in DEX TVL and 84% pool concentration in a single venue means exit liquidity is essentially nonexistent for any meaningful position. Supply has been flat at $5 million for weeks, suggesting the professional audience it targets has sized their exposure and stopped. The modular adapter architecture is genuinely interesting engineering — dynamic Curve liquidity management, fixed-rate TermMax lending, Morpho vault integration — but building sophisticated infrastructure around a product that deliberately skips the {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} step is the kind of experiment that works until it doesn't.

uty-xsy.title: Frozen on the Avalanche
uty-xsy.text: XSY's UTY is an AVAX-hedged {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar custodied at Ceffu and Copper with a 7-day unbonding — supply has been flat at $20.97M to the penny for a month. XSY's UTY hasn't moved in a month — supply is $20.97M, identical to the penny across weekly and monthly snapshots, the kind of flatline that suggests a product in stasis rather than operation. The F safety grade at 37 pairs with a DEWS Watch score of 17, up from the previous zero, indicating that even dormant products can accumulate stress signals. The {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} AVAX {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} strategy (35% long spot, 35% short perps, 30% USDC) is custodied at Ceffu and Copper {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} with Accountable attestations, but the 7-day unbonding period and fallback-class DEX coverage at $8.3M total TVL with $730K effective make exit an exercise in patience. Thirty-five depeg events with a worst of 287 basis points positive and 110 negative are relatively contained for an F-rated coin, suggesting the peg mechanism works when anyone bothers to test it. UTY reads less like a stablecoin and more like a locked vault on a quiet mountain.

gusd-gate.title: Exchange Scrip, Treasury Wrapper
gusd-gate.text: Gate USD is Gate's {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} dollar minted 1:1 from USDT/USDC deposits, backed by 70% {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and 25% stablecoins with 5% opaque CEX-managed strategies. Gate USD functions less as a stablecoin and more as a yield certificate: users deposit USDT or USDC on Gate, receive GUSD, and reclaim principal plus interest at {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. The reserve is 70% short-term Treasuries and 25% stablecoin deposits, but that final 5% in undisclosed CEX-managed yield strategies is the opacity that drags the safety grade to C. At $158M circulating from the Cayman Islands with exactly one DEX pool (HHI of 1.0 — maximum possible concentration), the on-chain exit route is effectively decorative. Nine depeg events with a tight 171 bps worst deviation suggest the peg mechanism works, but only because almost nobody tries to exit through DeFi. The 65-rated offchain redemption via Gate's own platform means your exit depends entirely on the exchange remaining operational and willing.

usdcv-societe-generale-forge.title: TradFi's On-Chain Experiment
usdcv-societe-generale-forge.text: SocGen-FORGE's USDCV is MiCA-regulated bank-issued plumbing with cash at BNY Mellon, institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and the calmest stress reading on the dashboard -- distribution still trails the regulatory pedigree. USDCV is what happens when Europe's sixth-largest bank decides to issue a stablecoin: 100% USD cash at BNY Mellon in bankruptcy-remote segregated accounts, an ACPR-regulated EMI license under MiCA, and a DEWS score of 1 -- literally the calmest stress reading on the entire Pharos dashboard. The B safety grade at 72 is held back not by risk but by reach: $26M in supply, a single DEX pool with $2.3M TVL, two-chain deployment on Ethereum and Solana, and multi-day settlement through SG-FORGE's issuer portal backed by Deloitte {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}. Only 2 depeg events in its lifetime and a worst negative deviation of just -118 bps make it one of the most stable assets tracked, period. Supply grew 13% month-over-month from $23.3M, suggesting the MiCA framework is starting to drive institutional demand for a product whose on-chain liquidity still hasn't caught up with its regulatory pedigree.

usdai-usd-ai.title: The Liquid Half of USD.AI
usdai-usd-ai.text: the low-risk, non-yielding side of USD.AI, framed around a PYUSD settlement rail rather than the GPU-credit book held by sUSDai. Base USDai is the low-risk side of the USD.AI stack: a liquid, non-yielding token that current issuer materials frame around a PYUSD-led settlement rail rather than around the GPU-credit book itself. That distinction matters. The queue, the AI-infrastructure {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} returns, and the GPU-loan underwriting risk belong to sUSDai, not to the base token holders using USDai as a transactional dollar. The remaining question is operational rather than conceptual: how durable the PYUSD-side {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rail stays under stress, and how tightly the market continues to trust the separation between the liquid stablecoin layer and the higher-risk yield layer sitting beside it.

susdai-usd-ai.title: The GPU-Credit Sleeve
susdai-usd-ai.text: USD.AI's structured-credit sleeve, where holders trade an instant redeem rail for GPU-loan yield and a queued unstake. sUSDai is where USD.AI stops behaving like a plain stablecoin and starts looking like a structured credit product wrapped in token form. Holders are opting into {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} exposure sourced from GPU-backed infrastructure loans and accepting the trade-off that exits are governed by a queued unstake flow rather than the base token's instant {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rail. The live proof-of-reserves API now lists 35 hardware-financing deals across H200, B200, B300, RTX PRO, and RTX 5090 chips spanning multiple jurisdictions, with the GPU-loan share of backing materially larger than the 5.6% snapshot in earlier disclosures -- the PYUSD sleeve still softens liquidity management, but compute-financing is increasingly the defining exposure. That makes sUSDai less a digital cash instrument than a NAV-style income token whose real question is how resilient that GPU-credit pipeline remains through borrower stress, collateral {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}}, and scaling cycles.

usx-solstice.title: The Solana Wrapper
usx-solstice.text: Solstice's USX is a Solana wrapper minted 1:1 against 55% USDC and 45% USDT, with Chainlink Proof of Reserve and KYC-gated institutional minting — inheriting its underlying stablecoins' safety rather than creating its own. Solstice's USX is structurally simpler than its Swiss pedigree and Galaxy Digital backing might suggest: 55% USDC and 45% USDT, minted 1:1, with Chainlink Proof of Reserve verifying the reserves on-chain. Classified as a wrapper with governance quality reflecting its pass-through nature, USX inherits the safety profile of its underlying stablecoins rather than creating its own — which makes the value proposition a question of Solana-native convenience rather than novel design. The KYC-gated institutional minting at a $500K minimum coexists with permissionless DEX access, creating a two-tier system where large minters get direct access and everyone else trades the secondary market. Plans to expand collateral to SOL, ETH, and BTC would change the risk profile entirely, but for now USX is a regulated stablecoin wrapper on a chain that already has USDC and USDT.

hollar-hydrated.title: Aave Fork, Polkadot Address
hollar-hydrated.text: Aave V3 fork on Hydration with diversified DOT/ETH/BTC/stablecoin collateral and HSM-anchored peg swaps; chain risk caps the ceiling. HOLLAR is an Aave V3 fork running on Hydration, Polkadot's largest DeFi protocol, backed by a diversified basket of DOT, ETH, vDOT, wrapped BTC, and stablecoins with automated partial liquidations that fire every block. The C grade at 55 has improved since launch, while the Stability Module's backstop design earns structural marks -- but everything runs on a chain Pharos classifies as unproven, which anchors the ceiling. At $11.7M circulating and gently contracting (down 4% monthly), HOLLAR isn't growing so much as stabilizing in place, with $2.7M in DEX liquidity concentrated entirely in a single pool. Seven depeg events with a worst deviation of -691 bps show the peg holds most of the time but can slip when liquidity thins. HOLLAR's viability ultimately tracks whether Polkadot's DeFi ecosystem expands or contracts -- a bet that has not paid off for most Polkadot-native projects to date. The core mechanics are a multi-collateral {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with per-block partial {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}}, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}, and an HSM swap module acting like a {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}.

musd-metamask.title: Distribution as Moat
musd-metamask.text: Stripe Bridge-issued M0-rail dollar stablecoin distributed inside the MetaMask wallet, 85% T-bills + 15% bankruptcy-remote cash, with on-chain validator attestations and growing but still modest supply. MetaMask mUSD is what happens when a wallet with 30 million monthly users decides to vertically integrate -- issued by Stripe's Bridge on M0 protocol rails, with 85% in {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and 15% in bankruptcy-remote cash verified by real-time on-chain {{term:attestation}}validator attestations{{/term}}. The B safety grade at 70 reflects solid fundamentals: DEWS at a tranquil 5, institutional-regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and a reserve composition that reads like a compliance team's wishlist. Supply has climbed 19% month-over-month to $32M, still modest for a product with that distribution funnel, but the trajectory is clear. Nineteen depeg events including a 557-bps positive spike and 236-bps negative deviation show the secondary market hasn't caught up with primary market confidence -- $2.5M in effective DEX TVL across 21 pools means mUSD's liquidity is spread wide but runs shallow.

cash-phantom.title: The Wallet's Dollar
cash-phantom.text: CASH is Phantom's wallet-native dollar on Solana, T-bill backed by Bridge Building Inc.; distribution edge over decentralization. Phantom's CASH leverages what no DeFi protocol can replicate: distribution through crypto's most popular Solana wallet, giving millions of users a native stablecoin without requiring them to understand anything about stablecoin infrastructure. Under the hood, Bridge Building Inc. backs CASH with {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, reverse repos, {{term:money-market-fund}}government money-market funds{{/term}}, bank deposits, and a 10% allocation to tokenized treasuries including BUIDL -- 90% of reserves in very-low-risk assets with bankruptcy-remote segregation under FinCEN and state money transmitter licenses. The B- report card at 67 with just 10 depeg events (none exceeding 181 bps) and a DEWS score of 11 in CALM territory reflects a genuinely stable product, while over $72M in DEX liquidity across Solana pools provides workable exit depth. Solana-only deployment is a feature, not a limitation -- CASH exists to be Phantom's default dollar, and the growing supply suggests that for wallet-native users, the trade-off between decentralization purity and tap-to-buy convenience was decided before it was ever offered. Bankruptcy-remote {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} backs 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}; the BUIDL slice is a tokenized {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} exposure.

tgbp-tokenised.title: The FCA's First Bet
tgbp-tokenised.text: the UK's first FCA-registered stablecoin, 100% backed by GBP cash and gilts at Enumis, still a regulatory proof-of-concept at 15.8M GBP. BCP Technologies' tGBP remains the UK's first FCA-registered stablecoin, backed 100% by GBP cash and zero-coupon gilts with Enumis {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} across six chains -- but at 15.8M GBP in circulation, it is still a regulatory proof-of-concept in a dollar-denominated world. The B- report card at 69 with a DEWS Watch band at 25 reflects decent fundamentals constrained by scale: 24 depeg events with a worst miss of 265 bps and $1.4M in DEX TVL spread thinly across 9 pools. Supply grew 43% from last month's 11M GBP, which is notable momentum for a non-USD peg that most of DeFi ignores entirely. tGBP's significance remains less about today's numbers and more about the regulatory precedent -- every UK stablecoin issuer that follows will be benchmarked against this template, including its 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} promise.

eurau-allunity.title: Deutsche Boerse's Euro Bet
eurau-allunity.text: EURAU is AllUnity's MiCA-licensed EUR stablecoin; full-reserve bank deposits, broad L2 reach, top-tier institutional sponsorship. AllUnity's EURAU is backed 100% by euro deposits at CRR-eligible EU credit institutions, BaFin-licensed as an EMI under MiCA, with institutional-regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and integration into Deutsche Boerse's Clearstream infrastructure — more institutional credibility than most euro stablecoins combined. Backed by DWS (Deutsche Bank's asset management arm), Galaxy Digital, and Flow Traders, the sponsor list reads like a TradFi-crypto {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} roster. Deployed across five EVM chains (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon), EURAU has broader L2 reach than competing euro stablecoins that remain Ethereum-only. The problem is the denominator: euro stablecoins represent a fraction of the global stablecoin market, making EURAU simultaneously one of the best-backed euro tokens and a reminder of how thoroughly the dollar dominates this space. Direct 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through AllUnity.

usdh-native-markets.title: Stripe's Stablecoin Beachhead
usdh-native-markets.text: Native Markets' USDH on HyperEVM is a Bridge-issued (Stripe) dollar with 40% short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} at JP Morgan plus tokenized treasuries -- a bet on Hyperliquid traction beyond the current niche. USDH sits at $94 million on HyperEVM with one of the more credible reserve compositions in the market: 40% short-term T-bills managed by BlackRock at JP Morgan, 20% tokenized {{term:treasury}}treasuries{{/term}} via BUIDL and USTB, and the rest in cash, repos, and {{term:money-market-fund}}treasury funds{{/term}} -- all flowing through Bridge Building Inc., Stripe's stablecoin subsidiary. The 12 depeg events with swings as wide as 227 basis points tell the story of a young stablecoin on a single chain still building the arbitrage infrastructure to enforce its peg tightly. A 7.8% APY on Morpho lending at B- safety is a respectable yield-to-risk ratio, though the fallback-class DEX liquidity and concentrated pool structure mean size limits on exits remain real. The validator vote that chose USDH over Paxos and Ethena was a bet on revenue redirection from Circle -- whether that bet pays off depends on whether Hyperliquid's ecosystem grows beyond its current niche.

sbc-brale.title: Infrastructure Demo Reel
sbc-brale.text:
Brale's SBC tripled to $12.2M with very-low-risk reserves and broader chain distribution than tokens 50x its size — a reference implementation for its stablecoin-as-a-service platform.

Brale's SBC tripled from $3.9M to $12.2M in the past month -- the fastest proportional growth in this batch -- while maintaining a B safety grade at 73 with 100% very-low-risk reserves split evenly between cash and short-duration {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}}. Deployed across 10 chains from a FinCEN-licensed money transmitter with regulated bank {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and zero-fee {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, SBC has broader distribution than tokens fifty times its size, which is entirely the point: this is a reference implementation for Brale's stablecoin-as-a-service platform, not a consumer product. The 35 depeg events with a worst deviation of 450 bps and an effective DEX TVL of just $5M against that 10-chain footprint reveal the tension between distribution breadth and liquidity depth. SBC exists so Brale can tell enterprise clients their infrastructure works -- and the tripling supply suggests those conversations are landing.

euri-banking-circle.title: The Binance Distribution Play
euri-banking-circle.text: EURI is Banking Circle's MiCA-licensed euro stablecoin with fee-free 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} — a {{term:custody}}credit-institution{{/term}} wrapper engineered for Binance distribution. Eurite exists because Binance needed a MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin and Banking Circle had the Luxembourg CSSF credit institution license to provide one — 70% euro cash in segregated fiduciary accounts, 30% EU government securities, Ernst & Young {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, all the regulatory furniture arranged correctly. The B grade at 73 matches the euro stablecoin peer group exactly, though the liquidity score of 33 and an HHI of 0.82 reveal the gap between having Binance's endorsement and generating organic on-chain trading depth. Supply has held flat week-over-week at roughly 60M EUR while growing about 9% over the prior month, suggesting institutional minting in discrete blocks rather than organic retail demand. No depeg data, no yield product, deployment limited to Ethereum and BSC — Eurite is less a standalone stablecoin and more a compliance wrapper that lets Binance's European users stay in euros without leaving the exchange's orbit.

msusd-metronome.title: Synths Still Standing
msusd-metronome.text: Pre-yield-farming overcollateralized synth dollar minted against USDC, Vesper yield tokens, DAI, and ETH/BTC; no direct redemption, only debt repayment, with a recent supply spike that breaks years of stasis. Metronome's msUSD is a synthetic dollar from the pre-yield-farming era that somehow kept its users -- minted against 30% USDC, 25% Vesper yield tokens, 20% DAI, and 20% ETH/WBTC/sfrxETH via {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}, with no direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanism, only debt repayment. The C+ safety grade at 62 with balanced B+ scores across peg stability, liquidity, and resilience is remarkably consistent for a product this niche, though the B- in dependency risk reflects exposure to DAI, USDC, and the legacy FRAX in its collateral basket. Supply has spiked over 40% in a single week -- an unusual surge for a synthetic asset that most of DeFi has forgotten about, suggesting renewed interest or a single large minter. The zero-slippage intra-protocol synth swaps remain a neat trick in a market where synthetic assets have largely fallen out of fashion, and the 63-day peg streak shows the collateral-provider buyback mechanism is doing its job.

aznd-mu-digital.title: Asia Credit in a Token
aznd-mu-digital.text: AZND is Mu Digital's KYC-gated, NAV-bearing dollar token backed by a Singapore-regulated Asia credit fund, with a muBOND junior tranche absorbing first losses — structured credit dressed as a stablecoin. Mu Digital's AZND wraps an Asian credit fund into a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} stablecoin on Monad, managed by Singapore-regulated Golden Hill Asset Management with a muBOND junior tranche providing {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} -- it is a structured credit product wearing a stablecoin's clothing. Accountable's real-time dashboard currently shows reserves concentrated in short-term cash (81%) and liquid bonds (19%), a notably more conservative posture than the published mandate targeting up to 20% illiquid private credit. The B- report card at 67 with a 6.8% NAV-appreciation yield is credible for the risk class, though the single-chain Monad deployment, concentrated DEX liquidity (HHI of 0.72 across just 2 pools), and weekly KYC-gated {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}} settling over days mean exit options are genuinely constrained. Supply has contracted roughly 20% in the past week alone, suggesting early holders are testing those redemption mechanics in practice. AZND targets a real gap -- institutional Asian credit exposure on-chain -- but the question is whether DeFi-native capital will accept fund-style lockups for single-digit yields.

nect-beraborrow.title: Liquity on Life Support
nect-beraborrow.text: Liquity v2-style CDP stablecoin on Berachain backed by an exotic collateral zoo (iBGT, WBERA, BTC/ETH derivatives, LP tokens); sub-million supply and razor-thin liquidity stop the redemption mechanism from doing its job. BeraBorrow's NECT runs Liquity-v2 {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics on Berachain's exotic collateral zoo -- 40% iBGT, 25% WBERA, plus wrapped BTC variants, ETH derivatives, and Kodiak LP tokens, all classified high-risk on an unproven chain. The C- grade at 52 understates the challenge: 245 depeg events with a worst deviation of 757 bps mean NECT has spent more time away from peg than on it, though DEWS has calmed to 5 from its former Alert-band reading. At $512K in circulation with $246K effective DEX liquidity, the coin is barely above the threshold where the CDP {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanism can function as designed -- you need arbitrageurs to show up, and the economics don't justify it at this scale. The 84-rated collateral redemption backstop and {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} buffer remain structurally sound on paper, but sound mechanisms need liquid markets to express themselves.

usp-pikudao.title: Turkish Carry Trade, Tokenized
usp-pikudao.text: PikuDAO's USP is a NAV-appreciating token with 50% in a Turkish lira {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} via Balsa Technologies, 40% in DeFi protocols, and 10% in stablecoin buffer — KYC-gated with whitelisted queue redemption. PikuDAO's USP is a NAV-appreciating token — 50% deployed into a Turkish lira FX arbitrage strategy via Balsa Technologies ({{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} TRY/USD trades capturing Turkey's inflation-driven {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} carry), 40% across DeFi protocols (Giza, Almanak, USD.AI, Ethena, Aave, Cap), and 10% in a USDC/USDT buffer. The very-high risk classification on the Turkish FX strategy and high risk on the DeFi allocations are reflected in the exotic collateral quality rating and a backstop of 65 with whitelisted queue-based {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at 0.2% fee — KYC/KYB required to mint or redeem, with a 24-hour FIFO settlement queue. It's a genuinely novel yield source for DeFi — Turkish carry trade returns are uncorrelated with crypto markets — but also one that concentrates geopolitical and counterparty risk in a single emerging market whose currency has lost over 90% against the dollar in a decade. The NAV has appreciated above $1.07, which proves the strategy works when it works — the question is what happens when it doesn't.

pmusd-precious-metals.title: Gold Bars, Sky Strings
pmusd-precious-metals.text:
Gold-backed supply paired with a sUSDS-funded PSM means pmUSD's peg defense depends on Sky Protocol staying healthy — a meaningful external dependency.

pmUSD's structural design now runs on two incompatible logics: supply is backed by gold via RAAC's RWf(x) fork and ION.au tokenized claims, but peg defense relies on a {{term:psm}}Peg Stability Module{{/term}} that holds sUSDS -- Sky Protocol's {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} savings wrapper -- as its reserve asset. Arbitrageurs swap discounted pmUSD for sUSDS at a $1 internal valuation when the market price dips, but the flow is one-directional and automatically halts when sUSDS reserves fall below 20% of PSM assets, meaning the peg backstop has a backstop condition. That architecture ties pmUSD's dollar recovery mechanism to Sky Protocol's stability -- a meaningful external dependency for a coin that was previously modeled as self-backed in scoring. The D grade still reflects F scores in both resilience and decentralization, with over 450 depeg events accumulated since launch as gold's dollar-independent price movements create a structurally recurring gap to close. Real-time Chainlink Proof of Reserves and Instruxi {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} document the gold backing with genuine rigor; the question was never whether the gold is there, but whether a Sky-Protocol-dependent PSM is the right lever to close the gap between what gold is worth and what a dollar costs.

jupusd-jupiter.title: Three Layers to Treasuries
jupusd-jupiter.text: Solana dollar from Jupiter, 90% backed by Ethena USDtb (BlackRock BUIDL) + 10% USDC; pristine collateral buried under three wrappers. JupUSD is Jupiter's play to own Solana's dollar layer: 90% backed by Ethena's USDtb (itself a wrapper around BlackRock's BUIDL tokenized Treasury fund) with a 10% USDC buffer, custodied by Anchorage Digital. The dependency chain runs JupUSD to USDtb to BUIDL to actual government bonds -- pristine collateral buried under three layers of operational and counterparty risk. At $80M circulating and growing 11% month-over-month, adoption is real, with $12M in DEX TVL though heavily concentrated (HHI of 0.71) in a few pools. Eight depeg events with modest deviations (-202 to +158 bps) and a calm DEWS of 11 suggest a clean launch, while the 79-rated backstop offers atomic settlement through whitelisted on-chain redemption into stablecoins. The C+ grade at 63 prices in the dependency complexity and centralized governance -- Jupiter is betting that BlackRock's brand travels well enough through intermediaries that Solana users won't mind the wrapper tax. The reserve trace lands in BUIDL's {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} via Anchorage {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, with whitelisted atomic {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} into USDC as the peg floor.

u-united-stables.title: A Dollar Made of Dollars
u-united-stables.text: a BVI meta-stablecoin wrapping 35% USDC, 35% USDT, 15% USD1, and 15% fiat under a Bermuda trustee, slowly bleeding supply. United Stables wraps 35% USDC, 35% USDT, 15% World Liberty Financial's USD1, and 15% fiat into a single token -- a meta-stablecoin approaching $1B in circulation that adds BVI {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} risk on top of assets that already work fine on their own. The B- report card at 65 with zero depeg events and a CALM stress band at 11 reflects the paradox: the underlying collateral is solid, but the wrapper's unregulated Bermuda trustee and centralized governance subtract more safety than the aggregation adds. Supply has contracted 3% month-over-month from $1B to $973M, a slow bleed that coincides with the market questioning whether wrapper premiums justify their counterparty overhead. The 89-rated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop via atomic stablecoin-redeem is U's strongest selling point -- but it also highlights the circular logic of a product whose best exit is unwrapping back into the assets you could have held directly.

reusd-re-protocol.title: Insurance Capital Goes On-Chain
reusd-re-protocol.text:
A NAV-appreciating token splitting deposits 50/30/20 across ETH basis trades, T-bills, and a USDC buffer — a reinsurance float deployed across DeFi yield sources.

Re Protocol's reUSD channels deposits into a 50/30/20 split of {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} ETH {{term:basis-trade}}basis trades{{/term}} via sUSDe, short-duration T-bills, and a USDC instant-{{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} buffer -- a structure that reads like a reinsurance float deployed across DeFi yield sources. Trading at $1.072 as a NAV-appreciating token, the B- grade at 66 reflects exotic collateral quality and Ethena dependency, while 8.2% APY via Pendle and a 0.24 yield-to-risk ratio position it competitively in the {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} stablecoin field. Supply has surged 38% month-over-month to $177M across six chains, with $18M effective DEX TVL providing genuine secondary-market depth. The queue-based redemption with 20% immediate capacity and BVI FSC licensing won't satisfy institutional compliance teams, but the Chainlink/Network Firm real-time {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} layer and the genuinely uncorrelated reinsurance revenue stream make reUSD one of the more intellectually honest yield products on the market.

rwausdi-multipli.title: The RWA Middleware Layer
rwausdi-multipli.text:
A KYB-gated UAE wrapper aggregating 100+ tokenized T-bills, gold, and market-neutral funds — with a Lloyd's de-pegging insurance policy that's a genuinely novel backstop.

Multipli's rwaUSDi wraps 100+ tokenized treasury products, gold tokens, and market-neutral fund units into a single mintable stablecoin — 50% in tokenized {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} (BUIDL, USDY, OUSG), 25% in aggregated treasury-backed stablecoins, 15% in tokenized gold, and 10% in institutional fund units from Nomura, Fasanara, and Edge Capital. The pitch is that lending protocols can't individually underwrite hundreds of {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} tokens, so rwaUSDi does the aggregation and due diligence — backed by a Lloyd's insurance policy covering de-pegging risk, which is a genuinely novel backstop for a stablecoin. UAE-domiciled with AFI-audited on-chain reserves, it operates on Ethereum only with KYB-gated institutional minting, making it less a retail product and more a composable RWA building block. The elegant abstraction adds a trust layer between holder and underlying assets, but with 99 peg score and only two depeg events on record, the machinery has functioned as designed.

usdm-mega.title: Funding the Sequencer
usdm-mega.text: MegaETH's USDm uses {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} yield from Ethena's USDtb (90% of backing, on BlackRock BUIDL) to subsidize sequencer fees -- elegant flywheel that spins both ways. MegaETH's USDm flips the L2 business model: instead of extracting sequencer fees from users, it uses reserve yield from Ethena's USDtb (90% of backing, itself holding BlackRock's BUIDL) to subsidize network operations -- the chain literally gets cheaper as more people hold its native stablecoin. A perfect peg score and only two depeg events with DEWS at 2 suggest the product is functioning cleanly, though the absence of any tracked DEX liquidity means exit routes are limited to the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanism. The dependency on Ethena's infrastructure for both reserve management and {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} adds counterparty risk that the underlying {{term:treasury}}Treasury bills{{/term}} don't carry, and the stablecoin's value proposition is inseparable from MegaETH's own traction as an L2. The economics reveal a flywheel where stablecoin adoption subsidizes network costs which drives adoption -- elegant when it works, but the flywheel spins in both directions.

usat-tether.title: Tether Goes Domestic
usat-tether.text: Tether's GENIUS-Act-compliant U.S. dollar issued by Anchorage Digital Bank with Cantor Fitzgerald custody, scaled to $152.7M circulating. Tether's USA-T has scaled to roughly $152.7M circulating per DefiLlama, backed 80% by {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills and 20% cash through Anchorage Digital Bank under an OCC federal charter with Cantor Fitzgerald {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} -- the cleanest regulatory setup Tether has ever assembled, anchored by recurring {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} disclosures. The B report card at 72 with CALM stress at 5 and zero depeg events reflects a product that hasn't had time to accumulate blemishes, though the Ethereum-only deployment and 20 DEX pools with $8.7M TVL suggest distribution is advancing faster than the old summary's liquidity score of 9 implied. The strategic logic is transparent: USA-T is Tether's answer to USDC on US soil, separating the domestic compliance story from USDT's $140B offshore empire, with a 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} promise through Anchorage. Whether American institutions will trust a Tether-branded dollar after a decade of skepticism is the billion-dollar question -- the early growth trajectory suggests at least some of them will.

yzusd-yuzu.title: Yield Vault in Stable Clothing
yzusd-yuzu.text:
A KYC-gated yield aggregator on Plasma minted 1:1 with USDT0, with a junior tranche absorbing first losses and zero secondary market to test the peg.

Yuzu's yzUSD packages curated DeFi yield strategies into an {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} stablecoin — 50% Pendle PT/LP positions, 20% Euler/Morpho lending, 20% other DeFi strategies, and a 10% USDT0 buffer — all classified as exotic collateral on an unproven chain (Plasma). A perfect peg score and zero depeg events sound reassuring until you note the absence of any DEX liquidity and queue-based {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}} scoring just 56 on the backstop, with the yzPP junior tranche absorbing first losses. The strict KYC gating — only accredited, qualified, or institutional investors can mint and redeem — makes yzUSD one of the most access-restricted stablecoins in DeFi, which explains both the zero depeg events (few holders means few sellers) and the non-existent secondary market. It's a yield aggregator that happens to maintain a dollar peg rather than a stablecoin that happens to generate yield — the distinction matters when things go wrong.

nusd-neutrl.title: The Contraction Test
nusd-neutrl.text: Delta-neutral synthetic dollar backed mainly by stablecoins plus hedged OTC positions; weathering a 24% one-month supply contraction without depeg, with whitelisted queue-based redemption and ~8.7% sNUSD yield. Neutrl's NUSD is being stress-tested by something more revealing than a depeg event: a 24% supply contraction in a single month, from $225M to $170M, as holders queue for the exit.
