The {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar backed by 93.5% stablecoins with OTC and hedged {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} positions in a {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} structure has maintained composure through the drawdown -- just 4 depeg events total and a CALM DEWS reading of 10 -- which says more about the mechanism than any bull-market AUM figure could. The B- safety grade at 69 with an 8.7% APY via sNUSD yields a modest 0.25 yield-to-risk ratio, respectable for a product with whitelisted queue-based {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and real-time Accountable {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}. Whether the outflow represents profit-taking or loss of confidence will become clear in the next quarter, but the {{term:funding-rate}}funding-rate{{/term}}-driven infrastructure is handling the drawdown with the quiet competence of a product that was built for exactly this scenario.

usdgo-osl.title: The Quiet Surge
usdgo-osl.text: OSL's USDGO has doubled supply to $134M with a near-perfect peg, backed 80% {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and 20% cash at Anchorage Digital under an OCC charter -- on-chain liquidity is the bottleneck, not credentials. USDGO has more than doubled in supply over the past month to $134 million, a growth rate that makes most stablecoin launches look lethargic, all while maintaining a near-perfect peg with zero depeg events. The safety grade has climbed to B at 71, reflecting 80% {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and 20% cash held at Anchorage Digital under an OCC federal bank charter -- credentials that outclass most competitors five times its size, with institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and same-day {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. Solana-only deployment and a modest $1 million in DEX TVL across just two pools make this an issuer-API exit story rather than an on-chain arbitrage play, but the CALM stress band and same-day settlement suggest OSL's institutional pipeline is doing the heavy lifting. The real question is whether USDGO's trajectory is sustainable demand from the Asia-Pacific trade corridor or a one-time institutional onboarding that plateaus once the initial wave settles.

fidd-fidelity.title: Fidelity's Trillion-Dollar Entrance
fidd-fidelity.text: FIDD is Fidelity Digital Assets' OCC-chartered dollar stablecoin backed by cash and short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} at BNY Mellon — a regulatory beachhead from a $5.8T asset manager. When the third-largest asset manager on earth issues a stablecoin, the signal overwhelms the product — and the product is deliberately boring: 80% T-bills and 20% cash at BNY Mellon, OCC national trust charter, and a B+ safety grade. At $48M circulating, FIDD is a rounding error on Fidelity's $5.8 trillion AUM, which is precisely the point — this is a regulatory beachhead, not a market play. The 65-rated offchain {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop with same-day settlement is institutional-standard but unremarkable. Four DEX pools with primary coverage and a 66 liquidity score suggest Fidelity is building the on-chain plumbing methodically rather than chasing TVL. The question is not whether FIDD can maintain its peg but whether Fidelity decides this experiment deserves real distribution.

aid-gaib.title: GPU Yield, Dollarized
aid-gaib.text: AID is GAIB's centralized dollar stablecoin, minted 1:1 against USDC and USDT and backed by T-bills and approved stables — its companion sAID accrues GPU/AI infrastructure financing yield. GAIB's AID is a conventional dollar stablecoin — {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and stablecoin reserves, 1:1 mint and burn — whose entire reason for existing is its companion token sAID, which accrues yield from GPU and AI infrastructure financing deals. The structure neatly separates stable value (AID) from exotic yield (sAID), letting users choose their risk exposure. At $21 million market cap it's early-stage even by {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} standards, betting that AI compute demand will create a durable yield substrate. Whether GPU financing agreements produce reliable enough cash flows to back a yield product is genuinely untested — but in a market where every new stablecoin needs a narrative, "AI infrastructure yield" is at least more substantive than most.

apxusd-apyx.title: Dividends as Collateral
apxusd-apyx.text: apxUSD is Apyx's dollar stablecoin backed by preferred shares of Digital Asset Treasury companies plus a cash and {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} buffer — an experimental collateral type that bets equity dividends from crypto-holding firms can stay near par. Apyx introduced what might be the most creative collateral backing in stablecoins: preferred shares from Digital Asset Treasury companies — publicly traded equity from firms like Strategy that hold large crypto positions. The theory is that variable-rate preferred shares trade near par regardless of crypto price volatility, providing stable collateral for a dollar token. Launched on Ethereum in February 2026 with DeFi Development Corp as an early investor, apxUSD is so new that market cap data barely exists. The Protocol-Owned Liquidity buffer is meant to absorb stress, but the underlying question is whether equity dividends from crypto-holding companies are truly uncorrelated with the crypto market they depend on. Pharos treats the reserve profile as closer to {{term:rwa}}real-world-asset{{/term}} credit than to a cash-only stablecoin.

jpyc-jpyc.title: The Yen's Licensed Pioneer
jpyc-jpyc.text: Japan's first FSA-approved yen stablecoin, 100% JPY deposit and JGB-backed under a Type II Funds Transfer license; market cap still modest. Japan's first FSA-approved yen stablecoin occupies an enviable regulatory position — Type II Funds Transfer license under the Payment Services Act, 100% backed by JPY deposits and Japanese government bonds, with institutional-regulated custody and zero transaction fees. Deployed on three chains with the JPYC EX platform handling mint/redemption via bank transfer after KYC, the infrastructure is sound but the market cap remains modest — a product that proves regulatory compliance alone doesn't drive adoption. The real threat isn't GYEN (regulated in New York but locked out of Japan's domestic market) but Progmat Coin from Mitsubishi UFJ, Sumitomo Mitsui, and Mizuho — three megabanks whose combined balance sheet makes JPYC look like a rounding error. Being first to market matters less when the second movers have trillion-dollar balance sheets and existing banking relationships with every corporation in Japan. The structural moat is reserves split between bank deposits and JGB {{term:treasury}}treasury bonds{{/term}}, FSA-mandated {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, institutional-regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and bank-rail {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} via JPYC EX.

xaut-tether.title: Tether Mints Bullion
xaut-tether.text:
Tether's Swiss-vaulted LBMA gold token rides USDT's brand and BDO Italia attestations but is steadily losing share to PAXG's bar-level transparency.

Tether's gold token is backed 100% by LBMA Good Delivery bars in Swiss vaults with BDO Italia {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, operating under El Salvador's CNAD jurisdiction with institutional-regulated custody — the same transparency framework as USDT, applied to physical bullion. XAUT commands the largest share of the tokenized gold market, which sounds impressive until you notice that share has been eroding as PAXG and newer competitors chip away at the margins. Deployed on Ethereum only, XAUT works exactly like you'd expect from Tether: a market that trades on brand recognition over the granular bar-level transparency that Paxos offers with PAXG's allocated serial numbers. With gold's rally inflating all boats, XAUT's real significance may be Tether's own physical gold accumulation rather than the tokenized wrapper itself.

paxg-paxos.title: Fort Knox With a Charter
paxg-paxos.text: Only federally regulated gold token, operating under Paxos's OCC national trust charter with KPMG monthly attestations and individually allocated LBMA Good Delivery bars at Brink's London; Ethereum-only deployment by design. The only federally regulated gold token in existence, PAXG operates under Paxos's OCC national trust charter with institutional-top {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, KPMG monthly {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, and individually allocated LBMA Good Delivery bars at Brink's London -- each with a serial number verifiable on the Paxos platform. The permanent second to Tether Gold by market share, PAXG is the first choice for anyone whose compliance department has veto power: allocated bars, bankruptcy-remote trust structure, and the kind of regulatory paper trail that makes institutional allocators comfortable. While XAUT trades on Tether's brand recognition, PAXG trades on verifiable custody -- in a market where gold itself is the product, trust infrastructure is the only real differentiator. Ethereum-only deployment limits DeFi composability but matches the product's institutional focus.

kau-kinesis.title: Gold That Pays Rent
kau-kinesis.text: 1 gram LBMA-gold-backed token with 15% transaction-fee yield sharing and Mastercard spending; Cayman VASP, Bureau Veritas audited. Kinesis cracked the code that other gold tokens missed: people want yield. KAU holders earn a share of 15% of all platform transaction fees, paid monthly in additional gold — backed 1:1 by LBMA-approved physical gold at 1 gram per token in ABX vaults, Bureau Veritas audited, under a Cayman CIMA VASP license. Add a virtual Mastercard for point-of-sale gold spending and you get something genuinely different: gold that functions as money, not just an asset, with institutional-regulated custody and independent attestation that the bars actually exist. The catch is that yield depends entirely on Kinesis's transaction volume — if trading dries up, so does the rent check, and without any tracked on-chain contracts, KAU exists primarily within Kinesis's own platform rather than the broader DeFi ecosystem. A growing challenger to the XAUT-PAXG duopoly, betting that yield and spendability matter more than Ethereum composability. Bureau Veritas {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} verifies the bars exist at the ABX vault {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} that backs physical {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}.

xaum-matrixdock.title: Asia's Institutional Bullion
xaum-matrixdock.text:
LBMA gold vaulted in Singapore and Hong Kong with Bureau Veritas audits — a deliberate Asia-domicile bet against London- and Swiss-vaulted competitors.

Matrixdock's XAUm is backed by LBMA-certified 99.99% gold bars at Brink's and Malca-Amit in Singapore and Hong Kong, Bureau Veritas audited via independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, with institutional-regulated custody and a minimum redemption of 32.148 XAUm (1 kg) restricted to KYC'd accredited investors. The Asia-Pacific custody thesis — Singapore and Hong Kong vaults rather than London or Switzerland — is a deliberate choice targeting institutions that prefer regional domicile for their gold exposure. Deployed on Ethereum and BSC, XAUm remains a modest share of the tokenized gold market, but the partnership with Bhutan's Gelephu Mindfulness City for sovereign gold tokenization signals ambitions beyond retail. Whether institutions actually prefer Asia-domiciled custody over the London and Swiss vaults that XAUT and PAXG offer remains the strategic bet.

cgo-comtech.title: DMCC-Stamped Bullion
cgo-comtech.text: CGO is ComTech's tokenized gold from Dubai vaults at 1 gram per token; impeccable local credentials, negligible global adoption. ComTech Gold's CGO is backed 1:1 by 24-karat 999.9% physical gold at 1 gram per token in Transguard vaults under the Emirates Group umbrella, DMCC endorsed, with individually serialized bars registered on DMCC Tradeflow and institutional-regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} under DAFZA jurisdiction. The {{term:redemption}}redemption-via-app{{/term}} workflow with minimum 10-gram delivery is the most retail-friendly physical gold offramp in the tokenized gold market, leveraging Dubai's regulatory clarity on {{term:rwa}}tokenized commodities{{/term}} that is genuinely ahead of most jurisdictions. Without tracked on-chain contracts, CGO exists primarily within the ComTech ecosystem rather than DeFi, and none of the UAE pedigree has translated into meaningful global adoption. Impeccable local credentials, negligible global presence — proving once again that regulatory clarity alone doesn't create liquidity.

dgld-gold-token-sa.title: Heritage Gold, Rebooted
dgld-gold-token-sa.text: DGLD is Gold Token SA's tokenized PAMP gold from Swiss vaults at 1 ounce per token; pristine heritage, negligible adoption. DGLD is backed 1:1 by allocated LBMA Good Delivery PAMP gold bars — the Swiss refiner whose name is synonymous with premium bullion — at 1 troy ounce per token with real-time reserve verification through on-chain bar serial numbers and VQF/FINMA regulatory oversight. MKS PAMP relaunched DGLD in late 2025 with deployments on Ethereum and Base, institutional-regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and minimum 1-gram {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} — the lowest physical gold redemption threshold of any tokenized gold product. A 60-year refining heritage and the most prestigious gold backing in crypto have produced one of the least adopted gold tokens on the market, proving that heritage is necessary but wildly insufficient for winning the tokenized gold race. The dual-chain deployment signals ambition beyond the institutional market, but DGLD's traction remains a fraction of what PAMP's reputation would suggest. Allocated gold qualifies it as a {{term:rwa}}real-world asset{{/term}} stable.

kag-kinesis.title: The Lonely Ounce
kag-kinesis.text: 1 troy oz silver-backed token with 15% transaction-fee yield sharing; Cayman VASP, Bureau Veritas audited, effectively the only tokenized silver in town. KAG is backed 1:1 by investment-grade physical silver at 1 troy ounce per token, Bureau Veritas audited under a Cayman CIMA VASP license — the same yield-sharing model as its gold sibling KAU, where holders earn a share of 15% of all platform transaction fees paid monthly in additional silver. In a world where tokenized gold has surged past $6 billion, tokenized silver remains a ghost town and KAG is effectively its only resident. Deployed on Ethereum with institutional-regulated custody, the product is structurally identical to KAU but without the macro tailwind: silver's performance has lagged gold's rally dramatically, limiting both demand and yield generation. The thesis is straightforward — if precious metals tokenization is real, silver must eventually follow gold — but 'eventually' is doing a lot of heavy lifting for a product this niche. Independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} from Bureau Veritas plus institutional-regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} support physical {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} of the underlying silver.

eurq-quantoz.title: The Enterprise Euro
eurq-quantoz.text: EURQ is Quantoz's DNB-supervised MiCA euro stablecoin with 102% reserves and direct SEPA integration — built for corporate {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, not DeFi. Quantoz built EURQ for corporate treasurers, not DeFi degens — DNB-regulated under MiCA, 102% reserved in 68% eurozone government bonds and 32% cash at Tier 1 European banks, with direct SEPA integration and institutional-regulated custody. The same Dutch compliance infrastructure as its USDQ sibling, EURQ carves a niche in programmable corporate payments where compliance is a feature, not a tax. The 2% over-collateralization buffer and self-reported {{term:attestation}}transparency{{/term}} are a quiet flex: enough to signal conservatism without dragging capital efficiency, supervised by the same DNB that oversees ING and ABN AMRO. Whether the enterprise market actually wants an on-chain euro or just talks about it at conferences remains the open question, but Quantoz is better positioned than most to find out.

deuro-deuro.title: The Oracle-Free Euro
deuro-deuro.text: DEURO is a decentralized euro stablecoin minted from BTC/ETH/crypto vaults using oracle-free Frankencoin-style auctions; rare genuinely decentralized euro. Born from the same codebase as Frankencoin (ZCHF), dEURO takes the contrarian position that price oracles are a point of failure, not a feature — its {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} model uses internal auctions instead of external price feeds, a design that trades capital efficiency for resilience against oracle manipulation. The collateral is omnivorous: 40% WBTC, 25% WETH, 10% XAUT (tokenized gold), and smaller positions in USDC, DAI, UNI, and ZCHF, all valued through auction-based mechanisms on five chains. With governance fully transferred to token holders and no founder control over contracts, dEURO is genuinely decentralized in a euro stablecoin market where that word usually means 'we have a multisig' — one of only two decentralized euro stablecoins tracked by Pharos. MiCA's evolving stance on decentralized stablecoins could be either tailwind or existential threat, depending on whether European regulators view oracle-free design as innovation or evasion. {{term:overcollateralization}}Overcollateralization{{/term}} and auction-driven {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} stand in for an oracle-fed margin call.

cetes-etherfuse.title: Three Counterparties, One Yield
cetes-etherfuse.text: CETES is Etherfuse's tokenized Mexican T-bill fund accruing in MXN; FX risk on top of sovereign and issuer risk. CETES are Mexico's equivalent of {{term:treasury}}Treasury bills{{/term}} — zero-coupon sovereign debt auctioned weekly by the Ministry of Finance — and Etherfuse has tokenized them into a NAV-accreting instrument backed 100% by CETES with INDEVAL {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, institutional-regulated oversight under CNBV/IPAB/CONDUSEF, and {{term:attestation}}independent attestation{{/term}}. The BBB- sovereign rating is honest about where Mexico sits in the credit hierarchy — legitimate investment grade, but peso volatility means dollar-denominated exposure carries FX risk that doesn't appear in the APY headline. Deployed across four chains (Solana, Base, Polygon, Stellar), CETES tokens offer genuine access to Mexican sovereign debt for holders who can navigate the KYC-gated minting process. The {{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}} is real and Banxico's rate cycle has kept CETES competitive globally — what the token hasn't resolved is which of its three dependencies (the peso, the sovereign, or the issuer) will cause the first inconvenient conversation. Functionally an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} sovereign-debt wrapper.

zarp-zarp.title: The Rand's Digital Outpost
zarp-zarp.text:
Old Mutual Wealth holds 100% ZAR backing with Kempen audits — the only regulated on-chain rand, but relevance is the question, not credibility.

ZARP is backed 100% by ZAR in a treasury managed by Old Mutual Wealth — one of Africa's largest financial institutions — independently audited by Kempen via periodic {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, with institutional-regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and an FSCA CASP license still pending. Deployed across Ethereum, Base, and Polygon, the infrastructure is sound but adoption has plateaued despite genuine demand for stable local-currency rails in a country where the rand regularly loses ground to the dollar. South African crypto regulation remains in perpetual draft mode, and ZARP's problem isn't credibility — it's relevance in a market that hasn't yet decided whether local-currency stablecoins solve a problem or just add complexity to existing USD pairs. For the small audience that needs on-chain ZAR exposure with direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} into ZAR, ZARP is the only regulated option; for everyone else, USDC denominated in dollars remains simpler.

syrupusdc-maple.title: Institutional Lending, Vaulted
syrupusdc-maple.text: one of the largest yield-bearing stablecoins, channeling USDC into overcollateralized institutional loans with independent Proof of Reserves. Maple Finance's syrupUSDC has become one of the largest {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} stablecoins, channeling deposits into {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}-backed institutional loans. The ERC-4626 vault design makes it composable enough that Aave V3, Morpho, and Pendle have all integrated it -- meaning your lending yield can itself be lent, borrowed against, or split into principal and yield tranches. Maple's new Proof of Reserves layer adds {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}-style independent verification by The Network Firm for collateral backing the loan book, improving transparency without eliminating credit, {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, or {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}}-timing risk. The risk is still the one that always haunts institutional credit: borrowers default, and 'overcollateralized' is only as good as the collateral's liquidation value in a downturn.

syrupusdt-maple.title: The Mirror Vault
syrupusdt-maple.text: syrupUSDC's USDT counterpart with identical Maple mechanics and Proof of Reserves, just smaller and Ethereum-only. Maple's USDT counterpart to syrupUSDC runs on identical mechanics -- ERC-4626 vault, institutional borrower pool, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}-backed credit lines -- as the smaller sibling. The distinction matters less than it appears: both feed from the same Maple lending infrastructure as {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} receipts, and Maple's Proof of Reserves now gives the USDT vault the same {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}-style independent loan-collateral verification by The Network Firm, with similar {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} dynamics if borrowers default. Ethereum-only deployment limits its DeFi composability compared to syrupUSDC's multi-chain reach, which may explain the size gap. For yield-seekers who prefer their stablecoin exposure in Tether rather than Circle, syrupUSDT is the vault; the economics are otherwise indistinguishable.

yousd-yield-optimizer.title: Fifty Strategies, One Token
yousd-yield-optimizer.text:
A USDC-only yield aggregator on Base whose NAV climbs above $1 — a sophisticated optimizer wearing stablecoin clothing, built and tested during a bull market.

YO Protocol's yoUSD automates what DeFi power users do manually — rebalancing USDC across 50+ yield sources on Ethereum, Base, Arbitrum, and Unichain, ranked by risk scores with per-pool and per-protocol concentration caps. The track record of positive returns with zero negative months looks miraculous until you remember it was built during a bull market. Backed by Paradigm, Haun Ventures, and Coinbase Ventures, the deposits are modest but growing as the NAV appreciation model means your 'dollar' climbs steadily above $1 — stable in the sense that it never goes down, not that it stays at one. The real tension is philosophical: yoUSD is a sophisticated {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} aggregator wearing a stablecoin's clothing, and the distinction matters when the bull market ends.

ustb-superstate.title: Wall Street's On-Chain Fund
ustb-superstate.text: Superstate's USTB sits at $810M in 100% short-duration government securities at BNY Mellon, sub-advised by Federated Hermes — a Reg D {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} that other stablecoins use as collateral rather than retail holds. Superstate's USTB sits at $810 million in 100% short-duration government securities at BNY Mellon, sub-advised by Federated Hermes, audited by Ernst & Young — a pedigree that reads like a traditional fund prospectus because it essentially is one. The B+ safety grade at 75 with A+ in resilience and dependency risk makes it one of the highest-rated {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} tokens on Pharos, though the SEC Reg D restriction to qualified purchasers and accredited investors means the audience is narrow by design. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills and {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} sit underneath, with institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at BNY Mellon as the anchor. Zero DEX liquidity and zero pool count confirm that USTB doesn't trade on decentralized markets at all; this is a subscribe-and-redeem product at daily NAV, now at $11.05 per share yielding 3.20%. The real significance remains infrastructural: USTB appears in the collateral stacks of other stablecoins that want {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} exposure without the BNY Mellon relationship, making Superstate less a consumer product than the institutional plumbing beneath DeFi's yield layer.

ousg-ondo-finance.title: The Hundred-Dollar Stablecoin
ousg-ondo-finance.text: Ondo's tokenized U.S. T-Bill fund (mostly BlackRock BUIDL plus FedFund and a USDC buffer); NAV-accreting at >$114 per token, KYC-restricted to U.S. Qualified Purchasers, with instant T+0 mint and redeem via USDC. OUSG has grown past $700 million -- 85% backed by BlackRock's BUIDL with 12% in BlackRock's FedFund and a 3% USDC liquidity buffer, making Ondo I LP BlackRock's largest single on-chain client and OUSG essentially a first-class derivative of BlackRock's tokenized {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} presence. At over $114 per token with NAV appreciating daily, it is the least dollar-like entry on any stablecoin dashboard, which is why Ondo maintains rOUSG -- a rebasing sibling that stays at $1 while OUSG accumulates. The SEC investigation closure in November 2025 without charges removed the key regulatory overhang, and the instant T+0 mint/{{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} via OUSGInstantManager against USDC through BUIDL on-chain liquidity makes OUSG's exit infrastructure better than most tokenized funds. Restricted to U.S. Qualified Purchasers with on-chain KYC enforcement -- tokens literally cannot transfer to non-whitelisted addresses -- OUSG is less a stablecoin and more a tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} that borrowed the infrastructure.

mtbill-midas.title: Europe's T-Bill Token
mtbill-midas.text: Compliance-first European tokenized U.S. T-bill product (BlackRock IB01 ETF, Swiss custody, FMA-approved MiFID II), restricted to non-U.S./UK retail; daily Ankura NAV attestations. mTBILL is Midas's compliance-first answer to the tokenized {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} race: 97% in BlackRock's IB01 ETF with Swiss {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at Maerki Baumann, issued as a Liechtenstein FMA-approved MiFID II instrument -- the exact bureaucratic architecture required to legally sell T-bill exposure to European professionals. Ankura Trust provides daily on-chain NAV {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, and the {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} collateral quality with regulated-entity governance earns institutional credibility that most crypto-native tokenized treasury products lack. The 'not available to U.S. or UK retail persons' restriction is the mirror image of USTB and OUSG's American access gates, carving out a European institutional niche in a market dominated by U.S. issuers. Deployed across five chains, mTBILL functions as infrastructure in Midas's product stack and as stable collateral in third-party structured products -- the European {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market-fund-like{{/term}} token for protocols that need regulatory certainty over DeFi composability.

wsrusd-reservoir.title: Ashes to APY
wsrusd-reservoir.text:
Reservoir's ERC-4626 NAV vault survived a $285M bank run, then reincarnated as a seven-stablecoin reserve managed by named curators with enforced solvency floors.

Reservoir's rUSD processed $285M in redemptions 'without failure' in November 2025, then flatlined — the protocol's precise way of surviving a bank run while losing the patient. The reincarnation as wsrUSD is an ERC-4626 NAV vault backed by an unusually varied diet: 30% USDC, 25% USDT, 10% PYUSD, 5% GHO, 5% RLUSD, 5% USD1, plus strategy vaults and lending markets — seven upstream stablecoin dependencies curated by Steakhouse, Gauntlet, and other named managers. Credit Enforcer smart contracts enforce minimum 105% liquidity, solvency, and capital ratios before any leverage-increasing action, which is the kind of on-chain risk management that most {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} protocols skip. Deployed across 15 chains with exotic collateral quality and multisig governance, wsrUSD's flexibility is genuine — but the seven-dependency architecture means the protocol's safety is a derivative of Circle, Tether, PayPal, Aave, Ripple, and World Liberty Financial simultaneously.

dusd-alto.title: The Isolated Vault Stablecoin
dusd-alto.text: DUSD is Alto's CDP-style stablecoin minted from isolated markets backed by ETH, BTC, and yield-bearing variants; tiny supply backstopped by a USDC PSM. Alto DUSD takes a kitchen-sink approach to collateral in isolated markets — 55% ETH and LSTs, 20% BTC tokens, 15% sUSDe, 5% Syrup USDC, and a 5M USDC {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} cap at 20 bps — so one bad collateral doesn't cascade into the rest. The 91-rated PSM backstop with permissionless atomic settlement is the structural highlight, and the perfect peg score with zero depeg events on $527K in circulation suggests the architecture works at micro-cap scale. DAO governance via ALTO token holders earns the decentralized classification, though the DEWS Watch band at 29 with 85% worst-pool stress signals that the on-chain market is thinner than the collateral diversity implies. The embedded Ethena dependency via sUSDe means DUSD inherits a slice of {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} basis risk on top of its {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} buffer — sophisticated risk engineering at a scale too small to stress-test. Isolated minting markets behave like ring-fenced {{term:cdp}}CDPs{{/term}}.

dusd-dtrinity.title: Post-Exploit Purgatory
dusd-dtrinity.text: dUSD is dTRINITY's reserve-backed dollar with Curve AMOs; post-exploit trust rebuild on a Frax-heavy reserve. The March 17 exploit hit dTRINITY at the worst possible moment — a protocol with genuinely novel economics (subsidized borrowing funded by reserve {{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}}) now carries a danger notice that overshadows everything else on the page. Supply has contracted to roughly $1.5M from $1.8M a month prior, Sonic deployment is paused, and the C grade at 57 reflects a protocol where the safety floor has cracked. The reserve composition tells the dependency story: 42% sfrxUSD and 35% Curve {{term:amo}}AMO{{/term}} positions mean dUSD is overwhelmingly a bet on Frax infrastructure, with chain-isolated reserves that at least prevent cross-chain contagion. DEWS has eased from Alert to Watch at 20, suggesting the acute crisis is stabilizing, but the 84-rated backstop with 40% immediate capacity is doing the heavy lifting to keep this from unwinding further. An elegant flywheel that proved fragile under pressure — the borrower subsidy model deserves a second chance, but this protocol needs to earn it. The 84-rated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop is currently doing most of the peg-defense work.

thbill-theo.title: Wrapping the Wrappers
thbill-theo.text: a three-entity, two-wrapper path from token to bond, backed by Standard Chartered Libeara's ULTRA fund managed by Wellington. Theo's thBILL is 100% backed by tULTRA, which wraps Standard Chartered Libeara's ULTRA fund, which holds actual U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills as a tokenized {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} managed by Wellington Management -- three entities and two wrappers between your token and a government bond. The Panama-incorporated structure with single-entity governance and no published proof of reserves contrasts sharply with the Ankura-{{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}-backed mTBILL and E&Y-audited USTB it competes against, though Standard Chartered's {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and Wellington's management provide institutional ballast at the bottom of the stack. The {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} collateral quality and institutional-regulated custody classification acknowledge what's actually holding the assets, even if the wrapper depth adds layers of operational risk that the T-bill label might obscure. Deployed across four chains with KYC-gated minting and T+4 settlement on underlying collateral, thBILL has found its niche among institutional investors who want T-bill exposure without caring too much about how many wrappers sit between them and the bonds.

usdp-parallel.title: Fee Yield, No Tricks
usdp-parallel.text: Parallel's USDp is backed 50/50 by sfrxUSD and sUSDe with a Parallelizer fee-adjustment peg mechanism; sUSDp yield is real protocol fees, not made-up rates. Parallel's USDp is backed 50% by sfrxUSD and 50% by sUSDe -- two yield-bearing stablecoins whose Parallelizer module adjusts minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fees dynamically to correct peg drift without oracles or {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} cascades. The yield story is unusually honest: sUSDp distributes 70% of actual protocol fees from the Parallelizer, bridging, and flash loan modules, meaning yield tracks real usage rather than governance votes on a made-up rate. DAO governance across five chains with Bailsec audit and Certora formal verification suggest Mimo Labs built this for durability rather than speed, though the dependency on both Frax (sfrxUSD) and Ethena (sUSDe) means USDp inherits the risk profiles of two very different stablecoin architectures -- one backed by BlackRock {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, the other by {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} {{term:basis-trade}}basis trades{{/term}}. The central tension is whether a fee-revenue yield model can remain attractive at small scale when it competes against synthetic dollar protocols running leveraged strategies at hundred-fold the size.

usdpt-western-union.title: May Launch, SWIFT Killshot
usdpt-western-union.text: Western Union's USDPT launches in May 2026 with Anchorage Digital issuance and U.S. Bank {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}; the actual product is a SWIFT alternative for interbank settlement, not retail. On the Q1 2026 earnings call (Apr 24), CEO Devin McGranahan confirmed what the seven-month buildout had been telegraphing: USDPT launches in May, and the first product is not a consumer wallet -- it's an alternative to SWIFT for Western Union's own interbank settlement. The Digital Asset Network went live four days later with its first partner, with seven more activations queued before year-end and a USD Stable Card targeting inflationary markets later in 2026. The plumbing is unchanged from October -- Anchorage Digital Bank issues, U.S. Bank custodies the reserves, the token lives on Solana -- but the framing has tightened: this is float-revenue capture and back-office disintermediation first, retail second. Western Union still has 360,000 payout locations across 200+ countries, which is the actual distribution moat that no DeFi-native stablecoin can replicate. The CoinGecko preview listing remains zero-supply pending mainnet, which is the last technical signal worth watching before promotion. McGranahan's quote -- 'It is no longer a question of if Western Union will be active in digital assets; it is now how fast we can scale' -- reads like a business-school case study line, but in this case the launch date now matches, with on-chain {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and reserve {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} still to be confirmed at mainnet.

roughrider-bnd.title: State-Owned Banking Goes On-Chain
roughrider-bnd.text:
North Dakota's state-owned bank cleared its biggest hurdle on March 25 for a Solana-based bank-to-bank settlement coin, targeting September 2026.

North Dakota's Bank of North Dakota — the only state-owned bank in the US — cleared its biggest hurdle on March 25 when the Industrial Commission unanimously approved the bank-to-bank use case for Roughrider Coin. Ten local banks have already expressed pilot interest, CEO Don Morgan rates the risk as 'low to moderate,' and the project is expected to be cost-neutral to the state. The coin runs on Solana via Fiserv's infrastructure, backed by USD reserves and 93-day {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} notes under the GENIUS Act's state-issued stablecoin exemption. It won't be publicly tradeable — this is pure interbank settlement plumbing, voluntary for ND banks and credit unions. September 2026 remains the target, pending Fiserv contract finalization. As the second US state stablecoin after Wyoming's FRNT, Roughrider represents an emerging pattern: state treasurers discovering that blockchain settlement is cheaper than correspondent banking, even when the vote requires a closed-door executive session lasting two and a half hours.

fiusd-fiserv.title: The Payments Stack Play
fiusd-fiserv.text: FIUSD is Fiserv's pre-launch Solana dollar stablecoin built on Circle and Paxos infrastructure — a payments-rails play with four-partner coordination risk. Fiserv processes $2 trillion in payments annually for 6,000+ financial institutions and wants to make stablecoins just another rail in that plumbing. FIUSD is less a single stablecoin and more a platform: Paxos handles issuance, Circle provides ecosystem interop, PayPal enables interoperability, and Mastercard connects the payments network. The centralized-dependent classification captures this architecture accurately — FIUSD depends on an entire constellation of {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} partners, any of which could become a {{term:bridge}}bottleneck{{/term}}. The end-of-2025 launch target has quietly slipped into 2026 with no firm date, which either means careful regulatory preparation or the inherent difficulty of coordinating four major fintech companies on a shared timeline.

eur-qivalis.title: Twelve Banks, One Euro
eur-qivalis.text: QEUR is a pre-launch MiCA-oriented euro stablecoin from a 17-bank consortium; targeting H2 2026 under a Dutch EMI license. Qivalis is the European banking establishment's answer to USDC and Tether: a MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin backed by a consortium of 12 major banks including BNP Paribas, ING, UniCredit, and BBVA. The reserve design — 30-40% bank deposits, the remainder in short-term eurozone government bonds — reads like a {{term:money-market-fund}}money market fund{{/term}} with a blockchain address. The blockchain question is now settled: Ethereum mainnet first (ERC-20), then Polygon and Base, all with a permissioned KYC layer — only pre-verified participants can hold or transfer the token, which is the banking consortium's compromise between public chain liquidity and institutional control. CEO Jan-Oliver Sell (ex-Coinbase Germany) is finalizing exchange partnerships, with Bit2Me named as one platform in discussions. The EMI license application has been filed with De Nederlandsche Bank but not yet granted. The central tension remains whether twelve banks that compete fiercely in every other market can cooperate long enough to ship before Circle's EURC and SocGen's EURCV eat the entire MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin market. {{term:custody}}Custody{{/term}} sits across consortium banks and 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rights remain pre-launch commitments.

pusd-polaris.title: Immutable CDP, Yield Included
pusd-polaris.text:
A pre-launch Liquity-style immutable CDP stablecoin on Ethereum that captures protocol revenue for holders rather than reserve interest.

Polaris Finance is building what its co-founders TokenBrice and 0xLuude call the successor to Liquity's ethos: a crypto-collateralized stablecoin on Ethereum with immutable core contracts, no admin keys, and no off-chain assets. pUSD is minted against pETH collateral via {{term:cdp}}CDPs{{/term}}, and the {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} angle comes from protocol revenue — borrowing interest, swap fees, conversion gains, and DEX fees — rather than from depositing reserves into Aave. The private testnet is live with a Q4 2026 target, which gives the team time to prove that you can ship immutability without sacrificing usability. For a market saturated with centralized fiat-backed tokens and yield products built on leverage, pUSD is a deliberate bet that there's still demand for the Liquity V1 philosophy, upgraded.

pgold-polaris.title: Synthetic Gold, No Vault Required
pgold-polaris.text:
A pre-launch synthetic gold exposure minted from pETH via CDPs, with no physical backing — decentralized to a fault.

Polaris Gold shares infrastructure with its sibling pUSD but pegs to gold rather than the dollar — and critically, does so without any physical gold backing. Unlike XAUT or PAXG, which tokenize actual bars in Swiss vaults, pGOLD is a synthetic gold exposure minted from the same pETH collateral pool via {{term:cdp}}CDPs{{/term}} on Ethereum. This makes it arguably more decentralized than any gold-pegged token on the market, at the cost of carrying all the risks of crypto collateral in a down market. Whether DeFi users want synthetic gold exposure from immutable contracts instead of custodied metal from Tether or Paxos is an experiment Polaris is willing to run.

usg-tangent.title: Productive Collateral, Dynamic Rates
usg-tangent.text: Tangent's USG is a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin for productive DeFi collateral (Curve LP, Pendle PTs) that explicitly skips {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} in favor of Peg Keepers and dynamic interest rates to push borrowers toward repayment. Tangent Finance — which pivoted from the Convergence protocol after an August 2024 exploit — has deployed USG as an {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin for productive DeFi collateral: Curve LP tokens, Pendle PTs, and other {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} or LP positions rather than plain ETH collateral. The peg mechanism borrows from crvUSD's playbook but explicitly skips redemptions: Peg Keepers, dynamic interest rates, and reward deductions become more aggressive when USG weakens, pushing borrowers toward repayment while directing revenue back to liquidity and sUSG. USG itself is not the {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} token; sUSG is the Yearn v3 savings wrapper that receives 25% of protocol revenue. Tangent now lists five audit reports — Sherlock, Egis, two Pashov reviews, and Zerocool — and Etherscan shows the Ethereum USG contract live with 40.02 million tokens outstanding, though the public site still exposes placeholder APY/TVL metrics and no CoinGecko or DefiLlama market row. The design bets that DeFi-native collateral can be more capital-efficient than traditional {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} models, while inheriting the composability risk of every protocol whose tokens it accepts and a {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} surface that depends on each underlying market's liquidity.

klarnausd-klarna.title: Buy Now, Settle On-Chain Later
klarnausd-klarna.text: Klarna's planned USD stablecoin on Tempo via Stripe Bridge Open Issuance; testnet only, mainnet TBD. Klarna — the Swedish fintech with 114 million customers and $112B in annual GMV — is building a stablecoin via Stripe's Bridge infrastructure on the Tempo L1. Tempo mainnet went live on March 18 with sub-second finality, fees under $0.001, and a Machine Payments Protocol co-authored with Stripe for autonomous AI agent payments — yet KlarnaUSD was conspicuously absent from the mainnet launch partners list (which included Anthropic, Mastercard, Visa, and Revolut). Bridge's conditional OCC national bank trust charter, approved in February, strengthens the regulatory foundation for KlarnaUSD issuance. The coin remains on Tempo's testnet for now, making it a matter of 'when' rather than 'if.' The interesting dynamic hasn't changed: Klarna doesn't need external adoption for KlarnaUSD to succeed — its own payment volume is large enough to justify the infrastructure, making DeFi liquidity a bonus rather than a requirement. Bridge's OCC trust charter brings regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and an {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} framework, with a {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} window scoped for Klarna's settlement flows rather than open DeFi liquidity.

trusd-tori.title: Ethena's Mirror, Three Days Old
trusd-tori.text: Tori Finance's soft-launched synthetic dollar copying Ethena's delta-neutral playbook, with TBA contracts and a controlled beta marketed as launch. Tori Finance soft-launched trUSD on Ethereum on March 24 with the same playbook Ethena popularized: a synthetic dollar backed by {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} trading positions ({{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} arbitrage, calendar spreads, hedged money markets) capturing {{term:funding-rate}}funding rate{{/term}} on {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} hedges, with a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} staked wrapper (strUSD, ~15% APY advertised). Delphi Ventures led the seed round alongside QInvest, CMCC Global, and Bering Waters. Accountable provides real-time proof of reserves via its DVN as an {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} layer, and two audits are complete (Sherlock Jan 2026, Nethermind Mar 2026). The bull case writes itself -- institutional yield strategies democratized at $1 minimums. The bear case is equally obvious: contract addresses are still listed as 'TBA' in the docs, the app endpoint refused connections during our research, TVL shows N/A on their own site, and the Nethermind audit was completed the same day as the 'launch.' Not on DefiLlama, not on CoinGecko, 17 total tweets. This is a controlled beta marketed as a mainnet launch, and the 0.1% mint/redeem fee plus 10% performance fee structure means Tori needs meaningful AUM before the economics work. Watch for contract publication and aggregator listings before treating this as anything more than a proof of concept.

ussd-sonic-labs.title: Yield Without the Yield
ussd-sonic-labs.text: Sonic Labs's USSD is a permissionless, zero-fee stablecoin backed entirely by tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills, where yield flows to the Sonic ecosystem as buybacks rather than to holders. USSD is Sonic Labs' answer to why a fast EVM chain should depend on Circle and Tether to denominate everything — a permissionless, zero-fee stablecoin backed entirely by tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills (BlackRock BUIDL, Superstate USTB, WisdomTree WTGXX) and built on Frax's frxUSD smart contract infrastructure. The design choice that distinguishes it from every other T-bill-backed stablecoin is also its most pointed: the {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} yield flows to the Sonic ecosystem as buybacks and incentives, not to USSD holders, meaning every dollar sitting in USSD generates a return that benefits the protocol's treasury while the holder earns exactly $1. At roughly $2M in circulation at launch, this subsidy is trivial; at meaningful scale, it becomes a permanent off-balance-sheet revenue stream funded by users who chose the zero-yield option. The GENIUS Act-compatible framing and U.S. jurisdiction signal suggest Sonic Labs is building for a regulatory environment that hasn't fully arrived yet, which will look prescient or premature depending entirely on how fast Washington moves.

pgold-pleasing.title: Gold Without Receipts
pgold-pleasing.text:
Pleasing's gold token claims 1:1 physical bullion backing but publishes no proof of reserves or independent attestation, making it the least transparent gold token on the dashboard.

Pleasing Gold's PGOLD is backed 1:1 by LBMA-standard 99.99% physical gold at 1 troy ounce per token, deployed on Arbitrum and ApeChain — the same Pleasing International that issues PUSD, sharing infrastructure and the Hong Kong precious metals firm's physical gold corridor. The institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and absence of any proof of reserves or independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} make PGOLD the least transparent gold token on the dashboard, relying entirely on the issuer's claims without external verification. Whether a gold token without audited reserves can compete with PAXG's KPMG attestations and XAUT's BDO Italia audits depends on the holder's trust in the issuer rather than the metal itself. For Pleasing's existing gold corridor clients, PGOLD may serve as a convenient tokenized bridge; for everyone else, the lack of verifiable custody is a hard pass.

ggbr-goldfish-gold.title: The Paper Gold Token
ggbr-goldfish-gold.text: GGBR is Goldfish Gold's gold-tracking token at 1/1000 troy ounce per token, backed by issuer balance-sheet exposure rather than allocated bars — counterparty risk, not custody risk. Goldfish Gold's GGBR represents 1/1000 of a troy ounce of gold per token, but unlike XAUT or PAXG, the backing is described as 'issuer balance-sheet gold exposure' rather than allocated physical bars — making it more a gold-tracking derivative than a tokenized commodity. The institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} with no published proof of reserves, no independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, and no disclosed jurisdiction means the entire trust chain runs through the Goldfish entity alone. Ethereum-only deployment with high-risk reserve classification reflects the Pharos assessment of what 'issuer-managed backing' means in practice: counterparty risk on the issuer rather than custody risk on the metal. In a tokenized gold market where PAXG offers individually serialized LBMA bars with KPMG attestations, GGBR's value proposition is hard to articulate beyond convenience.

axcnh-anchorx.title: The Offshore Yuan
axcnh-anchorx.text: AxCNH is AnchorX's centralized offshore-yuan stablecoin, redeemable 1:1 for CNH and backed by CNH cash reserves at regulated financial institutions — issued under a Kazakhstan AFSA license rather than Hong Kong or Singapore. AnchorX's AxCNH is a CNH-pegged stablecoin backed 100% by offshore Chinese yuan cash reserves at regulated financial institutions, issued under a Kazakhstan AFSA license — a jurisdiction that provides formal regulatory cover without the scrutiny of Hong Kong or Singapore. The institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} classification and absence of proof of reserves or independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} mean the trust assumptions sit entirely with the AnchorX entity and its reported reserve figures. Deployed on two chains, AxCNH occupies an unusual niche: on-chain access to CNH exposure for a currency whose on-shore variant (CNY) is heavily capital-controlled by the People's Bank of China. Whether the offshore yuan stablecoin market is large enough to sustain a product without established exchange partnerships or DeFi integrations remains the open question.

idrt-rupiah-token.title: Indonesia's Digital Rupiah
idrt-rupiah-token.text: 100% IDR-deposit-backed rupiah stablecoin across four chains; no published proof of reserves, gray-area regulation. Rupiah Token's IDRT is backed 100% by Indonesian rupiah bank deposits held by PT Rupiah Token Indonesia, deployed natively across four chains — making it one of the more broadly distributed local-currency stablecoins despite operating with institutional-unregulated custody and no published proof of reserves. Indonesia's crypto market is among the largest in Southeast Asia, giving IDRT a genuine addressable market for IDR-denominated on-chain transactions and remittances, though the absence of specific regulatory licensing and independent reserve attestation limits the product to users who trust the issuer directly. The domestic regulatory landscape for stablecoins in Indonesia remains in development, meaning IDRT operates in a gray area where compliance is self-defined rather than externally enforced. For a country with genuine demand for affordable digital payment rails, IDRT's existence is more practical than innovative. The trust gap is concrete: no third-party {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, opaque {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and a {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path that depends entirely on PT Rupiah Token honoring direct fiat exits.

tryb-bilira.title: The Lira's Digital Outpost
tryb-bilira.text: a Turkish-lira stablecoin backed 100% by TRY cash at the issuer, deployed natively across seven chains for breadth over depth. BiLira's TRYB is a Turkish lira stablecoin backed 100% by TRY cash reserves, deployed natively across seven chains -- the broadest distribution of any local-currency stablecoin in the Middle East and North Africa region. The institutional-unregulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and absence of proof of reserves or specific regulatory licensing reflect the current state of Turkish crypto regulation, where stablecoin issuance operates without a formal licensing framework. Turkey's double-digit inflation and persistent lira weakness create genuine demand for digital TRY rails -- the same macro dynamics that make PikuDAO's USP profitable as a carry trade make TRYB useful as an on-ramp for Turkish crypto traders who need local-currency denomination, with {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} relying on BiLira's issuer rail. Seven-chain deployment suggests BiLira is building for breadth rather than depth, covering the chains where Turkish users actually trade.

ebusd-ebisu.title: Gold and Shorts on Plasma
ebusd-ebisu.text: ebUSD is Ebisu's Liquity-v2-style CDP stablecoin; eclectic collateral basket (synthetic dollars, BTC, tokenized gold, LSTs) at micro-cap scale. Ebisu's ebUSD is a Liquity V2-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with one of the most eclectic collateral baskets on the dashboard: 44% sUSDe (Ethena's {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} token), 24% WBTC, 24% XAUt0 (Tether Gold on Plasma), 6% stcUSD, and 3% weETH — mixing synthetic dollars, wrapped Bitcoin, tokenized gold, and ETH LSTs into a single {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} position. At barely $260K in market cap with 169 depeg events and persistent below-peg trading, ebUSD is too small to attract meaningful arbitrage, and the 78-rated collateral redemption backstop provides a structural floor that the thin secondary market can't close efficiently. Deployed natively on both Ethereum and Plasma with user-set interest rates, the Liquity V2 architecture is sound but the alt-LST-bridged collateral quality classification and DEWS Watch band at 35 reflect the risk profile of accepting tokenized gold and {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} derivatives as CDP backing. ebUSD is a micro-cap experiment in exotic collateral CDP design — interesting architecture on a scale too small to stress-test.

usdaf-asymmetry.title: Decentralization's Price Tag
usdaf-asymmetry.text: an immutable Liquity V2 CDP minted from yield-bearing stablecoin and BTC collateral, structurally pure but $1.04M small and trading at $0.986. USDaf achieves what almost no stablecoin can claim: immutable contracts and a perfect governance score, built on Liquity V2 as a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with collateral drawn from the {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} stablecoin canon -- 65% ysyBOLD, 23% scrvUSD, 7% sUSDS, and scraps of tBTC, sfrxUSD, and WBTC -- relying on conservative {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}. The B- safety grade at 66 is a significant upgrade from the C it held last month, though the price of recursive decentralization remains steep: $1.04M in circulation (down 33% from last month), 103 depeg events, and a current price of $0.986 that suggests the Liquity V2 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} floor around $0.995 isn't always reached in practice. The 82-rated permissionless collateral-redemption backstop is structurally sound and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} mechanics inherit Liquity's battle-tested design, and six DEX pools provide more coverage than a million-dollar stablecoin typically deserves. USDaf is the purest expression of trustless stablecoin design currently live -- and also a reminder that the market values liquidity over ideology.

usnd-nerite.title: Immutable Code, Invisible Scale
usnd-nerite.text: Nerite's USND was a Liquity-V2 fork {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} on Arbitrum that earned an A safety grade on $1.3M circulating before being frozen when an rsETH hack impaired an approved collateral branch. Nerite's USND earned an A safety grade at 83 on $1.3 million in circulation — the highest safety score at that market cap — built on immutable Liquity V2 contracts on Arbitrum with permissionless collateral {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. The collateral was 86.5% tBTC with rETH and WETH rounding out the reserve, giving it A+ marks in both decentralization and dependency risk that most nine-figure stablecoins couldn't match. But the DEWS Watch band at 19, 172 depeg events, and a worst deviation of 1,016 basis points positive revealed the cost of being small: the peg wobbled because nobody sat on the other side of the trade. DEX liquidity was $14K across three fallback-class pools, meaning the backstop's 82-rated permissionless collateral {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} with {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} mechanics were the only real exits before the freeze. USND was the answer to a question very few people were asking — whether you can build a truly decentralized, immutable stablecoin that scored well on every metric except the one that requires other people to care.

ftusd-flying-tulip.title: Cronje's Carry Trade
ftusd-flying-tulip.text: ftUSD is Flying Tulip's USDC/USDT-collateralized dollar with staking carry from borrowed native assets — a domesticated {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} pitch with $225M raised and $730K used. Andre Cronje's Flying Tulip raised $225 million to build a DeFi super-app, and the stablecoin at its center has attracted roughly $730K in circulation from 20 holders — a ratio of venture capital to actual usage that would make a Web2 startup blush. The delta-neutral pitch echoes Ethena's playbook but runs a domesticated version: USDC and USDT lent into Aave with borrowed native assets staked to generate carry, no CEX perpetuals in sight. {{term:yield-bearing}}Yield{{/term}} flows exclusively to sftUSD stakers while unstaked ftUSD proceeds feed the protocol {{term:treasury}}treasury{{/term}}, a design that makes the base token a zero-yield stablecoin whose holders subsidize the protocol by default. Deployed on Ethereum and Sonic with single-entity governance, circuit breaker contracts, and full dependency on the two largest centralized stablecoins, ftUSD is less a standalone dollar and more an opt-in yield wrapper for USDC and USDT with extra steps.

brla-brla-digital.title: Brazil's Dollar Problem, Inverted
brla-brla-digital.text: BRLA is Avenia's centralized Brazilian real stablecoin, mint/redeemed 1:1 for BRL and backed by Brazilian government bonds and BRL cash in regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} — inverting the usual emerging-market dollar-escape pattern. Most stablecoins let emerging-market users escape their local currency into dollars. BRLA does the opposite: it tokenizes the Brazilian Real for on-chain use, backed by government bonds (titulos publicos) and BRL cash held by Avenia (formerly BRLA Digital), a Sao Paulo startup with $17M in Series A funding. Deployed natively on Polygon, Gnosis, Celo, and Moonbeam with no Ethereum presence, BRLA's chain footprint is unusual — Celo dominates with 76% of the ~$14.7M supply. The contract is upgradeable with full blacklisting via a COMPLIANCE_ROLE, governed by a single entity with no multisig or DAO, and proof-of-reserves {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} are self-reported on a Notion page. Yield variants (stBRLA, yBRLA) exist as separate tokens, positioning BRLA as infrastructure for BRL-denominated DeFi rather than just a remittance rail — though at sub-$15M market cap, the infrastructure is still looking for its builders.

silk-shade-protocol.title: The GDP-Weighted Privacy Dollar
silk-shade-protocol.text:
A GDP-weighted basket of 20 currencies on Secret Network, defended by overcollateralized CDPs — conceptually ambitious, but hard to acquire at ~$1.1M circulating.

SILK is what happens when you cross a stablecoin with a macro index fund and deploy it on a privacy chain. Pegged to a GDP-weighted basket of 20 global currencies — USD at 30%, CNY at 22%, EUR bloc at 14%, plus JPY, GBP, INR, and fourteen others — SILK doesn't track any single fiat currency, making it one of the most conceptually ambitious stablecoins tracked on Pharos. Built entirely on Secret Network using the SNIP-20 privacy token standard, every transaction is private by default with optional auditability via viewing keys. The stability architecture layers {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} lending (ShadeLend) via {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} vaults, stablecoin {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} pools, bounded minting with DAO governance, and ShadeDAO bonds — a belt-and-suspenders approach deployed on a chain that most DeFi users have never touched. At ~$1.1M in circulation on a single unproven chain with no {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} to Ethereum, SILK is simultaneously the most interesting basket stablecoin in crypto and one of the hardest to actually acquire.

idrx-idrx.title: Eighteen Billion Tokens, One Dollar
idrx-idrx.text: Eight-chain IDR fiat stablecoin backed by IDR deposits and Indonesian government bonds; KYC-gated, supply quietly bleeding down. IDRX is PT IDRX Indo Inovasi's fiat-backed Indonesian rupiah stablecoin, deployed natively across eight chains with built-in bridge functions and CertiK-audited contracts -- architecturally more ambitious than its rival IDRT, even if the market doesn't seem to care yet. At roughly $1.1M in circulating supply denominated in a currency where each token is worth $0.000058, the token count runs into the billions while the economic value barely registers. The B- safety grade at 65 is surprisingly strong for a token with no published proof of reserves, no named custodian, and explicit blacklisting capabilities baked into the contract. DEWS sits at a calm 9 across $252K in DEX liquidity spread thinly over nine pools, which is technically diversified but practically illiquid. Supply has been quietly trickling down month-over-month, suggesting organic contraction rather than growth -- the Indonesian crypto market may ultimately decide it needs zero rupiah stablecoins rather than two. Reserves combine IDR deposits and Indonesian {{term:treasury}}government bonds{{/term}}, but the trust profile is still weighed down by missing {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, undisclosed {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and KYC-gated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} via the native {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} functions.

mxnb-juno.title: Peso Stablecoin, New Issuer Jurisdiction
mxnb-juno.text: 1:1 MXN-pegged stablecoin with quarterly attestations; issuer just moved from Mexico (CNBV) to El Salvador (CNAD) as of April 2026, with reserves still in regulated peso banking. MXNB remains a 1:1 Mexican peso stablecoin with quarterly reserve {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} and the same multichain FiatToken-style deployment across Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, and Avalanche. The material change is issuer jurisdiction: beginning April 8, 2026, MXNB says issuance moved to Nvio Pagos El Salvador, S.A. de C.V., an authorised digital-asset issuer in El Salvador. The reserves are still described as Mexican peso assets held with regulated financial institutions under bank {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, so Pharos keeps the fiat-backed model while updating the regulatory owner from Mexico/CNBV to El Salvador/CNAD.

cjpy-yamato.title: ETH-Backed Yen, Quietly Running
cjpy-yamato.text: CJPY is Yamato's decentralized JPY stablecoin from ETH-only CDPs; minimal governance, almost no users, by design. Yamato Protocol's CJPY is a JPY-pegged stablecoin built on a clean, ETH-only {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} model by DeFiGeek Community Japan — a DAO with no corporate entity behind it. The mechanism echoes Liquity's playbook: deposit ETH at 130% minimum collateralization, borrow CJPY with a one-time fee and no accruing interest, and face {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} via a subrogation system that uses accumulated protocol fees to automatically repay underwater positions. The {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} floor — 1 CJPY always redeemable for 1 JPY worth of ETH from the riskiest pledge — provides a hard price floor without forced liquidation penalties. Deployed only on Ethereum with ~$1M in circulation, CJPY occupies the same philosophical space as RAI and LUSD: minimal governance, pure crypto collateral, no blacklisting, no upgradeability theater. The YMT governance token with veYMT vote-escrowed mechanics is planned but the protocol currently runs with DAO oversight via Snapshot. In a market where JPY stablecoins are dominated by centralized issuers like JPYC and GYEN, CJPY is the decentralized alternative that almost nobody uses — which, for its builders, may be precisely the point. Strict 130% {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} keeps every pledge solvent.

usdkg-gold-dollar.title: Kyrgyz Gold, Dollar Wrapper
usdkg-gold-dollar.text: USDKG is a Kyrgyz Republic gold-backed stablecoin minted against 376 kg of LBMA bullion, with 100.6% overcollateralization but only ISRS 4400 procedures rather than a full audit {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. USDKG is a sovereign experiment in commodity-backed stablecoin design: the Kyrgyz Republic's Ministry of Finance sold 376 kilograms of LBMA Good Delivery gold bars to LLC Virelint Group, which stores them in sealed boxes at an unnamed bank, and the state-owned OJSC "Issuer of Virtual Assets" mints USD-pegged tokens against that pile. The gold is real -- Kyrgyzaltyn, the state mining monopoly that refined it, has been LBMA-listed since 2022 -- but the trust chain from bullion to token runs through private intermediaries whose bank won't even let auditors see the access logs. Kreston Global's quarterly report is an ISRS 4400 agreed-upon procedures engagement, not an audit, and it explicitly disclaims assurance -- a distinction that matters when 100.6% overcollateralization is the only buffer between a gold price dip and undercollateralization. The ConsenSys Diligence smart contract audit found no critical issues but confirmed what the architecture implies: owner multisig can pause all transfers, compliance multisig can blacklist any address and destroy its tokens. At $50M across Tron and Ethereum with thin DEX-only liquidity, USDKG is less a stablecoin for DeFi and more a cross-border payments rail for Central Asian corridors -- the question is whether Bishkek's gold vaults can inspire the same confidence as, say, Brink's London.

usdh-hermetica.title: Bitcoin's Synthetic Dollar, On Stacks
usdh-hermetica.text: Hermetica's USDh is the Ethena playbook on Bitcoin-native infrastructure: a {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar deployed on Stacks L2 with a Runes variant on Bitcoin L1. Hermetica brings the Ethena playbook to Bitcoin-native infrastructure: BTC spot plus short {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} futures creating a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} synthetic dollar, deployed exclusively on Stacks L2 with a Runes variant on Bitcoin L1. At $9 million in circulation from a protocol that raised $1.7 million in seed funding, USDh is the smallest delta-neutral stablecoin on the dashboard and the only one that touches neither Ethereum nor a single EVM chain. Yield flows to sUSDh stakers via {{term:funding-rate}}funding-rate{{/term}} payments from the short perpetual positions, with Hermetica advertising up to 25% APY -- a figure that depends entirely on perpetual funding rates staying positive, which historically they do until they catastrophically don't. Minting requires KYC/AML verification through Hermetica's app, collateral sits on centralized exchanges with CEX-tier {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and a DIA oracle prices the token on-chain -- a trust stack that makes this less a trustless Bitcoin dollar and more a managed fund with a Clarity smart contract wrapper. The single-chain, single-entity design is refreshingly honest about what it is: a bet that Bitcoin's basis trade can sustain a stablecoin ecosystem outside the EVM monoculture.

usdsc-startale.title: Sony's Dollar, M0's Plumbing
usdsc-startale.text: USDSC is a Soneium-exclusive 1:1 wrapper around M0's $M with the same {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} reserves and {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} -- the bet is Sony's L2 generating enough gravity for a chain-native dollar. USDSC is what happens when a Sony-backed L2, a Singapore web3 studio, and M0's T-bill infrastructure converge on the thesis that every blockchain needs its own branded dollar. The token is a 1:1 wrapper around M -- the same short-term {{term:treasury}}Treasury bill{{/term}} reserves, the same on-chain Validator {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, the same bankruptcy-remote SPV structure -- repackaged with freeze authority and a Soneium-exclusive deployment for Startale's app ecosystem. At $4 million in supply on a single chain with 6,000 holders, USDSC is less a stablecoin competing for market share and more a distribution play: onramp through MoonPay, transact in the Startale App, earn yield through sUSDSC vaults audited by Quantstamp, OpenZeppelin, and four other firms. The bet is that Sony's Soneium -- an OP Stack L2 with 500 million transactions -- generates enough user gravity to make a chain-native stablecoin viable where dozens of others have failed. Whether the world needs another M0 wrapper with a different logo remains an open question, but the institutional lineage is harder to dismiss than most sub-$5M coins can claim.

ctusd-citrea.title: Bitcoin's Dollar, MoonPay's Rails
ctusd-citrea.text: ctUSD is Citrea's native dollar issued by MoonPay on M0; T-bill backed and fiat-onramp wide, but tiny on a brand-new BTC ZK-rollup. ctUSD is the native stablecoin for Citrea, the first Bitcoin ZK-rollup, issued by MoonPay and powered by M0's T-bill infrastructure — the same bankruptcy-remote SPVs, the same on-chain Validator {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, the same short-term {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} backing that now underwrites half a dozen branded dollars across the ecosystem. At roughly $1 million in circulation on a single chain that most DeFi users have never heard of, ctUSD's value proposition is less about the dollar and more about the distribution: MoonPay's 30 million verified users can buy in via Visa, Mastercard, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and PayPal across 49 U.S. states and 160+ countries, making the on-ramp wider than the destination chain's current user base. The Founders Fund and Galaxy Digital backing lends the kind of institutional credibility that typically accompanies products ten times this size, while Citrea's Bitcoin-secured ZK-rollup architecture means ctUSD settles on the most decentralized base layer in existence — even if the stablecoin itself is as centralized as every other M0 derivative. The bet is straightforward: Bitcoin needs a native, compliant dollar to unlock DeFi beyond wrapped-BTC vaults, and MoonPay's fiat rails plus M0's reserve plumbing make ctUSD the path of least resistance for that thesis. Reserves are an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} short-Treasury fund and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through MoonPay's fiat rails.

usdat-saturn.title: Saylor's Yield, M0's Backing
usdat-saturn.text: Saturn's USDat is a permissioned M0 wrapper of short-term {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, with the actual Saylor exposure sitting one floor up in the sUSDat vault that rotates into Strategy's perpetual preferred equity. Saturn pitches itself as the digital monetary layer for a financial system backed by Bitcoin, but at launch USDat is just another M0 wrapper -- 100% of the collateral is short-term Treasury bills via M0 Protocol, which means the dollar in your wallet is bankrupt-remote SPV plumbing wearing Saturn's logo. The Bitcoin part lives one floor up, in the sUSDat staking vault, where capital is dynamically rotated into STRC -- Strategy's perpetual preferred equity -- based on Michael Saylor's loan-to-value ratio, targeting 11%+ APY routed through Clear Street {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and a Securitize-administered BVI fund. USDat is permissioned and geofenced from the United States, the EEA, and OFAC jurisdictions, so the audience is sophisticated offshore capital comfortable with both KYC onboarding and a 3-7 day unstaking queue. With $33 million in circulation barely a month after the March 2026 deployment, three audits from Certora and Three Sigma, and live proof-of-reserves still pending Accountable and Chainlink integration, USDat is the cleanest expression yet of the thesis that crypto's next yield wave doesn't come from on-chain perps or {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} T-bills -- it comes from being long whatever Saylor is short.

usdk-orki.title: Swellchain's Restaked Dollar
usdk-orki.text: Orki's USDK brings Liquity V2's immutable {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} architecture to Swellchain, betting the protocol on LST/LRT collateral and the restaking thesis staying solvent. Orki Finance brings Liquity V2's immutable {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} architecture to Swellchain, accepting LST and LRT collateral like swETH and rswETH to mint USDK -- a design that bets the entire protocol on the restaking thesis staying solvent. At roughly $10K in circulation, USDK is less a functioning stablecoin and more a proof of concept that Liquity's code can be deployed wherever restaked ETH derivatives accumulate. The collateral mix of liquid staking and liquid restaking tokens earns an alt-lst-bridged-or-mixed quality classification, reflecting the layered smart contract risk inherent in assets that are themselves wrappers of wrappers. User-set interest rates and permissionless collateral {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} with Liquity-style dynamic fees preserve the decentralized governance story -- no admin keys, no multisig, no entity to call when things go sideways. Whether Swellchain generates enough DeFi activity to justify a native {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} dollar remains the open question, but at least the architecture is honest about what it is: a minimalist borrowing primitive for restaking degens who want leverage without leaving the chain, with Liquity-style {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}} as the only safety net.

usdq-quill.title: Scroll's Liquity Outpost
usdq-quill.text: Quill's USDQ deploys Liquity V2's immutable {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} on Scroll with wETH/wstETH/weETH/SCR collateral; accepting the host chain's own token introduces a reflexivity loop. Quill Finance deploys Liquity V2's immutable {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} blueprint on Scroll, minting USDQ against wETH, wstETH, weETH, and -- notably -- SCR, Scroll's own native token, which injects a layer of alt-L1 governance token risk that Liquity's Ethereum-native design never contemplated. At roughly $132K in circulation, USDQ is a micro-cap stablecoin on a Stage 0 zk-rollup, meaning both the dollar and the chain it lives on are still proving themselves. The collateral mix earns an alt-lst-bridged-or-mixed classification: LST derivatives are reasonable CDP fodder, but accepting SCR as collateral ties the stablecoin's health to the market sentiment of the very chain hosting it -- a reflexivity loop that gets uncomfortable in a drawdown. Immutable code and Liquity-style dynamic {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} fees preserve the decentralization credentials, with no admin keys or multisig to intervene when collateral ratios tighten and {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}} fire. The thesis is that Scroll needs a native {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} dollar and Liquity's battle-tested architecture is the safest way to build one -- but with supply this thin, the real test is whether anyone shows up to use it.

chfau-allunity.title: The Frankfurt-Zurich Pipeline
chfau-allunity.text: CHFAU is AllUnity's MiCA-licensed CHF stablecoin, backed 1:1 in segregated EU bank accounts; competes on trust infrastructure, not yield. AllUnity's CHFAU extends the Deutsche Boerse consortium's stablecoin ambitions from the euro to the Swiss franc, backed by the same DWS-Galaxy-Flow Traders alliance that produced EURAU and regulated under the same BaFin EMI license. CHF reserves sit 1:1 at CRR credit institutions in segregated accounts, a reserve model that is aggressively boring by design — MiCA's EMT rules prohibit interest on token holdings, so CHFAU competes on trust infrastructure rather than {{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}}. At roughly 2.5 million CHF in early circulation on Ethereum alone, it enters a CHF stablecoin market shared with VNX's VCHF and Frankencoin's decentralized ZCHF — three philosophically distinct approaches to putting the Swiss franc on-chain. The safe-haven currency angle is real: in periods of macro stress, CHF demand spikes, and having a MiCA-compliant on-ramp with institutional-grade plumbing positions CHFAU for a use case that only materializes when everything else is going wrong. Institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at credit institutions supports statutory 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} under MiCA Article 49.

buck-buck-assets.title: The Bitcoin Dollar Bet
buck-buck-assets.text: BUCK was Bridge Building's USDC-redeemable savings stablecoin backed by Strategy Inc. preferred stock (STRC) before its April 2026 wind-down. BUCK billed itself as "the world's first SavingsCoin" — a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} stablecoin whose treasury was 77% Strategy Inc. perpetual preferred stock, making it less a dollar and more a leveraged view on MicroStrategy's Bitcoin conviction with a dollar wrapper. The yield story (targeting 7% annually via STRC dividends, distributed as monthly rebases) was compelling until you traced the dependency chain: STRC pays dividends from a company whose entire thesis is that Bitcoin goes up forever, which is either a feature or a ticking clock depending on your priors. A BVI-domiciled entity with a single-entity governance model, upgradeable proxy contracts, and a denylist — controlled by ex-Uber and ex-Bird executives — was not the typical stablecoin trust model, though monthly {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} from The Network Firm added a layer of professional accountability. At roughly $2 million in circulation with 261 holders and negligible DEX volume, BUCK ended its life as a micro-cap experiment in whether you can build a savings product on top of someone else's Bitcoin maximalism.

bd-basedollar.title: Liquity's Fork, Aerodrome's Yield
