bd-basedollar.text: BD is a pre-launch Liquity V2 fork on Base, designed as an {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} dollar stablecoin minted against LP token collateral and earning AERO yield. Base Dollar takes Liquity V2's battle-tested {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} architecture and replants it on Base with a twist: instead of ETH collateral, borrowers deposit LP tokens — routing the stablecoin's security model through Aerodrome's liquidity layer and harvesting AERO farming rewards as the yield engine. Revenue splits three ways between users, a protocol-owned liquidity treasury, and BD stakers, a design that ties the protocol's survival to the depth of Base's DEX ecosystem rather than ETH price alone. The project recently completed an external audit that surfaced a high-severity LP token price manipulation vulnerability and a medium-severity timelock bypass, both now remediated with fuzz testing added — the kind of findings that are routine for a Liquity fork adapting to exotic collateral types but worth watching post-launch. Still in the auditing phase with a Q2 2026 target, Base Dollar is betting that LP-collateralized debt positions can offer better capital efficiency than vanilla ETH CDPs, though the trade-off is inheriting every smart contract risk in the Aerodrome stack on top of its own.

wm-m0.title: The Plumbing's Plumbing
wm-m0.text: wM is M0's non-rebasing ERC-20 wrapper over M, backed by short-term U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills in bankruptcy-remote SPVs — holders forfeit the yield, which routes to TTG-approved earner accounts. wM is the non-rebasing wrapper that turns M0's {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}}-bill token into something a normal ERC-20 contract can hold without breaking — and the price of that convenience is that holders volunteer to forfeit the yield. Underneath sits the same 30-to-90-day {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills, the same bankruptcy-remote SPVs, the same Validator {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} as M itself, but the WrappedMToken contract routes all accrued yield to TTG-approved earner accounts (read: the downstream M0 ecosystem — USDat, USDSC, ctUSD, mUSD, USD0, and friends) via claimExcess(), leaving wM holders with a flat dollar that does nothing. There is no blacklist, no freeze, no pause function — a refreshingly minimal surface for a centralized stablecoin built on {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} collateral — and wrap/unwrap are open and free, so the peg holds by pure arbitrage against M. At roughly $93M in circulation across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Plume, and Solana, wM is the composability primitive the entire M0 ecosystem builds on top of: nobody is meant to hold it directly, everyone is meant to hold something built from it. It is the cleanest expression of M0's thesis that the yield should belong to whoever bothers to put the dollar to work, not to whoever happens to be holding it when the music stops.

usdnr-nerona.title: A Private Bank for Five Wallets
usdnr-nerona.text: Nerona's USDnr is a $50M M0-wrapper stablecoin held by exactly five wallets, with permissioned KYC-gated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} -- the T-bill carry accrues to Nerona, not holders. Nerona USD is a $50M M0-wrapper stablecoin issued by a private-wealth-management startup that has so far convinced exactly five wallets to hold it -- a holder count more befitting a family office than a stablecoin. The token is structurally a thin wrapper over M0's $M (collateralised by Superstate's USTB {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} fund and minted by MXON), and despite Nerona's marketing copy promising capital that 'works while you don't', USDnr itself is non-yield-bearing: the T-bill carry accrues to the M0 reserve and Nerona, not to holders. Governance is single-entity, redemption is permissioned and KYC-gated, and the wrapper inherits every M0-layer risk -- minter insolvency, M0 governance deactivation, and the small matter of being unregulated. Mind the symbol: this is USDnr (Nerona, on Ethereum), not USDN (Noble's M0-wrapper on Cosmos) -- sloppy press copy and screenshots conflate the two, but they share nothing beyond the M0 plumbing underneath. A private bank for the onchain era, with a circulating-supply-to-holders ratio that rounds to $10M per client.

usdk-kast.title: The Anjouan Card Dollar
usdk-kast.text: KAST's USDK is an Anjouan-domiciled M0 wrapper of tokenized {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, distributed via a fintech card app -- T-bill yield is retained by KAST, not passed to holders. KAST Dollar is what you get when a Comoros-domiciled fintech wraps M0's tokenized {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, slaps a card on top, and quietly pockets the yield. The token sits on Solana as a Token-2022 mint with permissioned transfer hooks and confidential-transfer extensions wired in -- useful if you trust KAST and BitGo, awkward otherwise. At roughly $24M outstanding it is still proof-of-concept scale, riding entirely on M0 Validator {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} rather than its own audit trail. Holders earn nothing; if you want the T-bill carry you're nudged into USDKy, KAST's separately rebasing twin. The legal stack -- KAST Tech in Anjouan, {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} by partners, 'not a bank' disclaimer in bold -- is the modern offshore neobank uniform. A cleaner version of buying T-bills than most card-app stablecoins, provided you've made peace with single-jurisdiction issuer risk and a regulator most maps don't bother to label.

xo-exodus.title: Self-Custody's Custodial Dollar
xo-exodus.text:
MoonPay mints, M0 wraps, Exodus distributes — a Treasury-backed Solana token whose yield accrues to issuers and whose authorities live on a single MoonPay key.

When a self-custody wallet best known for letting users hold their own keys decides to mint its own dollar, the result is XO Cash: a MoonPay-issued, M0-wrapped {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} claim wearing an Exodus hoodie. The reserves sit in MoonPay's regulated SPVs under institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and the M0 yield quietly accrues to the issuers, not the holders, which is the polite way of saying XO is a payment rail with a stablecoin garnish. Token-2022 ships with pausable, transfer-hook, and permanent-delegate authorities all held by a single MoonPay key, so the 'self-custody' marketing applies to your wallet but not to your tokens. Initial proof of product-market fit was paying X Games athletes $2,500 signing bonuses, which is either a charming retail use case or a launch metric in search of a thesis. Backed by short-dated Treasuries, geofenced where it has to be, and aimed squarely at the Exodus Pay card audience that has never asked what an SPV is.

jpysc-sbi-startale.title: Japan's First Trust-Bank Yen
jpysc-sbi-startale.text: Pre-launch trust-bank yen from Shinsei + SBI VC Trade + Startale under Japan's Type III electronic payment framework; Q2 2026 target. JPYSC is the first JPY stablecoin issued through Japan's trust bank framework rather than under JPYC's prepaid payment instrument workaround — and that distinction is the entire product. Shinsei Trust & Banking issues, SBI VC Trade distributes, and Startale Group (the Astar Network operator and Sony's Soneium co-developer) handles the technology, with the Q2 2026 target conditional on Financial Services Agency sign-off. Type III electronic payment instrument classification gives JPYSC the legal teeth that JPYC has been negotiating around for three years: redemption rights backed by trust law, segregation of customer assets, and — crucially — permission to allocate up to 50% of reserves to Japanese government bonds, generating yield that the prepaid model can't legally touch. The deployment chain is unannounced, which is unusual for a launch this close, and likely reflects a multi-chain or institutional rail strategy rather than a public-DeFi play. JPYSC is a bet that Japan's $309B-stablecoin-market participation has been gated on legal infrastructure, not technology — and that SBI's institutional client book plus Startale's blockchain stack is the right hand to play once the regulator signs. The trust-bank framework legalizes up to 50% JGB {{term:treasury}}treasury bonds{{/term}} in reserves, trust-segregated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, FSA-grade {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, and statutory {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rights.

rgbp-revolut.title: 13 Million Users, One Brand Ban Away
rgbp-revolut.text:
Revolut's pre-launch UK GBP stablecoin must issue from the e-money subsidiary, not the bank, and is sandbox-only until October 2027 — with proposed BoE rules that legal analysts call structurally unviable.

Revolut got its full UK banking licence on March 11 after a 20-month mobilisation — and promptly confirmed its proposed GBP stablecoin would NOT be issued from the new banking entity. Bank of England rules prohibit a UK bank and its affiliated group from issuing stablecoins across different subsidiaries, so issuance falls back to Revolut Ltd, the e-money entity. That structural wrinkle is the smaller of Revolut's UK regulatory headaches. At the House of Lords on March 25, Head of UK Policy Rory Tanner told peers the UK is 'already behind' the US and EU — and flagged the BoE's proposed ban on 'branded' stablecoins as a commercial blocker (the issuer couldn't put its own name on the token). Priority use case per Tanner: the UK→India remittance corridor, the seventh-largest in the world, not retail payments. The FCA sandbox cohort Revolut joined on Feb 25 is testing phase only; the full UK authorisation regime doesn't activate until October 2027, and the BoE's proposed 40% unremunerated-reserve requirement plus £20,000 individual-holder cap describe a commercial model that UK legal analysts call structurally unviable. Revolut's real asset isn't the token — it's 13 million UK users who already open the app daily, with the bank-style {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} stack the issuer plans to bolt on top. Whether that distribution survives the BoE rulebook is the actual question.

ausdt-tether-alloy.title: Gold Collateral, Dollar Target
ausdt-tether-alloy.text: aUSDT is Alloy by Tether's dollar stablecoin — a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} where verified users deposit Tether Gold (XAUT) and mint dollars at up to 75% LTV, so the peg sits on top of {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} gold rather than a bank account. Alloy Tether turns Tether Gold into a dollar-tracking credit instrument: verified users deposit XAUT into an Ethereum vault, mint aUSDT against a 75% mint-to-value ceiling, and return aUSDT plus fees to withdraw collateral. That gives Pharos a clean on-chain reserve view because the XAUT backing sits in the CMPVault, but it also means aUSDT inherits Tether Gold {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, gold-price volatility, whitelist access, and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} mechanics. The peg is not a bank-account promise; it is an overcollateralized gold position engineered to trade near one dollar.

usdsui-sui.title: Sui Gets Its Native Dollar
usdsui-sui.text: USDsui is Sui's native dollar issued through Bridge (Stripe), backed by short-dated {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}}/repos/MMFs -- a native fiat-backed dollar rather than a bridged USDC. USDsui is the Sui ecosystem dollar issued through Bridge, Stripe's stablecoin infrastructure arm. The asset gives Sui a native fiat-backed stablecoin rather than another {{term:bridge}}bridged{{/term}} dollar, with DefiLlama exposing supply and price data for live peg monitoring. The reserve model is conventional Bridge Open Issuance: cash, short-dated {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}}, repos, and government {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market funds{{/term}} support mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, with institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. Pharos tracks the runtime supply and peg through DefiLlama while keeping reserve composition curated until Bridge exposes a USDsui-specific public reserve feed or Sui supply probe suitable for live reserve sync.

brlv-crown.title: Brazilian Bonds On Chain
brlv-crown.text: BRLV is Crown's centralized Brazilian real stablecoin, mint/redeemed 1:1 for BRL and backed mostly by Brazilian federal {{term:treasury}}Treasury bonds{{/term}} in segregated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. Crown BRLV is a Brazilian real stablecoin backed by federal government bonds pledged for token holders through a security-agent structure. That is a cleaner reserve story than most emerging-market fiat coins: the backing is local sovereign debt rather than offshore dollar liquidity, and the legal structure is designed to keep reserve claims separate from Crown itself. The risks are equally specific: BRL liquidity, Brazilian sovereign-rate volatility, and KYC-gated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}. Pharos tracks the BRL peg directly while treating reserves as curated-validated evidence until Crown's reserve page proves machine-readable enough for a dedicated adapter.

usdglo-glo.title: Public-Goods Float
usdglo-glo.text: Glo Dollar is a Brale-issued USD stablecoin whose reserve yield funds public goods, with monthly {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} and 1:1 mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through Brale. Glo Dollar is a Brale-issued U.S. dollar stablecoin whose reserve yield funds public-goods causes rather than flowing back to token holders or exchange partners. The mechanics are familiar: cash, cash equivalents, and short-duration U.S. government-backed debt, monthly {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}, and 1:1 mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through Brale. The differentiation is distribution and mission, not financial engineering. At small supply, USDGLO matters to Pharos because it already appears inside other reserve stacks such as Mento, making explicit tracking useful for dependency analysis even before it becomes a large standalone market.

usdon-ondo.title: Ondo Settlement Cash
usdon-ondo.text: USDon is platform settlement cash inside Ondo Global Markets, backed 1:1 by USD in brokerage accounts -- institutional rails with a whitelisted {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route, not retail. USDon is the dollar settlement token inside Ondo Global Markets, backed 1:1 by U.S. dollars in brokerage accounts and used to move between cash and tokenized assets including {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} positions. It is closer to platform settlement cash than a standalone retail stablecoin, which shapes the risk model: institutional rails, access restrictions, and dependence on Ondo's Global Markets structure. CoinGecko provides the runtime price and market-cap path, while Pharos models reserves as brokerage-account cash and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} as a whitelisted platform route until Ondo exposes a dedicated public liquidity or reserve feed.

audm-macropod.title: Australia's New On-Chain Dollar
audm-macropod.text: AUDM is Macropod's centralized Australian dollar stablecoin, redeemable 1:1 by approved clients and backed by AUD cash held in segregated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at Westpac and Banking Circle Australia. Macropod AUDM brings an Australian-dollar unit into the active Pharos set with DefiLlama supply, CoinGecko pricing, Ethereum, Solana, and Redbelly contracts, and issuer documentation describing segregated AUD reserve accounts at Australian ADIs. The product is straightforward: approved Macropod clients can mint and redeem through the platform, with current reserves split mostly between Westpac and Banking Circle Australia, and primary {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} gated to approved clients. The main constraints are scale and disclosure cadence. Pharos can monitor the AUD peg immediately and validate live token supply, while a monthly-report adapter would be needed for stronger reserve automation.

audf-forte.title: Australia's New Regulated Long Tail
audf-forte.text: AUDF is Forte Tech Solutions' centralized Australian dollar stablecoin, redeemable 1:1 with AUD reserves and cash-equivalent assets held in segregated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. Forte AUD is the straightforward version of an Australian stablecoin: issuer-run, AFSL-regulated, publicly documented, and redeemable back into bank-account AUD for eligible users. The reserve story is respectable for a long-tail fiat token because Forte publishes recurring reserve reports and legal terms instead of treating backing as a black box, but the public evidence is still PDF-based rather than a continuously queryable feed. At roughly $3.6 million in market cap, AUDF is not systemically important; the primary path back to fiat is issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} for eligible users. It is interesting because the legal and reserve posture is cleaner than many niche fiat coins even while the liquidity footprint remains small.

busd0-usual.title: Fixed-Maturity USD0 Bond
busd0-usual.text: bUSD0 is Usual's bond-leg wrapper of USD0; before maturity it behaves like a discount bond, not a spot dollar. bUSD0 is Usual's fixed-notional USD0 bond, formerly USD0++, with a June 11, 2028 maturity. It is backed by locked USD0 but does not behave like a spot stablecoin before maturity: par exit requires both bUSD0 and the separate rt-bUSD0 early-exit right, while secondary-market bUSD0 can trade below one dollar. Yield is paid through USUAL coupons rather than dollar NAV growth, so the risk is a mix of USD0 reserve quality, Usual DAO parameter risk, and liquidity/discount risk before maturity. Par {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} requires both tokens, and the underlying USD0 reserve is itself an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} claim.

susde-ethena.title: Ethena's Savings Sleeve
susde-ethena.text: the yield-bearing wrapper over USDe that capitalizes basis-trade income into a rising share price, with cooldown-gated exits. sUSDe is the {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper over USDe. It keeps the same core reserve and {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} stack as USDe, but packages {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} and {{term:funding-rate}}funding rate{{/term}} income from {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} hedges into a rising exchange rate instead of leaving the holder in the base token. The important difference is exit shape: unstaking burns sUSDe immediately, but withdrawing USDe still runs through Ethena's cooldown flow and staking-contract restrictions, so this should not be treated like instant cash.

susds-sky.title: The Plain Sky Savings Token
susds-sky.text: the clean ERC-4626 savings receipt over USDS, with wrapper risk confined to the vault and the underlying Sky reserve mix. sUSDS is the straightforward savings wrapper in the Sky stack. Unlike stUSDS, it does not push holders into a risk-capital module or SKY-backed borrower exposure; it is the direct ERC-4626 savings receipt over USDS. That makes it the clean {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} expression of Sky's base dollar, with wrapper risk mostly limited to the vault contract and the underlying USDS reserve mix, while {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} ultimately falls back to the USDS {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}.

sdai-sky.title: The Classic DSR Wrapper
sdai-sky.text:
The original Dai savings receipt — deposit DAI, accrue the DSR through a rising exchange rate, with wrapper-contract risk on top of DAI-tier CDP risk.

sDAI is the original Dai savings receipt: deposit DAI, receive a token whose redeemable DAI balance grows with the Dai Savings Rate. It adds very little conceptual complexity beyond the base asset, but it still belongs on its own row because holders are choosing a NAV-appreciating {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper with its own liquidity, integrations, and wrapper-contract risk rather than plain DAI — and the underlying still inherits DAI's {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} collateral profile.

sfrxusd-frax.title: Frax's Yield Sleeve
sfrxusd-frax.text:
A staking wrapper over frxUSD that concentrates Frax's custodian and reserve assumptions into a rising-exchange-rate vault share.

sfrxUSD is the savings wrapper over frxUSD. Holders are effectively taking the Frax USD reserve stack and opting into a rising exchange rate instead of the flat base token, so the key risk is not a new reserve book but the same Frax {{term:custody}}custodian{{/term}} and wrapper assumptions concentrated into a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} vault share over T-bill-style {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} collateral.

scrvusd-curve.title: Borrower Interest Receipt
scrvusd-curve.text:
Curve's savings share for crvUSD, whose value grows as Curve routes part of borrower interest and protocol revenue into the vault.

scrvUSD is the savings share for Curve's crvUSD system. It is backed by deposited crvUSD, but its value grows as Curve routes part of crvUSD borrower interest and protocol revenue into the vault. The result is a cleaner hold-for-{{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}} version of crvUSD, while still inheriting the base stablecoin's BTC/ETH {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} collateral profile and peg-defense design.

cusdo-openeden.title: Non-Rebasing OpenDollar
cusdo-openeden.text: cUSDO is OpenEden's non-rebasing wrapper of USDO; same T-bill reserve, yield compounds via price rather than balance. cUSDO is OpenEden's non-rebasing wrapper for USDO. It keeps the same {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}}-backed reserve and issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} framework as the base token, but converts daily {{term:yield-bearing}}yield{{/term}} distribution into price appreciation so it can plug into protocols that do not handle rebasing balances well. Economically it is still an OpenDollar claim, just in a different wrapper format. The underlying claim is an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} short-Treasury exposure.

syusd-aegis.title: Aegis Cooldown Wrapper
syusd-aegis.text: the staked, cooldown-gated wrapper over Aegis YUSD that capitalizes BTC delta-neutral funding into a rising share price. sYUSD is the staked version of Aegis YUSD. It inherits YUSD's BTC spot plus short-{{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} hedge design and off-exchange {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} assumptions, then adds a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} vault wrapper and a seven-day unstaking cooldown on top. That makes it meaningfully different from base YUSD even though both ultimately depend on the same {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} machine running on {{term:funding-rate}}funding rate{{/term}} income.

stusds-sky.title: Sky Risk-Capital USDS
stusds-sky.text: Sky's expert-mode risk-capital module over USDS that funds SKY-backed borrowing and absorbs shortfall via slashing. stUSDS is Sky's expert-mode risk-capital token, not a plain sUSDS savings receipt. Deposited USDS funds SKY-backed borrowing while idle liquidity earns the Sky Savings Rate, exposing holders to borrower shortfall, governance slashing, utilization, and withdrawal-liquidity risk. As a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} module distinct from passive {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} paths, it inherits the broad Sky/USDS ecosystem but should rank differently from USDS and sUSDS because its value can be affected by staked-SKY loan performance.

stcusd-cap.title: Cap Yield Wrapper
stcusd-cap.text:
Cap's ERC-4626 staked wrapper of cUSD where operators borrow reserves against restaker collateral and repay above hurdle — adding operator, restaker, and vault risk on top.

stcUSD is the {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} version of Cap cUSD. Users stake cUSD into an ERC-4626 vault while Cap operators borrow reserve assets against restaker collateral and repay with yield above the hurdle rate. Cap's design attempts to keep stablecoin holders whole through {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} and slashing, but stcUSD still adds operator, restaker, strategy, and vault risk on top of the underlying cUSD basket and its {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanics.

said-gaib.title: AI Infrastructure NAV Token
said-gaib.text:
GAIB's staked AID vault token floats with the NAV of AI infrastructure financing positions — a different asset profile from AID's stable base.

sAID is GAIB's staked AID vault token. Unlike AID, which is intended as the stable base currency backed by {{term:treasury}}Treasuries{{/term}} and accepted stablecoins, sAID floats with the NAV of AI infrastructure financing positions plus stable reserve buffers — a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper sitting on a private credit book. Monthly withdrawal cycles, unrealized-loss-aware unstaking NAV, and private AI financing exposure make it a materially different asset from AID.

msy-main-street.title: Main Street Strategy Share
msy-main-street.text: Yield share over msUSD that accrues from Main Street's options/derivatives strategy reserve; exit requires conversion back through msUSD, carrying strategy, custody, and liquidity risk on top of base USDC redemption. msY is Main Street's {{term:yield-bearing}}yield share{{/term}} over msUSD. It accrues value from the protocol's options and derivatives strategy reserve, while final exit ultimately depends on converting back through msUSD and Main Street's USDC {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} process. The token therefore carries strategy execution, exchange/{{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, liquidity, and governance risk that should not be folded into the base msUSD row.

yusd-yieldfi.title: YieldFi USDC Strategy Vault
yusd-yieldfi.text:
ERC-4626 USDC vault allocating across Pendle PTs, Morpho/Silo vaults, and private credit; risk is allocator decisions and venue performance, not USDC backing.

YieldFi yUSD is an ERC-4626 {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} vault over USDC that allocates capital across Pendle principal tokens, Morpho and Silo vaults, and private-credit vaults. Its stability depends on USDC as the native underlying, but its holder risk comes from active allocator decisions and the performance of those yield venues. Pharos tracks it separately from Aegis YUSD and YO Protocol yoUSD because the name collision hides a distinct issuer and reserve strategy.

sbold-k3-capital.title: K3 Stability Pool BOLD
sbold-k3-capital.text:
A K3-managed ERC-4626 wrapper around BOLD deployed into Liquity V2 Stability Pools — earning interest and liquidation gains but adding vault, oracle, and solver risk.

sBOLD is K3 Capital's ERC-4626 wrapper around BOLD deposited into Liquity V2 Stability Pools. It earns interest and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} gains while automating the conversion of liquidated ETH and LST collateral back into BOLD. The base BOLD system is immutable and fully on-chain with {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-based issuance, but sBOLD adds K3-controlled vault, oracle, solver, and fee-switch risk, so it belongs as a separate wrapper exposure.

ybold-yearn.title: Yearn's BOLD Stability Pool Vault
ybold-yearn.text:
Yearn's ERC-4626 wrapper deploys BOLD into Liquity V2 Stability Pools, layering vault and strategy risk onto Liquity's CDP-redemption design.

yBOLD is Yearn's ERC-4626 wrapper around BOLD deposited into Liquity V2 Stability Pool strategies — a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper that auto-compounds {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} rewards from Liquity's {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} system. It keeps the economic exposure anchored to BOLD while automating allocation across Stability Pools and liquidation-reward compounding through Yearn-managed strategy contracts. Holders can {{term:redemption}}redeem{{/term}} the vault share back into BOLD at the live exchange rate, but the exposure is not the same as holding base BOLD: it adds Yearn vault governance, strategy execution, auction, and smart-contract risk on top of Liquity's collateral-redemption design.

stkgho-umbrella-aave.title: Aave Umbrella GHO Staking
stkgho-umbrella-aave.text: a slashable GHO staking receipt that absorbs Aave bad-debt deficits, distinct from passive savings GHO. Aave Umbrella stkGHO is the slashable GHO staking receipt for Aave's upgraded safety module. It is backed by GHO, but unlike liquid GHO or simple savings GHO, holders accept Umbrella-specific cooldowns, withdrawal windows, and automated {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} if covered GHO deficits occur. That makes it a distinct loss-absorption asset rather than a plain yield venue on the base {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin, with the underlying GHO still relying on {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}.

myrc-blox.title: First Malaysian Ringgit stablecoin
myrc-blox.text: First Malaysian ringgit stablecoin, 1:1 MYR at Maybank under UTMB trustee with monthly attestations; eKYC-gated to Malaysian residents, unlicensed by BNM/SC, tiny supply, single-bank single-jurisdiction concentration. MYRC is a Malaysian Ringgit-pegged stablecoin issued by Blox Blockchain Sdn Bhd, deployed natively on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, and Solana. Each token is collateralised 1:1 by MYR cash deposits held at Maybank under the trustee {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} of Universal Trustee (Malaysia) Bhd. Mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} flow through Malaysian banking rails (FPX) and require eKYC via MyKad, restricting access to Malaysian residents with linked local bank accounts. Blox publishes monthly third-party {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} on its transparency page, but the issuer holds no license from Bank Negara Malaysia or the Securities Commission Malaysia -- SC Malaysia disclaimed jurisdiction in 2022 and BNM has not yet finalised a stablecoin framework. Circulating supply is small (~MYR 5.3M) and reserves are concentrated in a single bank and trustee in a single jurisdiction.

krwq-iq.title: First Korean Won stablecoin, RWA-backed
krwq-iq.text: First 1:1 KRW stablecoin from IQ/Frax, transitioning from USDC backing to a Korean T-bond-heavy reserve via Etherfuse Stablebonds; KYC-gated institutional access. KRWQ is the first stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the South Korean won, launched October 2025 by IQ in partnership with Frax. It uses LayerZero's Omnichain Fungible Token (OFT) standard with Ethereum as the canonical mint chain and Base as the primary bridged destination, sharing unified supply across deployments. Reserves are transitioning from initial USDC backing toward a target mix dominated by short-term Korean Treasury Bonds, which are tokenized through Etherfuse's Stablebond framework and held in segregated, bankruptcy-remote custody at Shinhan Securities, alongside USDC and Frax frxUSD. Mint and redemption are KYC-gated to institutional counterparties (exchanges, market makers, OTC desks), and KRWQ is explicitly not marketed to South Korean residents while domestic stablecoin legislation moves through the National Assembly. The issuer commits to independent monthly attestations starting 2025 but has not yet named an auditor or published a report; live reserves are currently a self-reported on-chain dashboard. Reserves anchor on tokenized Korean {{term:treasury}}treasury bonds{{/term}} as {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} held in segregated Shinhan Securities {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, with KYC-gated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and LayerZero OFT acting as the cross-chain {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}}.

reur-royal-euro.title: Euro Rail, Early Liquidity
reur-royal-euro.text:
A new euro-referenced stable from RIB Digital Holdings with meaningful early market cap but thinner reserve disclosure than mature euro peers.

REUR is a euro-referenced stable-value token issued by RIB Digital Holdings Limited and tracked by CoinGecko across Ethereum, BNB Chain, and Tron. The token has meaningful early market capitalization for a new euro peg, but reserve and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} disclosures are thinner than the larger euro issuers already covered by Pharos, so its risk profile depends heavily on issuer execution rather than mature public transparency.

kgst-kyrgyz-som.title: Central Asia's On-Chain Som
kgst-kyrgyz-som.text: Kyrgyz som stablecoin on BNB Chain claiming 1:1 KGS bank reserves; no verified attestation cadence, USD normalization via secondary FX feeds. KGST is a Kyrgyz som stablecoin tracked by CoinGecko on BNB Chain. It is presented as a fully backed 1:1 KGS token, giving Pharos a direct Central Asian local-currency peg, but public reserve and redemption materials remain limited compared with established regulated fiat issuers. KGST also depends on secondary FX feeds for USD normalization because CoinGecko does not currently expose a native KGS quote. Without a verified cadence of {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, transparent {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, or a documented {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} window, the issuer's 1:1 claim remains unaudited by Pharos.

audx-aussie-dollar-token.title: AUD Liquidity With Sparse Footing
audx-aussie-dollar-token.text: AUDX is TAU Pty Ltd's centralized Australian dollar stablecoin, designed for 1:1 AUD {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and backed by AUD cash and government-backed instruments. AUDX is an Australian dollar stablecoin issued by Tau Pty Ltd, trading as AUDX Token, and tracked by CoinGecko across Ethereum, Polygon, and Conflux. The issuer describes AUSTRAC registration and 1:1 AUD reserves held in regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at financial institutions. Market depth is still small, so Pharos treats the reserve story as useful but less battle-tested than older AUD rails with longer public operating histories.

cngn-compliant-naira.title: Naira Settlement Goes Multichain
cngn-compliant-naira.text: cNGN is a centralized NGN stablecoin held 1:1 at designated Nigerian banks, with multichain deployment but issuer/contract-control risk. cNGN is a naira-backed stablecoin tracked by CoinGecko across Base, Ethereum, BNB Chain, Polygon, Monad, and Solana. The issuer describes 1:1 NGN reserves held in designated commercial banks, giving the dashboard a direct Nigerian naira peg with native NGN quote support where CoinGecko provides it. The Solana mint includes administrative controls, so holder risk includes issuer and contract-control assumptions in addition to banking concentration. {{term:custody}}Custody{{/term}} sits at the bank level and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is issuer-managed rather than open.

brl1-brl1.title: Small-Cap Real Exposure
brl1-brl1.text: BRL1 is a centralized Brazilian real stablecoin, targeting a 1:1 peg with a BRL reserve mix of Brazilian {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} ETFs, repo agreements, and cash equivalents. BRL1 is a Brazilian real stablecoin tracked by CoinGecko on Polygon. It adds another BRL-denominated route alongside the older Brazilian real tokens in Pharos, but with a smaller operating footprint and less public reserve transparency than the most established local issuers, including the absence of regular third-party {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}. Pharos therefore models the peg as issuer-backed while keeping disclosure confidence conservative.

wars-argentine-peso.title: ARS Peg With Split Signals
wars-argentine-peso.text: WARS is an Argentine peso stablecoin from Ripio's wFIAT suite, tracked across six EVM chains with the same contract address but weaker reserve and redemption confidence than major fiat issuers. WARS is an Argentine peso stablecoin tracked by DefiLlama across Ethereum, Base, World Chain, BNB Chain, Polygon, and Gnosis, with CoinGecko also listing the token below the current $1M market-cap threshold. That split makes it eligible through DefiLlama coverage but still a higher-uncertainty addition: the same contract address appears across the EVM deployments via {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} infrastructure, while ARS {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} confidence remain weaker than major fiat issuers.

pusd-polymarket.title: The Prediction-Market Wrapper
pusd-polymarket.text:
An application-tier dollar balance token mapped to USDC on Polygon, with risk concentrated in the Polymarket app rails rather than a new reserve.

Polymarket USD is the dollar balance token used around Polymarket deposits and withdrawals on Polygon. Its collateral story is simple: the token is intended to map to USDC and USDC.e in Polymarket rails, so reserve risk is mostly wrapper, {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}}, and app-access risk rather than a new asset mix. Pharos enables curated reserve validation against the Polygon contract and keeps the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path documented through Polymarket docs. The token should be read as an application dollar, not an independent issuer reserve.

rusd-royal-dollar.title: The Royal Reserve Claim
rusd-royal-dollar.text:
A Royal/R Coins fiat-backed dollar on three chains whose reserve composition and redemption mechanics are not yet transparent enough to model rigorously.

Royal Dollar presents itself as a fiat-backed dollar issued by the Royal/R Coins ecosystem across Ethereum, BSC, and Tron. Public material supports the existence of issuer-managed reserves, but the composition and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanics are not transparent enough to model as a high-quality fiat backstop. Pharos classifies the collateral as {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-backed while assigning a high reserve-risk slice until stronger {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} data exists. The live reserve sync is limited to validating that tracked on-chain supply is present and then displaying the curated reserve view.

usdr-ring.title: The Ring Protocol Dollar
usdr-ring.text: Ring Protocol's USDR is a small crypto-backed synthetic dollar with modest documentation; the dashboard models the reserve stack conservatively as protocol collateral and liquidity positions. Ring USD is a crypto-backed synthetic dollar from Ring Protocol. Its public footprint is small, so the dashboard models the reserve stack conservatively as protocol collateral and liquidity positions rather than a granular attested basket. The Ethereum supply is eligible for curated reserve validation, but {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} quality still depends on Ring-specific mechanics and protocol liquidity. That makes USDR a long-tail collateralized dollar with meaningful smart-contract and governance dependency.

uusd-anything-labs.title: The BSC Unity Dollar
uusd-anything-labs.text: Unity USD is a small BSC dollar token from Anything Labs with limited public reserve detail — tracked with a high-risk reserve slice and conservative redemption assumptions. Unity USD is a BSC dollar token from the UUSD/Anything Labs ecosystem. The collateral and peg design are presented as protocol managed via {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} mechanics, but public reserve detail is limited, so Pharos uses a single high-risk reserve slice rather than implying precision. The BSC contract is tracked for supply and curated reserve validation. Until clearer reserve proofs are available, UUSD should be treated as a small, governance-dependent crypto-backed stablecoin where {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} parameters and exit liquidity are not externally verifiable.

jusd-jusd-stable-token.title: The Small Multichain Dollar
jusd-jusd-stable-token.text: Long-tail multichain USD token (BSC + Polygon) with issuer/protocol-managed crypto collateral; reserve composition unverified. JUSD is a long-tail dollar token with BSC and Polygon contracts and issuer/protocol documentation. Pharos models its reserves as protocol-managed crypto collateral because public materials do not provide a reviewed, granular collateral breakdown. The BSC deployment is used for curated validation, while Polygon is kept for discovery. Its main risk is not the stated dollar target, but the limited transparency around reserve composition and live redemption depth. Until JUSD publishes a third-party {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} and discloses {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop and reserve quality remain unmodelled by Pharos.

jusd-juicedollar.title: Bitcoin-backed dollar on Citrea
jusd-juicedollar.text: Citrea-native BTC-collateralized USD using a Frankencoin/d-EURO oracle-free CDP architecture; sub-$1M cap, early-network depth is the main risk. Juice Dollar is a Citrea-native USD stablecoin minted from BTC collateral in overcollateralized positions. The design follows the Frankencoin / d-EURO lineage: no external price oracle, no admin-key intervention path in the published docs, on-chain collateral positions, and liquidation mechanics instead of issuer custody. CoinGecko classifies JUSD as a Citrea ecosystem crypto-backed stablecoin, but current public market cap is still sub-$1M, so the main risk is early-network depth and liquidation-market maturity rather than off-chain reserve opacity. The model is a Frankencoin-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with on-chain {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} and bidding-based {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} standing in for an external oracle.

usda-alpha-partner.title: The Alpha Partner Dollar
usda-alpha-partner.text: a BSC-only dollar token with protocol-managed reserves and opaque mechanics, tracked at long-tail confidence. Alpha Partner USDA is a BSC-issued dollar token with protocol-managed reserves and liquidity controls. The available docs support adding it to the catalog, but they do not support a detailed collateral split, an independent {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} score, or a clean {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} story. Pharos therefore treats USDA as crypto-backed and high risk, with curated validation only checking the tracked on-chain token supply. It belongs in the long-tail cohort where metadata coverage matters but confidence remains limited.

xdai-gnosis.title: The Native Gnosis Dollar
xdai-gnosis.text:
Gnosis Chain's native gas token is an economic claim on bridged DAI, so its peg quality cascades from Maker/Sky and Gnosis bridge infrastructure.

xDAI is the native gas token of Gnosis Chain and is economically tied to DAI {{term:bridge}}bridged{{/term}} into the network. Unlike a normal ERC-20 stablecoin, its canonical supply is native-chain accounting, so Pharos lists the WXDAI wrapper as a traded contract rather than using it as the supply contract. The reserve view is a DAI {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} dependency, making peg quality depend on Maker/Sky DAI — itself a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-backed dollar — and Gnosis bridge infrastructure. It is more infrastructure dollar than issuer token.

usdx-kava.title: The Legacy Kava Debt Dollar
usdx-kava.text: Kava USDX is a legacy {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} debt token trading well below peg, kept in the catalog as a historical depeg case rather than a healthy par dollar. Kava USDX is the older Kava Mint {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} debt token backed by crypto collateral and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} mechanics, sustained by {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} that has not been enough to defend the peg in practice. The asset remains visible in DefiLlama provider data, but its market price has spent extended periods below the dollar target, so Pharos flags it as a legacy depeg-risk entry. There is no supported canonical token contract to attach for reserve sync. Its tracking value is mostly historical and analytical: it shows how a live provider entry can coexist with a prior depeg narrative.

xtusd-xt.title: The XT Exchange Dollar
xtusd-xt.text:
XT.com's centralized dollar token has minimal public reserve disclosure; Pharos treats it as CEX-issued credit with very high transparency risk.

XTUSD is an exchange-issued dollar token associated with XT.com. The provider footprint is enough to admit it through CoinGecko, but its main chain is outside the configured Pharos chain set and public reserve detail is thin. Pharos treats the reserves as issuer-managed CEX assets under undisclosed {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} with very high transparency risk, and no holder-side {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop is modeled. That keeps the token visible without overstating its redemption or reserve quality.

hbd-hive.title: The Hive Conversion Dollar
hbd-hive.text: HBD is Hive's {{term:algorithmic}}algorithmic{{/term}} dollar redeemable on-chain for $1 of HIVE via witness-set conversion, with haircut rules when system debt exceeds thresholds. Hive Backed Dollar is a protocol-native dollar claim inside the Hive ecosystem. It targets $1 through HIVE conversion rules and witness-set savings parameters, not through cash or Treasury {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. That makes the collateral base reflexive to the value and governance of Hive itself, especially under haircut conditions. Pharos classifies HBD as crypto-backed and decentralized while flagging that the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop is protocol conversion capacity, not liquid off-chain reserves.

jpyc-jpyc-v1.title: The Legacy JPYC Series
jpyc-jpyc-v1.text: Legacy prepaid-payment yen token series predating JPYC's funds-transfer-token migration; retained only for discovery and validation. JPY Coin v1 is the older JPYC token series, separate from the current JPYC deployment already tracked by Pharos. It is backed by yen-denominated reserve obligations and legacy redemption processes rather than the newer funds-transfer-token contracts. The Ethereum, Polygon, and Gnosis deployments are retained for discovery and reserve validation. Its main reason to track separately is migration clarity, because the old and current JPYC contracts are not interchangeable. The legacy prepaid {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} model and its narrower {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} processes are the reason v1 is not interchangeable with the current FSA-licensed JPYC contract.

nxusd-nereus.title: The Nereus CDP Dollar
nxusd-nereus.text: Small Avalanche CDP stablecoin minted by Nereus Finance against overcollateralized lending positions; transparent enough to track, risky enough to score conservatively, with a sustained soft-depeg pattern. NXUSD is a crypto-backed debt token minted through Nereus Finance on Avalanche via {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics. The reserve stack is modeled as {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} lending positions, which makes the peg dependent on collateral volatility, {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}}, and protocol governance. Pharos uses the Avalanche contract for curated reserve validation, but does not infer a liquid par {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path from that alone. NXUSD fits the small CDP stablecoin pattern: transparent enough to track, risky enough to score conservatively.

wemix-dollar-wemix.title: The WEMIX Ecosystem Dollar
wemix-dollar-wemix.text: WEMIX Dollar is a dollar token native to the WEMIX ecosystem, admitted via CoinGecko with no in-scope contract — issuer and ecosystem managed, high-risk until more granular proofs are available. WEMIX Dollar is a dollar token native to the WEMIX ecosystem. It is admitted through CoinGecko, but its primary chain is not part of the current Pharos contract universe, so the catalog stores no contract and no live reserve sync. The reserve view is therefore issuer- and ecosystem-managed with WEMIX-side {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and the underlying {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} composition is classified high-risk until more granular proofs are available. It should be treated as an ecosystem unit rather than a broadly composable stablecoin.

suiusde-sui.title: The Sui Ethena Dollar
suiusde-sui.text: a Sui-native Ethena whitelabel synthetic dollar that inherits Ethena's basis-trade and custody mechanics. eSui Dollar is a Sui-native Ethena whitelabel synthetic dollar rather than a simple bridged USDe wrapper. Pharos models the dependency through Ethena-style collateral and hedging mechanics, with reserve risk concentrated in digital-asset collateral, short {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} execution under {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} construction, off-exchange {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and Sui deployment controls. It is tracked through DefiLlama and the Sui contract, but current reserve sync adapters do not probe Sui supply.

vcred-vcred.title: The Hemi Credit Dollar
vcred-vcred.text: vCRED is a Hemi-based credit stable asset with thin public reserve detail — protocol credit and crypto collateral, no verified fiat reserve. vCRED is a Hemi-based credit stable asset with limited public reserve granularity. Pharos adds the Hemi contract and treats the backing as protocol credit and crypto collateral via {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} rather than a verified fiat reserve. The curated reserve sync can validate supply on the configured EVM chain, but it cannot validate the off-chain or strategy quality behind the collateral. The result is a tracked but high-risk long-tail dollar where {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} parameters and redemption depth remain operationally opaque.

mai-qidao.title: The Multichain QiDao Dollar
mai-qidao.text: QiDao's long-running overcollateralized stablecoin minted against crypto vaults across multiple EVM chains; resilience depends on collateral quality, liquidations, and governance rather than an issuer balance sheet. MAI is the long-running QiDao overcollateralized stablecoin, minted against crypto vaults across multiple EVM deployments through {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics. Its resilience depends on collateral quality, bridge exposure, {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}}, and QiDao governance rather than an issuer balance sheet. Pharos tracks the major supported deployments and uses Polygon for curated reserve validation. The entry also preserves the MIMATIC provider identity while presenting the more familiar MAI name.

spusd-soulpeg.title: The SoulPeg Dollar
spusd-soulpeg.text:
A small BSC dollar wrapping a soul-bound sUSDC position via Venus lending; no Pharos-reviewed holder USDC exit path makes it protocol-dependent.

SoulPeg USD is a BSC dollar token with protocol-managed collateral and liquidity. Public docs support the basic peg and contract metadata but do not expose enough reserve detail for a granular basket, so Pharos therefore uses a high-risk curated reserve slice and validates the BSC supply path. Until {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} and reserve data become more transparent, spUSD remains a small protocol-dependent dollar rather than a high-confidence stablecoin.

inalpha-nest.title: The Nest Vault Share
inalpha-nest.text: NAV-priced dollar vault token holding private/structured credit with nTBILL and stablecoin buffers; not a par stablecoin. Nest Alpha Vault LP is included because providers classify it as a dollar-referenced asset, but its behavior is closer to a NAV share than a par stablecoin. The token can appreciate or drift with vault strategy performance, so Pharos marks it yield-bearing and NAV-style. Reserve validation checks the on-chain token, while the reserve slice remains the Nest Alpha strategy book. This is useful coverage, but it should not be compared directly with cash-backed dollars. The underlying mix is {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} credit with an nTBILL {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} buffer, so {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} depth depends on the vault's liquid stablecoin layer rather than direct par exit.

eusd-telcoin.title: The Telcoin Bank Dollar
eusd-telcoin.text: eUSD is Telcoin Digital Asset Bank's dollar stablecoin issued under a Nebraska depository charter, with KYC-gated 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through banking rails. Telcoin eUSD is a bank-issued dollar token from Telcoin Digital Asset Bank. Its regulatory posture is stronger than most long-tail additions, but public reserve telemetry is still limited, so Pharos uses a conservative single reserve slice until more detailed reporting is available. The token has Ethereum, Base, Polygon, and Solana deployments, with Ethereum used for curated validation. The redemption model is issuer-gated through banking-rail {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} rather than permissionless on-chain liquidity.

money-defi-money.title: The defi.money Stablecoin
money-defi-money.text: crvUSD-style crypto-collateral CDP stablecoin on Arbitrum and Optimism, with market-specific risk parameters and limited public collateral transparency. MONEY is defi.money's crypto-backed loan stablecoin on Arbitrum and Optimism, closer to a crvUSD-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} system than to a fixed USDC reserve wrapper. Users deposit approved collateral such as WBTC or ETH, then borrow MONEY against market-specific risk parameters and conversion ranges, with {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}} triggered when those bands are breached. Pharos now treats the reserve description as protocol-approved crypto loan collateral instead of a static USDC-plus-strategy split, while keeping the entry conservative because live collateral composition is still not as transparent as larger CDP systems.

fusd-freedom-dollar.title: The Zano Privacy Dollar
fusd-freedom-dollar.text: FUSD is a Zano privacy-chain dollar token with limited public reserve detail and no Pharos-supported chain {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} — visibility only, low confidence. Freedom Dollar is a Zano ecosystem dollar asset admitted through CoinGecko. Its privacy-chain context and unsupported chain mean Pharos cannot attach a contract or run reserve sync today. The reserve model is therefore a high-risk single slice based on ecosystem collateral and documented peg intent. With no independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} or verifiable {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} disclosures, FUSD remains visible in the dashboard while confidence is kept appropriately low.

zsd-zephyr-protocol.title: The Zephyr Privacy Dollar
zsd-zephyr-protocol.text:
A Djed-inspired algorithmic dollar on Zephyr's Monero-derived private chain, minted against volatile native ZEPH with reserve-ratio constraints.

Zephyr Stable Dollar is a protocol-native private-chain stablecoin admitted through CoinGecko plus Zephyr Scanner telemetry rather than a supported Pharos contract path. Its Djed-inspired {{term:algorithmic}}algorithmic{{/term}} design mints and redeems ZSD against ZEPH reserve collateral, with reserve-ratio constraints intended to preserve {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}. Pharos sources ZSD supply and reserve ratio data from Zephyr's official API, but keeps the reserve slice high risk because the backing asset is volatile native ZEPH on an unsupported private chain.

zys-zephyr-protocol.title: The Zephyr Yield Share
zys-zephyr-protocol.text:
NAV-style yield-share wrapper over ZSD that inherits Zephyr's private-chain and ZEPH-collateral risk through its underlying reserve dependency.

Zephyr Yield Share is the NAV-style {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper for Zephyr's ZSD yield reserve, not the base stablecoin itself. ZYS supply, price, and APY come from Zephyr Scanner because CoinGecko and DefiLlama do not expose the wrapper as a market row. Pharos tracks it separately so yield is attributed to the actual yield-share token while base ZSD remains non-yield-bearing. The entry inherits Zephyr's private-chain and {{term:algorithmic}}algorithmic{{/term}} ZEPH-collateral risk through its ZSD reserve dependency.

iusd-indigo-protocol.title: The Cardano Synthetic Dollar
iusd-indigo-protocol.text: Cardano-native synthetic dollar minted from overcollateralized Cardano-asset CDPs; live reserve adapter does not yet probe Cardano supply. Indigo iUSD is a Cardano synthetic dollar minted against overcollateralized positions in Indigo Protocol. Its risk profile is a classic crypto-CDP profile: collateral volatility, liquidation execution, oracle quality, and governance all matter. Pharos stores the Cardano asset identifier and DefiLlama provider ID, but current live reserve adapters do not probe Cardano supply. The reserve view stays curated until a Cardano-capable live path exists. Risk is dominated by classic {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} dynamics: collateral volatility against the {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} ratio and the maturity of the {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} venue on Cardano.

cdp-enosys.title: The Enosys Flare CDP
cdp-enosys.text: CDP is Enosys's overcollateralized USD stable on Flare, minted from Flare-ecosystem collateral via vaults. Enosys Loans CDP is a Flare-based {{term:cdp}}collateralized debt{{/term}} stable asset. The collateral is modeled as {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} crypto positions inside Enosys Loans, with {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}} and repayments serving as the peg machinery. Pharos tracks the Flare contract and enables curated reserve validation on the EVM-compatible chain. The asset remains high risk because collateral granularity and live {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} depth are limited.

luausd-lumi-finance.title: The Lumi Floor-Dollar
luausd-lumi-finance.text: NAV-style dollar reference token on Arbitrum tied to LUA floor-price mechanics; not a 1:1 redeemable fiat stablecoin. Lumi Finance LUAUSD is not a conventional 1:1 redeemable dollar. It is a dollar-referenced synthetic tied to LUA floor-price and protocol-owned liquidity mechanics, so Pharos marks it as NAV-style and high risk. The Arbitrum contract enables curated validation, but the reserve slice is intentionally broad because public proof is weak. This entry is included for provider coverage, with a warning that the stability claim is nonstandard. The peg claim is closer to an {{term:algorithmic}}algorithmic{{/term}} floor-price reference than fiat backing, and no documented {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} window or third-party {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} is currently modelled by Pharos.

susd-solayer.title: The Solana T-Bill Rebase
susd-solayer.text: a Solana Token-2022 interest-bearing dollar backed by short-dated U.S. T-bill exposure through Solayer workflows. Solayer sUSD is a Solana Token-2022 interest-bearing dollar backed by T-bill exposure through Solayer workflows. The balance-growth mechanics make it {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} rather than a static par token, and the primary risks are {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, issuer workflow access for {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, and Solana token semantics. Pharos uses the Solana mint for curated reserve validation and a 100% {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} reserve slice. A dedicated transparency API would improve the entry, but the current process is enough for tracked coverage.

usx-dforce.title: The Discounted dForce Dollar
usx-dforce.text: dForce USD is an older multichain {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style stablecoin trading at a severe discount to the dollar, tracked as a depeg-risk reference rather than a healthy par dollar. dForce USD is an older multichain stablecoin with both stablecoin and {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} protocol routes, sustained by {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style collateral and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} mechanics. It remains active in DefiLlama, but current provider prices show a severe discount to the dollar target, so Pharos flags the depeg risk directly. The Ethereum contract is used for curated reserve validation, while the reserve slice stays broad because public collateral composition is not granular enough. USX is tracked, but not treated as a healthy par-dollar backstop.

home-homecoin.title: The Property-Lien Dollar
home-homecoin.text: USD stablecoin backed by U.S. home-loan liens and property receivables; foreclosure is the recovery path, not redemption liquidity. HomeCoin is backed by U.S. home loan liens and property-backed receivables rather than cash, T-bills, or crypto collateral. That makes the asset interesting but illiquid: a foreclosure right is not the same thing as immediate redemption liquidity. Pharos tracks the Ethereum contract, self-reported collateral source, and DefiLlama provider entry while assigning high reserve risk. The real-estate lending model is documented in metadata, but the HOME token is not marked as runtime yield-bearing until a holder-level yield source is verified. Reserve risk is dominated by mortgage-lien {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} quality rather than cash {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, and the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path runs through loan workouts, not an issuer window.

cdxusd-cod3x.title: The Facilitator-Minted Dollar
cdxusd-cod3x.text: cdxUSD is Cod3x's Base stablecoin minted by permissioned Facilitators against strategy-managed collateral; risk concentrates in those mint permissions. Cod3x USD is a Base stablecoin minted by protocol Facilitators under configured limits and strategies. The model can be powerful, but it also concentrates risk in facilitator permissions, collateral management, and strategy transparency. Pharos adds the Base contract and uses a single high-risk reserve slice until the backing is more granular. Its {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop is documented at the mechanism level, not scored as a liquid public route. Facilitator-managed minting resembles a permissioned {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} variant rather than a public {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}.

susd-hedgecore.title: The Soul-Bound USDC Yield Token
susd-hedgecore.text: a soul-bound BSC yield wrapper minted from USDC and routed through Venus lending, with operator-controlled exits rather than open redemption. HedgeCore Staked USD Coin is built around USDC deposits routed into Venus yield strategies on BSC. Pharos marks the token as {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} because the product documentation describes yield distribution through HedgeCore mechanisms, while keeping the yield source conservative until a reliable APY feed is wired. The token is operationally restricted: docs describe soul-bound behavior and operator-controlled early {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} paths. Pharos tracks the BSC contract, marks the USDC/Venus dependency, and enables curated reserve validation while keeping the exit path conservative.

usd3-reserve-protocol.title: The Reserve Basket Dollar
usd3-reserve-protocol.text: a Reserve Protocol DTF whose basket pools yield-bearing USDC and USDS wrappers, exposed through Reserve's app-level basket feed. Web 3 Dollar is a Reserve Protocol DTF backed by a basket of {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} stablecoin strategies: Savings USDS, Aave USDC, wrapped Compound USDCv3, and Steakhouse USDC. The mechanism is more transparent than many small stablecoins because the Reserve app and API expose the basket, but {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} still depends on RToken/DTF throttles and basket mechanics. Pharos stores the Reserve proof URL, tracks Ethereum and Base contracts, and syncs the Reserve Protocol basket feed directly. The main risks are strategy exposure, governance, and the fact that the token is a NAV-style basket rather than a simple bank dollar, with indirect {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} exposure flowing through each wrapper underneath.

sofid-sofi.title: The Fed's Own Stablecoin Customer
sofid-sofi.text:
The first nationally chartered FDIC-insured US bank to issue a stablecoin on a public chain, with reserves at the Federal Reserve master account — 100M tokens, three holders.

SoFi Bank is the first nationally chartered, FDIC-insured U.S. bank to issue a stablecoin on a public permissionless blockchain — and the reserves sit in the Federal Reserve's own master account, which is a sentence that would have been science fiction three years ago. SOFID launched on Ethereum in December 2025, minted 100 million tokens for institutional settlement, and has exactly three holders — making it the highest-supply, lowest-holder-count stablecoin on the dashboard by a margin that borders on absurd. The Mastercard settlement partnership and BitGo Mint infrastructure suggest the plumbing is designed for scale with bank-grade {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}; the Solana expansion announced at Accelerate Miami in May 2026 adds the speed layer. The real question isn't whether SoFi can issue a technically competent stablecoin — it clearly can — but whether 13.7 million retail SoFi members will be told they're holding a stablecoin or just 'dollars in their account,' and whether that distinction matters more to regulators than to users.

usdb-bridge.title: Stripe's Invisible Dollar
usdb-bridge.text: Bridge's USDB is Stripe's invisible stablecoin rail, with reserves at BlackRock {{term:money-market-fund}}MMFs{{/term}} under an OCC trust charter and distribution embedded in $1T of annual payment flow. USDB is the stablecoin most people will never know they're using. Bridge -- Stripe's $1.1 billion acquisition -- quietly powers Stablecoin Financial Accounts in 101 countries, turning every Stripe merchant into a potential stablecoin endpoint without the merchant ever touching a token. The OCC conditional national trust bank charter from February 2026 gives Bridge the federal regulatory cover that most stablecoin issuers spend years pursuing, and the reserves sit in cash and BlackRock money market funds with institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. What makes USDB strategically interesting isn't the token itself -- it's that Stripe processes $1 trillion annually and can embed stablecoin settlement into existing payment flows without asking permission from anyone downstream. The competitive moat isn't technology or regulation; it's distribution through indifference.

hkdap-anchorpoint.title: Hong Kong's First Licensed Dollar
hkdap-anchorpoint.text: The first HKMA-licensed HKD stablecoin under the Stablecoins Ordinance; HKD-backed by HQLA in segregated accounts. HKDAP is what happens when Standard Chartered, Hong Kong's largest telco (HKT), and Animoca Brands form a joint venture to build the first stablecoin licensed under the HKMA's Stablecoins Ordinance — a regulatory framework that went from proposal to law faster than most jurisdictions manage a consultation paper. The HKD peg is backed by high-quality liquid assets in segregated accounts, which is regulatory-speak for 'we learned from Tether's early years.' The B2B2C model targeting RWA settlement and cross-border payments positions HKDAP as infrastructure for Hong Kong's push to become Asia's regulated digital asset hub. Whether the consortium structure — a bank, a telco, and a gaming company — can move at stablecoin speed rather than committee speed is the operational question nobody has answered yet. The licensing playbook is built on segregated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, HKMA-mandated {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, and a regulated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path scoped for HKD-denominated {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} settlement.

hkd-hsbc.title: PayMe Gets a Blockchain
hkd-hsbc.text: HSBC's HKMA-licensed HKD stablecoin (pre-launch, H2 2026) leveraging 3.3M PayMe users as its distribution moat. HSBC's HKD stablecoin is the second HKMA-licensed entry and the one with the distribution advantage that matters: 3.3 million PayMe users who already use the app for peer-to-peer payments and won't need to download anything new. The integration into HSBC's HK App for tokenized investment subscriptions hints at the actual product thesis — not a standalone stablecoin for DeFi, but a settlement layer for HSBC's own digital asset products. H2 2026 is the target, the reserves will be HKD-denominated high-quality liquid assets in segregated accounts per HKMA rules, and the symbol hasn't even been confirmed yet. The interesting tension: HSBC is building a stablecoin specifically to avoid depending on anyone else's stablecoin, which is either strategic autonomy or institutional NIH syndrome depending on your perspective. Expect institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, HKMA-mandated {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} routed through PayMe and the HSBC HK app.

okrw-hashed.title: Korea Builds Its Own Chain
okrw-hashed.text: Pre-launch native KRW stablecoin of Maroo, Hashed Open Finance's sovereign L1 testnet built specifically for Korean Won; regulated and open issuance tracks, mainnet targeted for late 2026. Hashed Open Finance didn't just build a KRW stablecoin -- it built an entire Layer 1 blockchain to host it. Maroo is positioned as the first 'sovereign L1' purpose-built for Korean Won stablecoins, with a dual-track design that offers both a regulated path (bank-backed, KYC-gated) and an open path (permissionless issuance). The testnet went live in May 2026 with OKRW as the native token, and mainnet is targeted before year-end. In a country where crypto trading volumes regularly rival the stock market but regulated stablecoin infrastructure is virtually nonexistent, the thesis is less about technology and more about regulatory positioning: whoever builds the compliant KRW on-ramp first captures a market that has been using USDT as a proxy currency by default.

arc-anq.title: The Rupee's On-Chain Debut
arc-anq.text: ARC is a pre-launch INR stablecoin from Anq, designed for a regulated 1:1 rupee peg backed by cash, fixed deposits, and Indian government securities. ARC is India's first attempt at a regulated rupee stablecoin, built by Anq with Polygon's backing and designed to prevent the USD liquidity outflow that India's regulators have been quietly panicking about since USDT volumes on Indian exchanges started dwarfing domestic payment rail throughput. The collateral — cash, fixed deposits, and Indian government securities — reads like a mutual fund prospectus, with {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at regulated Indian banks, and the two-tier framework is explicitly designed to complement rather than compete with the RBI's digital rupee CBDC. The Uniswap v4 whitelisting for compliance is a novel technical approach to the 'permissioned token on a permissionless chain' problem, and primary {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} will run through KYC-gated issuer rails rather than open market making. Whether India's regulatory apparatus will actually let a private rupee stablecoin operate alongside its CBDC remains the existential question that no amount of technical architecture can answer.

brl-b3.title: The Stock Exchange Mints Money
brl-b3.text: BRL-B3 is a pre-launch Brazilian real settlement stablecoin from B3, Latin America's largest stock exchange, designed for its tokenized {{term:rwa}}real-world-asset{{/term}} trading platform. When Latin America's largest stock exchange decides it needs its own stablecoin for tokenized asset settlement, the signal is less about crypto adoption and more about what traditional financial infrastructure considers table stakes in 2026. B3's BRL stablecoin fills the gap left by Brazil's Drex CBDC narrowing its scope — the central bank's digital currency was supposed to handle settlement, but as the project slowed, B3 apparently decided to build the plumbing itself. The H1 2026 target, the exchange-as-issuer model, and the settlement-first use case make this less a DeFi primitive and more a capital markets upgrade with a token wrapper, with {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} expected to sit inside B3's existing clearing infrastructure. The question isn't whether B3 can issue a BRL stablecoin — it clears $3 trillion annually — but whether the regulatory environment will let a stock exchange compete with the central bank's own digital currency project.

usdf-flipcash.title: Coinbase's White-Label Dollar
usdf-flipcash.text: Flipcash's USDF is the first Coinbase Custom Stablecoin, a USDC wrapper used to prove out the stablecoin-as-a-service platform. USDF is the first stablecoin minted through Coinbase's Custom Stablecoins platform -- a stablecoin-as-a-service product that lets any business launch a branded dollar backed 1:1 by USDC. Flipcash is the guinea pig, and the product itself is less interesting than the platform it proves out: if Custom Stablecoins works, every fintech, neobank, and loyalty program can have its own branded dollar without touching reserve management. The dependency chain is explicit -- USDF is a wrapper around USDC, which is a wrapper around BlackRock-managed {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} -- and the governance is centralized-dependent because the token's existence depends on Coinbase continuing to operate the platform. Whether the world needs branded USDC wrappers or whether this is just a new distribution strategy for Circle's existing product is a question Coinbase would prefer you didn't ask too loudly.

krw-imbank.title: Quantum-Resistant Won
krw-imbank.text: Korean commercial-bank KRW PoC on Kaia with post-quantum security; symbolic of regulatory thaw rather than a commercial product. iM Bank's KRW stablecoin proof-of-concept has a feature that most stablecoins won't need for a decade but makes excellent press releases: quantum-resistant post-quantum cryptography via BTQ Technologies on the Kaia blockchain. Set aside the security theater angle, and the actual significance is that a Korean commercial bank is building a KRW stablecoin at all — South Korea's regulatory stance on private stablecoins has been cautious to the point of paralysis, and a bank-led PoC signals that the regulatory ice may be thawing. The Finger partnership handles the wallet and DeFi integration layer, while iM Bank brings the banking license and the KRW reserves. Whether this moves beyond proof-of-concept depends entirely on whether Korean regulators want to compete with Hashed's OKRW for the title of first regulated KRW stablecoin — or whether they'd prefer neither existed. As a bank-issued PoC, the stack assumes regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} of KRW reserves, statutory {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, and a banking-rail {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path that has yet to face commercial traffic.

gldy-streamex.title: The Yield-Bearing Gold Ounce
gldy-streamex.text: GLDY is Streamex's {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} tokenized gold ounce on Base, with Chainlink Proof of Reserve and gold-leasing receivables as the source of returns. Streamex GLDY tracks one troy ounce of gold while passing gold-leasing yield back to token holders. The entry is stronger than most new commodity tokens because it has a Chainlink proof-of-reserves feed on Base and a source-reviewed primary-market {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route for eligible investors. The main caveat is that the yield comes from issuer-managed gold leasing rather than passive vault storage, so Pharos separates the live reserve feed from the still-unwired APY source. GLDY is tracked as a commodity stablecoin, not as a generic RWA fund.

vnxau-vnx.title: The Liechtenstein Gram-Gold Token
vnxau-vnx.text: VNX Gold represents one gram of physical gold under Liechtenstein's regulated-issuer pattern, with AREVA reserve reports and Ethereum supply tracking. VNX Gold represents one gram of physical gold and fits the same regulated-issuer pattern as VNX's fiat stablecoins. AREVA reserve reports and {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}-style VNX documentation give enough backing detail to track the token, while the Ethereum supply probe provides lightweight live sync until a stronger public reserve API is available. Redemption is meaningful but operationally constrained: verified platform users can sell or request physical delivery from larger bar denominations. The risk is less the gold unit and more the issuer, custody, and platform access path.

xagm-matrixdock.title: Matrixdock's Silver Ounce
xagm-matrixdock.text:
Matrixdock extends the XAUm bullion-token model to LBMA silver, with issuer-reported ozPerToken drift the main reconciliation gap.

Matrixdock Silver brings the XAUm model to silver, with LBMA Good Delivery bars and public issuer pages showing supply and bullion metrics. Pharos uses one troy ounce as the silver reference, but the metadata flags Matrixdock's ozPerToken metric because the issuer can report slight dynamic drift. The current live sync validates on-chain supply; a dedicated Matrixdock reserves adapter would be needed for higher-grade live bullion reconciliation against issuer {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} is available through Matrixdock for KYC-approved users, but public fee and capacity terms remain issuer-process dependent.

gramg-token-teknoloji.title: Turkey's Gram-Gold Token
gramg-token-teknoloji.text: GRAMG is Token Teknoloji's Turkish gram-gold stablecoin backed by physical gold at Turkish bank custodians, with issuer-published proof but no machine-readable {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. Token Teknoloji's GRAMG is a one-gram gold stablecoin with reserve materials pointing to Turkish bank custody. The Avalanche deployment has meaningful live supply, so Pharos tracks that chain first and uses CoinGecko commodity admission for runtime coverage. The reserve proof is weaker than a machine-readable attestation, but stronger than a pure marketing claim because the issuer publishes bank-backed proof materials. Pharos does not add a {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop yet because public direct-holder redemption terms are not specific enough.

grams-token-teknoloji.title: Turkey's Gram-Silver Token
grams-token-teknoloji.text: GRAMS is Token Teknoloji's Turkish gram-silver stablecoin backed by physical silver at Turkish bank {{term:custody}}custodians{{/term}}, with supply liveness over independent reserve reconciliation. GRAMS mirrors Token Teknoloji's gold product for silver, with one token representing one gram of physical silver. The research packet found enough issuer reserve material and live Avalanche supply to add the asset, but no clean public reserve API. Pharos therefore treats the live feed as supply liveness over curated reserves rather than independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} remains unmodeled until direct holder terms, limits, and capacity are documented.

euroe-membrane.title: The Small Regulated Euro
euroe-membrane.text: EUROe is Membrane Finance's Finnish EMI-licensed euro stablecoin with 1:1 {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} — small in supply but clean in {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. EUROe is a Finnish-issued euro stablecoin with DefiLlama supply coverage and public Membrane transparency materials. Its circulating supply is small, but it improves non-USD euro coverage and has a clear verified-user issue and redeem path. Pharos uses Solana on-chain supply liveness against curated euro reserves because the reserve {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}} are not exposed as a clean public API. The entry is regulated-issuer coverage, not a high-liquidity market signal.

gbpm-mento.title: Mento's CDP Pound
gbpm-mento.text: GBPm is Mento's British pound stablecoin on Celo, minted from {{term:cdp}}CDPs{{/term}} collateralized by USDm with oracle-priced {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}.
