GBPm extends Mento's Celo FX stablecoin set into sterling using USDm-collateralized CDP rows rather than the older shared reserve basket alone. The new Mento adapter mode reads the dashboard API's GBPm troves and turns live collateral and debt into Pharos reserve metadata. That makes the entry useful despite a modest supply footprint because the backing path is visible and cheap to maintain. The primary risk is dependency on Mento oracles, Celo execution, and USDm collateral quality.

jpym-mento.title: Mento's CDP Yen
jpym-mento.text: Small CDP yen on Celo backed by USDm collateral via Mento troves; CoinGecko-admitted, Mento API exposes live CDP collateral. JPYm is a small but active yen stablecoin on Celo, backed by USDm collateral in Mento CDP troves. Pharos deliberately uses CoinGecko admission because DefiLlama's JPYm supply row was zero during review, while the Mento API still exposes live CDP collateral. The new adapter path keeps reserve sync aligned with GBPm and CHFm without adding a separate infrastructure family. JPYm is tracked for strategic non-USD coverage, with liquidity and oracle dependency as the main caveats. As a Mento FX stablecoin, JPYm rests on a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with USDm {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} and oracle-priced FPMM swaps acting as the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} surface against the reserve.

chfm-mento.title: Mento's CDP Franc
chfm-mento.text: CHFm is a Mento CDP-backed Swiss franc stablecoin on Celo, minted against USDm collateral rather than fiat reserves. CHFm gives Pharos another Swiss-franc stablecoin, but with a very different risk profile from fiat-backed VCHF or Frankencoin. Its reserves are USDm collateral posted into Mento {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} troves, and the live Mento adapter now syncs those rows directly. The asset is small, but the data path is clean enough to track with minimal infrastructure changes. The residual risks are the Celo/Mento mechanism, USDm collateral path, and thin secondary liquidity. {{term:overcollateralization}}Overcollateralization{{/term}} and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} logic inside Mento drive peg maintenance.

bfusd-binance.title: Binance's Account Dollar
bfusd-binance.text: BFUSD is a Binance account product redeemable inside Binance against USD stablecoins, backed by an opaque collateral pool and a {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} hedging portfolio — not a normal on-chain stablecoin. BFUSD is included because it has meaningful CoinGecko coverage and a large Binance user footprint, but it is not a normal on-chain stablecoin. The product lives inside Binance accounts, earns Binance-set rewards, and is {{term:redemption}}redeemable{{/term}} only through Binance-controlled terms that allow limits, fees, delays, and suspension. Pharos therefore treats the reserve stack as very-high-risk opaque exchange {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} rather than independent proof. The entry is useful for market coverage, not for permissionless DeFi composability.

pathusd-bridge.title: Tempo's Bridge Dollar
pathusd-bridge.text: Bridge-issued dollar quote token for Tempo, backed by institutional reserves and redeemable through Bridge-supported flows; matters more as a payment-chain rail than for current scale. pathUSD is the Bridge-issued dollar quote token for Tempo, backed by a conventional reserve portfolio and redeemable back through Bridge-supported {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} flows. The asset matters less because of current scale than because it is native to a payment-focused chain that may become an important stablecoin rail. The risk profile is straightforward: institutional reserve assets and issuer redemption on the strong side, new-chain execution and limited independent reserve telemetry on the weak side.

djed-coti.title: Cardano's Reserve-Band Stablecoin
djed-coti.text: DJED is COTI's overcollateralized Cardano dollar stablecoin; SHEN absorbs reserve volatility but the reserve is volatile native ADA. DJED is Cardano's {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} ADA-backed stablecoin, with SHEN reserve holders absorbing reserve-ratio volatility. The design is more transparent than an issuer account product, but still depends on Cardano liquidity, COTI-run operational components, and a volatile native-asset reserve. Pharos tracks it as a strategic below-threshold asset because it is one of the better-known Cardano stablecoin systems, while leaving live reserves and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} unmodeled until a cleaner adapter path exists. The design is a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style ratio band over native ADA.

usdv-solomon.title: The Ceffu Strategy Dollar
usdv-solomon.text: Solomon's USDv is a Solana stablecoin backed by Ceffu-custodied {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} margin, with aggregate disclosure but no live composition feed and no documented holder redemption path. Solomon USDv is a Solana stablecoin backed by Ceffu-custodied strategy assets and off-exchange {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} margin via {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} positions. The public supply is easy to validate on-chain, but the reserve disclosure is aggregate and does not expose a live composition API. That keeps the Pharos entry conservative: useful for tracking a visible Solana dollar, but not a high-confidence reserve model. Without a documented holder {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route and with all collateral sitting in Ceffu {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, the backstop remains intentionally unmodeled.

xai-silo-finance.title: Silo's Credit-Line Dollar
xai-silo-finance.text:
A Silo Finance CDP dollar minted against approved isolated-market collateral; risk is governance, liquidation quality, and venue-thin secondary liquidity.

XAI is a Silo Finance credit-line stablecoin: users borrow it against approved Silo collateral and repay it to close debt, while SiloDAO controls the credit-line parameters. Pharos validates Ethereum supply and carries the reserve stack as curated Silo collateral rather than a full live vault decomposition. The risk is classic {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} risk in a narrow venue: governance parameters, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} buffers, {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} quality, and whether secondary liquidity can enforce the peg when borrow demand changes.

fxd-fathom.title: XDC's Native CDP Dollar
fxd-fathom.text: FXD is Fathom's {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-minted dollar on XDC, {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} by XDC and stabilized by {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}} plus a stability module. Fathom Dollar gives the XDC ecosystem a native overcollateralized dollar backed by XDC and Fathom collateral-pool positions. It is tracked for chain coverage and DefiLlama visibility despite modest scale. The design is familiar CDP plumbing -- mint against collateral, burn to repay, liquidate weak positions, and use a stability module for peg support -- but the collateral base and chain liquidity make it materially riskier than larger Ethereum CDP systems.

usp-pareto-credit.title: Private Credit With a Dollar Wrapper
usp-pareto-credit.text: Pareto USP is a dollar token backed mostly by private credit vault exposure, with small liquid stablecoin buffers and verified-user-only mint and redeem. Pareto USP is a dollar token backed mostly by Pareto credit vault exposure, with small liquid stablecoin buffers. Verified users can mint and redeem, but open-market holders still depend on liquidity or onboarding, so Pharos models the issuer route with that access caveat. The reserve profile is the main tradeoff: credit exposure may produce useful yield elsewhere in the system, but private credit is not the same as holding {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills or cash behind a redeemable stablecoin, and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through a permissioned path rather than open arbitrage.

dllr-sovryn.title: Rootstock's Mynt Basket
dllr-sovryn.text: DLLR is Sovryn's BTC-backed dollar basket on Rootstock; reserves are other CDP stables (ZUSD-dominated), readable on-chain. DLLR is Sovryn's Rootstock dollar basket, currently dominated by ZUSD with a small DOC position. This is one of the cleaner additions in the batch because the reserve holder can be read on-chain with the existing branch-balances adapter, and the Mynt {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route maps naturally to a basket backstop. The residual risk is not opaque {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, but concentration in Rootstock liquidity, Sovryn governance, and the quality of the underlying BTC-backed stablecoins. Underlying bAssets are themselves {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoins with {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} against rBTC.

xusd-babelfish.title: The Rootstock Stablecoin Basket
xusd-babelfish.text:
A Rootstock basket dollar minted 1:1 from bridged stablecoins — a basket exit route, not a fiat-issuer promise, with recursive bridge and dependency risk.

XUSD is BabelFish's Rootstock basket stablecoin, backed by DLLR plus {{term:bridge}}bridged{{/term}} USDT, USDC, DAI, DOC, and related bAssets, with mint and redeem flowing through a basket-level {{term:psm}}PSM-style{{/term}} module. Pharos tracks live branch balances directly from the basket holder and links the largest dependency back to the newly tracked DLLR entry. The model is useful but recursive: XUSD inherits the risks of Rootstock {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} liquidity, DLLR's own basket, and BabelFish's balancing fees. It is a basket exit route, not a fiat issuer promise.

susdd-tron-dao-reserve.title: Savings USDD Wrapper
susdd-tron-dao-reserve.text: an ERC-4626 savings passthrough over USDD whose ultimate peg exit still flows through USDD's own PSM and reserve stack. sUSDD brings USDD into the {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper set as an ERC-4626 style savings token on Ethereum and BNB Chain. The useful distinction is that the wrapper can be proven on-chain while ultimate reserve risk still follows USDD itself, so Pharos models it as a savings passthrough rather than a fresh reserve stack, with final {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} routed through USDD's {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}}.

onyc-onre.title: Reinsurance NAV Token
onyc-onre.text: Solana yield token tied to OnRe-managed structured insurance and reinsurance positions; queued, high-touch design with transparency links but no score-grade composition adapter yet. ONYC expands Pharos coverage into a small but distinct RWA/NAV design: a Solana {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} token tied to OnRe underwriting and collateral returns rather than a simple fiat cash reserve. The entry treats the product as high-touch and queued, with transparency links but no score-grade composition adapter yet.

apyusd-apyx.title: Apyx Savings Share
apyusd-apyx.text: apyUSD is the ERC-4626 {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper of apxUSD, capturing dividends and preferred-equity yield from Apyx's Digital Asset Treasury collateral. apyUSD is the value-accruing wrapper over apxUSD, whose collateral base is unusual: preferred equity and a {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} buffer rather than standard cash-only reserves. Pharos tracks the wrapper with ERC-4626 reserve proof and keeps the underlying Apyx collateral risk visible through the parent dependency.

susd1plus-lorenzo.title: Lorenzo Strategy Dollar
susd1plus-lorenzo.text: Lorenzo's staked receipt over the USD1+ strategy dollar, blending WLFI USD1 reserve yield with delta-neutral CEX strategies on BNB Chain. sUSD1+ adds Lorenzo Protocol exposure to the USD1-linked strategy-dollar family. The wrapper is {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}}, with returns sourced from {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} {{term:basis-trade}}basis trade{{/term}} positions and CEX strategy access driven by {{term:funding-rate}}funding rate{{/term}} dynamics. Public data supports metadata and supply tracking, but the reserve and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanics are less transparent than the cleaner ERC-4626 wrappers, so the entry carries exotic collateral and CEX-strategy {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} risk.

savusd-avant.title: Avant Staked Dollar
savusd-avant.text:
A short-cooldown staked wrapper of avUSD that compounds delta-neutral strategy yield while inheriting the parent's USDC redemption path.

savUSD is the staked, {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-accruing{{/term}} form of Avant USD. The dashboard models it as a wrapper on avUSD with a short cooldown, preserving the parent {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} strategy risk while separately tracking the savings-token supply and contract footprint, and exits inherit avUSD's USDC {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path.

steakusdc-steakhouse.title: Prime Instant USDC
steakusdc-steakhouse.text: a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} Morpho ERC-4626 vault share over USDC, priced by borrower interest rather than by Circle reserves. Steakhouse USDC is a Morpho Prime Instant vault share over USDC, making it a DeFi lending wrapper rather than a new fiat issuer. Pharos uses ERC-4626 proof to validate the vault asset and classifies the risk around lending liquidity rather than around Circle reserve quality alone.

srusde-strata.title: Senior Ethena Tranche
srusde-strata.text:
Strata's senior tranche over a USDe yield strategy with junior capital absorbing first-loss; better structured than a plain loop, but still Ethena-dependent.

Strata Senior USDe turns Ethena exposure into a senior tranche with junior capital absorbing first-loss risk via {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} hedges. Pharos models the token as a risk-absorption variant of USDe: better structured than a plain loop, but still dependent on Ethena, sUSDe yield, and Strata {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} terms.

syzusd-yuzu.title: Yuzu Staked Wrapper
syzusd-yuzu.text: Yuzu's staked wrapper over yzUSD, carrying the same strategy exposure onto newer chains without double-counting parent risk. syzUSD is the staked wrapper for Yuzu USD, carrying the {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} exposure of the Yuzu system onto newer chains. The tracked entry separates wrapper-level identity from the parent Accountable reserve feed so aggregate supply can be monitored without double-counting the underlying risk, while {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} still flows through the Yuzu primary path.

fxsave-f-x-protocol.title: f(x) Stability Vault
fxsave-f-x-protocol.text: fxSAVE is a {{term:yield-bearing}}value-accruing{{/term}} vault share over f(x) Protocol's Stability Pool, inheriting fxUSD {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} collateral risk on WBTC and wstETH. fxSAVE packages f(x) Protocol Stability Pool exposure into a value-accruing vault share. It is not a plain fxUSD balance: the reserve path runs through fxSP, so Pharos treats it as a high-risk strategy vault while keeping the fxUSD parent dependency and {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} requirements explicit.

steakusdt-steakhouse.title: Prime Instant USDT
steakusdt-steakhouse.text: the USDT-denominated twin of steakUSDC, accruing Morpho lending interest while inheriting Tether issuer risk underneath. Steakhouse USDT mirrors the Steakhouse USDC setup on top of USDT: an ERC-4626 Morpho lending vault with NAV appreciation and liquidity-dependent {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} capacity. The entry gives Pharos separate visibility into the vault while preserving the Tether dependency.

susn-noon.title: Noon Savings Share
susn-noon.text: sUSN is Noon's staking wrapper of USN — NAV appreciates from a {{term:rwa}}private-credit, CLO, DeFi-lending, and T-bill mix{{/term}} layered with {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} CEX strategies, but final {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} still inherits Noon whitelisting and USN reserve constraints. sUSN is the staked savings form of Noon USN. The token is useful to track separately because its NAV appreciates and its supply can diverge from liquid USN, while final redemption still inherits Noon whitelisting and USN reserve constraints.

mre7yield-midas.title: Midas Re7 Yield Token
mre7yield-midas.text: Midas managed-yield product with a public NAV oracle but no granular strategy adapter; a USD-referenced NAV token with exotic strategy risk, not a cash-backed dollar issuer. mRe7YIELD adds a Midas managed-yield product with a public NAV oracle but without a granular strategy-composition adapter. Pharos treats it as a USD-referenced NAV token with exotic {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-adjacent strategy risk, not as a cash-backed dollar issuer.

hbusdt-hyperbeat.title: Hyperbeat USDT Vault
hbusdt-hyperbeat.text: USDT0 vault wrapper on HyperEVM; ultimate fiat par exit still routes through Tether. hbUSDT is a HyperEVM vault share built around USDT0, USDe, USR, and Hyperbeat strategy liquidity. Metadata and contract tracking are ready, but live reserve sync remains intentionally conservative until a product-scoped Hyperbeat adapter can separate hbUSDT from aggregate Accountable data. Treat hbUSDT as a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper whose exit depends on Hyperbeat vault liquidity and an upstream Tether {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} route, with cross-chain settlement riding the USDT0 {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}}.

witry-brix.title: Wrapped Turkish Lira Yield
witry-brix.text: wiTRY is a Brix staking wrapper over iTRY, exposing holders to a BVI-regulated TRY money-market fund and local Turkish-lira instruments. wiTRY brings a TRY-pegged {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper into the catalog. The Ethereum wrapper can be verified on-chain, while the underlying iTRY reserve and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} process remain more issuer-dependent than the mature fiat stablecoin set. The underlying iTRY exposure points at a BVI-regulated TRY money-market structure and local-currency instruments, which Pharos treats as {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} collateral with high jurisdictional and operational risk for a thinly traded TRY product.

srusd-reservoir.title: Reservoir Savings Token
srusd-reservoir.text:
Reservoir savings exposure tracked directly rather than via the wrapped wsrUSD; the reserve stack is diversified lending and RWA exposure, not a single cash account.

srUSD tracks Reservoir savings exposure directly instead of only through the wrapped wsrUSD token. The protocol has a live reserve endpoint and a documented savings path, but the reserve stack is diversified lending and {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} exposure rather than a single cash account, making srUSD a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} share over a mixed credit book.

usdn-smardex.title: Delta-Neutral USDN
usdn-smardex.text: SMARDEX USDN is an Ethereum {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} synthetic dollar backed by a wstETH-centered {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} vault, unrelated to Noble USDN or Neutrino USDN. SMARDEX USDN is unrelated to Noble USDN and the old Neutrino USDN. It is an Ethereum synthetic dollar backed by the USDN vault and wstETH-centered {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} mechanics, with rebasing yield and protocol-state {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} constraints.

scusd-rings.title: Rings Stable Collateral
scusd-rings.text:
A Sonic/Ethereum stablecoin backed by stablecoin collateral plus Veda DeFi strategy exposure; the liquid token isn't the main yield wrapper.

Rings scUSD adds Sonic/Ethereum scAsset coverage with Veda-backed strategy exposure. The liquid token is not the main {{term:yield-bearing}}yield wrapper{{/term}}, so Pharos treats it as a stablecoin backed by stablecoin collateral plus DeFi strategy risk rather than as a savings token.

weusd-picwe.title: PicWe USDC Wrapper
weusd-picwe.text: WEUSD is tracked under PicWe (not WEMIX) as a USDC wrapper minted and redeemed 1:1 against USDC, currently trading off-peg near $0.91 despite the documented backing. WEUSD is tracked under PicWe, not WEMIX, because the current documentation and contracts describe PicWe WEUSD. The reserve model is simple today — USDC backing with on-chain {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} rails — while future {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}/yield collateral stays outside the current scoring assumptions. The off-peg pricing despite documented backing suggests the cross-chain arbitrage loop is not closing efficiently.

gbpe-monerium.title: GBP E-Money Rail
gbpe-monerium.text: GBPe is Monerium's licensed-EMI British pound e-money, with {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} through regulated bank-transfer rails on permitted EMI reserve assets. Monerium GBPe extends the Monerium e-money model to British pounds across several EVM chains. Pharos uses the official Monerium token API addresses where they diverge from older CoinGecko metadata and treats redemption as regulated bank-transfer e-money rails backed by safeguarded GBP funds in regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}.

qcad-stablecorp.title: Regulated CAD Stablecoin
qcad-stablecorp.text:
A small but properly regulated Canadian-dollar stablecoin under VRCA and FINTRAC, with a live reserve feed and issuer API.

Stablecorp QCAD adds a live Canadian-dollar reserve feed with official supply and fiat reserve totals. The product is small, but the Canadian VRCA framework, FINTRAC registration, and issuer API make it a useful non-USD fiat stablecoin to track. Pharos surfaces the curated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path and reserve composition while leaving room for stronger {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} coverage as Stablecorp publishes more frequent updates.

usdxl-last.title: Position-backed synthetic dollar on Hyperliquid
usdxl-last.text: Last USD (USDXL) is a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style synthetic dollar minted on HypurrFi (Aave V3 fork on HyperEVM), drawn against HYPE, HYPE LSTs, UBTC, and ETH collateral with {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} as the only peg defense. Last USD (USDXL) is a crypto-collateralized synthetic dollar minted on HypurrFi, an Aave V3 fork on HyperEVM operated by Last. Users open {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} borrowing positions against HYPE, HYPE LSTs, bridged BTC (UBTC), and ETH, then draw USDXL against that collateral — closer to a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} than to a 1:1 reserve-backed dollar. Repaying the loan burns the synthetic, and undercollateralized positions are hit with {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} to defend the peg. Circulating supply sits in the low single-digit millions, with the asset {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}}d between Hyperliquid's HyperEVM (18 decimals) and Hyperliquid L1 spot (8 decimals).

bnusd-balanced.title: Balanced's CDP stablecoin extending ICON DeFi cross-chain
bnusd-balanced.text: bnUSD is Balanced's decentralized dollar stablecoin on ICON, minted from {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} {{term:cdp}}CDPs{{/term}} against sICX and bridged cross-chain via xCall. BNUSD is the overcollateralized stablecoin of Balanced, a Cosmos/ICON-native lending and DEX protocol. Holders borrow it against sICX (staked ICX) and other Hub collateral on ICON for a 0.2% origination fee plus 2% annualized interest, and the same supply circulates wrapper-free across connected EVM chains and Injective via Balanced's xCall messaging layer. Adding BNUSD gives Pharos coverage of the ICON/Cosmos stablecoin niche — a small but durable ecosystem that no other tracked asset represents — and exposes the cross-chain Hub-issuance pattern as a category. The asset is sub-$5M and currently mid-migration to a v2 design re-anchored on Sonic, so supply and the canonical issuance chain are expected to evolve.

dusd-fluid.title: Banked-cash backing, smart-contract enforced
dusd-fluid.text: DUSD is Fluid Finance's banked-cash USD stablecoin on Arbitrum; self-reported oracle caps mint to safeguarded bank balance. Fluid Finance SA's DigitalDollar is the rare USD stablecoin that holds the float in literal client-safeguarded bank cash — not {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}}, not commercial paper — at regulated European banks, with theft and fraud cover from Lloyd's of London. The differentiator is the smart-contract verifiedOffchainAssetBalance: an oracle publishes the bank balance to Arbitrum, and the contract refuses to mint DUSD beyond that ceiling. It is the only tracked DUSD that is a single-chain fiat coin, deployed only on Arbitrum at modest ~$3M supply with about 1,000 holders. The structural trade-off is that 'verifiable 24/7' is still self-reported via the issuer's oracle, not an independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, and Fluid Finance SA remains a single Swiss entity rather than a regulated bank. {{term:custody}}Custody{{/term}} sits at regulated European banks and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} burns DUSD on-chain against an IBAN credit.

iusd-initia.title: Initia's AUSD-wrapped ecosystem dollar
iusd-initia.text: Single-chain Initia wrapper of bridged Agora AUSD; reserve yield diverted to ecosystem incentives, redemption routes back through AUSD. iUSD is the native dollar on Initia, the new Move-based Cosmos L1. Each iUSD is backed 1:1 by Agora's AUSD bridged in via LayerZero, so the ultimate reserve trace is Agora's short-dated U.S. Treasuries, repos, and cash custodied at State Street under VanEck management. Unlike standard fiat-backed stables, the reserve yield is redirected by Initia into ecosystem incentives — Echelon lending, liquidity programs, and Cabal vaults — rather than paid to holders. Supply is small (~$4M) and the chain is brand new, so resilience scoring leans on AUSD's transparency rather than an Initia-issued attestation. Holder redemption ultimately routes back through the LayerZero bridge to Agora's USD redemption window. Reserve trace runs into AUSD's {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} and cash at State Street with VanEck-managed {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, with the {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} layer and Agora's {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} window owning the exit path.

usdcx-movement.title: Movement's native USDC-backed dollar
usdcx-movement.text: USDCx is Movement's USDC-backed dollar issued via Circle's xReserve smart contract, with CCTP/Gateway {{term:bridge}}bridging{{/term}} to and from USDC across 30+ chains -- partner-issued plumbing, not direct Circle paper. USDCx is Movement Network's native dollar stablecoin, launched on M1 mainnet in March 2026 through Circle's xReserve infrastructure. Each USDCx is backed 1:1 by Circle USDC held in a Circle-deployed xReserve smart contract on Movement, and can be moved to USDC across 30+ chains via CCTP and Gateway without third-party {{term:bridge}}bridges{{/term}}. The issuer is Move Industries, the team behind Movement, rather than Circle directly -- making USDCx a partner-issued stablecoin whose ultimate solvency inherits from USDC's regulated reserves and Circle {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. Circulating supply is still modest (~$2.8M), positioning USDCx as ecosystem rails for Movement-native DeFi, neobank partners like KAST, and Global South payment corridors.

usdh-hubble.title: Solana's original crypto-backed CDP stablecoin, now dormant
usdh-hubble.text: Hubble's USDH was Solana's first MakerDAO-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin at 150% min collateral; today it circulates at ~$1.2-1.5M and is structurally dormant. Hubble Protocol's USDH was the first MakerDAO-style {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} stablecoin on Solana, minted against a basket of SOL, mSOL, BTC, and ETH at a minimum 150% collateralization ratio with Stability Pool {{term:liquidation}}liquidations{{/term}}. The protocol launched in 2022, raised $5M from Three Arrows, Crypto.com and others, and originally aspired to challenge centralized stablecoin dominance on Solana. Today USDH circulates at roughly $1.2-1.5M with negligible secondary volume, and the team has pivoted its development energy to sister protocol Kamino Finance. No formal sunset has been announced and the borrow app remains live, but USDH is structurally dormant rather than growing. The 'USDH' symbol is shared with Native Markets and Hermetica -- three distinct issuers, three distinct collateral models.

zkusd-goal3.title: ZKsync-native sportsbook stablecoin with limited reserve disclosure
zkusd-goal3.text:
A Goal3 sportsbook stable on ZKsync Era, claimed to be overcollateralized but with no itemized backing — treat as venue-restricted credit redeemable through one portal.

zkUSD Dollar is the in-house stable issued by Goal3, a sportsbook on ZKsync Era, with circulating supply just over $1M. Goal3 documents the asset as {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} by assets held in the sportsbook, redeemable 1:1 for USDC through the official portal, but the specific accepted collateral, ratios, and on-chain backing addresses are not publicly itemized. Pharos tracks zkUSD primarily for ZKsync ecosystem coverage rather than scale; users should treat it as venue-restricted credit on a single-chain operator and weight {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} access through the Goal3 Portal as the only modeled exit. Secondary liquidity exists on SyncSwap and a small MEXC listing.

ist-agoric.title: Cosmos-native crypto-backed stable with sub-$5M strategic coverage
ist-agoric.text: Agoric's overcollateralized dollar minted from IBC ATOM/stATOM vaults with a PSM for 1:1 IBC stablecoin swaps; tiny strategic Cosmos coverage. Inter Stable Token (IST) is the Agoric platform's native fee token and an overcollateralized crypto-backed stablecoin governed via Inter Protocol. IST is minted two ways: through vault positions collateralized by IBC-bridged ATOM and stATOM with a stability fee and Dutch-auction liquidations, and through a Parity Stability Module (PSM) that swaps approved IBC stablecoins (USDC, USDT, DAI) for IST 1:1. Total circulating supply is ~$1.4M across Agoric native, Osmosis, Archway, and Secret Network deployments — well below Pharos's $5M soft threshold, but tracked as a strategic Cosmos-ecosystem entry where overcollateralized fiat-pegged designs remain rare. Pharos uses DefiLlama as the primary supply feed; coverage today reflects the Osmosis IBC slice only until upstream tracking broadens to Agoric native. The design is a textbook {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} with {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}}, Dutch-auction {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}}, and an IBC-stablecoin {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} as the peg backstop.

benji-franklin-templeton.title: The Onchain '40 Act Money Market Fund
benji-franklin-templeton.text: BENJI is the on-chain share token for Franklin Templeton's FOBXX, an SEC-registered U.S. government {{term:money-market-fund}}money market fund{{/term}} with a stable $1.00 NAV. BENJI is Franklin Templeton's tokenised share class of FOBXX, the Franklin OnChain U.S. Government Money Fund — a Securities Act of 1933 and Investment Company Act of 1940 registered money market fund custodied at BNY Mellon. The token holds a stable $1.00 NAV; yield is distributed by rebasing the holder's share count on-chain rather than letting the price drift, which makes BENJI behave like a par-redeemable dollar even though it is legally a fund share. With roughly $2 billion in assets across Stellar (primary), Polygon, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Aptos, Base, Solana, BNB Chain, Canton, and Ethereum, it is the largest tokenised '40 Act {{term:money-market-fund}}MMF{{/term}} in market. Pharos currently tracks the Ethereum supply contract and runs reserves on a curated weekly snapshot of the official Franklin Templeton factsheet pending per-chain verification and oracle availability.

wtgxx-wisdomtree.title: WisdomTree's 24/7 Dealer-Traded Treasury Fund
wtgxx-wisdomtree.text:
A SEC-approved tokenized government MMF trading at a fixed $1 NAV 24/7 through WisdomTree Connect dealers, with $857M across seven chains.

WTGXX is the digital share class of WisdomTree's Government Money Market Digital Fund, a '40 Act-registered {{term:money-market-fund}}money market fund{{/term}} that received SEC approval in early 2026 to support 24/7 dealer trading at a fixed $1.00 NAV — making it one of the most stable-coin-like tokenised MMFs in market. Subscriptions and {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}} are gated to WisdomTree Connect users with USDC dealer settlement and USD-wire alternatives; holdings are short-duration U.S. government obligations ({{term:treasury}}Treasury bills{{/term}}), repos, and cash as the {{term:rwa}}real-world asset{{/term}} backing. Around $857 million of AUM sits across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Avalanche, Base, Optimism, Plume, and Stellar; Pharos tracks the Ethereum supply contract first and runs a curated weekly snapshot of the official WisdomTree fund factsheet for reserves.

vbill-vaneck.title: VanEck's Securitize-Administered Treasury Share
vbill-vaneck.text: VBILL is VanEck's on-chain {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} fund share advised by Van Eck Associates and administered by Securitize on Ethereum, with Wormhole bridges to Avalanche, BNB Chain, and Solana. VBILL is the on-chain share token of the VanEck {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} Fund, a BVI Professional Fund advised by Van Eck Associates and administered by Securitize on Ethereum with bridged Wormhole deployments on Avalanche, BNB Chain, and Solana. The token is NAV-accreting (price drifts upward with T-bill yield) and {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} rather than rebasing; subscription minimums of $100k/$1M apply by chain and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} settles through Securitize Markets against USDC, AUSD, or USD wire. Backed by {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} collateral with institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} cadence appropriate for a regulated {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}}-adjacent structure. A Chainlink NAVLink oracle publishes daily NAV for Aave Horizon and other integrations; Pharos tracks the Ethereum supply contract with a curated reserves snapshot pending oracle wiring.

acred-apollo-securitize.title: Private Credit, Not Treasuries
acred-apollo-securitize.text: ACRED is a tokenized, NAV-accreting feeder share into Apollo's diversified private credit fund — backing is illiquid private credit, not T-bills, so the risk profile is medium-to-high rather than cash-like. ACRED is the on-chain feeder share into Apollo Diversified Credit Fund, a multi-strategy private credit portfolio combining direct lending, structured credit, performing credit, and dislocated credit. Unlike BUIDL or BENJI, the collateral is illiquid private credit rather than {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} — risk profile is medium-to-high and closer to syrupUSDC than to a stable-NAV vehicle. ACRED is NAV-accreting; primary {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is monthly at fund NAV through Securitize Markets, supplemented by an on-demand liquidity pool sized to roughly 5% of NAV, and RedStone publishes a NAV oracle used by integrations. Pharos tracks the Ethereum supply contract and flags this asset as a private-credit NAV token rather than a par stablecoin.

eutbl-spiko.title: Europe's First Tokenised T-Bill MMF
eutbl-spiko.text: EUTBL is Spiko's AMF-regulated UCITS short-term {{term:money-market-fund}}MMF{{/term}} backed by Eurozone {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} — Europe's first tokenized {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} sovereign fund. EUTBL is Spiko's EUR-denominated short-term money market fund — the first AMF-regulated UCITS MMF tokenised on Ethereum. The fund holds short-dated Eurozone sovereign T-bills with weighted average maturity under two months, and EUTBL behaves as a VNAV (variable-NAV) share that accretes value as T-bill yield compounds. Primary subscriptions and redemptions settle same-day at fund NAV with a €1k minimum; Chainlink CCIP bridges issuance to Arbitrum and Polygon. EUTBL is one of Pharos's few EUR-pegged RWA assets and one of the cleanest fits for European institutional users seeking regulatory-grade tokenised cash.

ustbl-spiko.title: Spiko's USD T-Bill MMF Cousin
ustbl-spiko.text: USTBL is Spiko's USD-denominated AMF-regulated UCITS {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} holding short-dated U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills, deployed across Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Polygon via Chainlink CCIP. USTBL is the USD-denominated sister fund to Spiko's EUTBL — same AMF-regulated UCITS {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} architecture, same ERC-1967 upgradeable proxy, same Chainlink CCIP multi-chain rollout (Ethereum, Arbitrum, Polygon), but holding short-dated U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills instead of Eurozone sovereigns. The VNAV share accretes value as T-bill yield compounds, with $1k minimums and same-day NAV settlement. Backed by {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} collateral with institutional {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and AMF {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, USTBL behaves as a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} share rather than a par stablecoin. The combined Spiko AUM passed $1 billion in late 2025, making the pair one of the larger EU-regulated tokenised treasury franchises in market.

jtrsy-anemoy.title: S&P's Highest-Rated Tokenised Fund
jtrsy-anemoy.text: BVI Professional Fund holding short-duration U.S. T-bills via Centrifuge ERC-7540; AA+f / S1+ S&P rating, NAV settlement for whitelisted professionals. JTRSY is the Janus Henderson Anemoy Treasury Fund, a BVI Professional Fund where Janus Henderson acts as sub-advisor and Centrifuge handles the on-chain ERC-7540 vault. The fund is rated AA+f / S1+ by S&P, currently the highest credit rating assigned to any tokenised fund. Holdings are short-duration U.S. T-bills; primary subscriptions and redemptions settle same-day at fund NAV for whitelisted non-U.S. Professional Investors via Centrifuge's issuer rail. Distribution extends across Centrifuge V3 to additional chains; Pharos tracks the Ethereum supply contract first with a curated snapshot until the Centrifuge on-chain NAV publishing path is wired into the live reserves adapter. Holdings are pure short-duration {{term:treasury}}U.S. T-bills{{/term}} held as a tokenized {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} fund share with permissioned Centrifuge {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and same-day NAV {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}.

bib01-backed.title: Backed's Flagship Treasury Tracker
bib01-backed.text: bIB01 is Backed's NAV-accreting tracker token for the BlackRock iShares 0-1 year U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury Bond{{/term}} UCITS ETF, KYC-gated under Swiss DLT Act framework — not pegged to $1. bIB01 is Backed Finance's most-traded tokenised {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} ETF: a Swiss DLT Act-registered tracker certificate that fully backs each token with the BlackRock iShares $ Treasury Bond 0-1yr UCITS ETF (IB01). The token is NAV-accreting and not pegged to $1 — price drifts upward continuously as the underlying T-bill ETF accrues yield. Primary mint and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} are KYC-gated through Backed; secondary liquidity is on Uniswap and CoW Protocol. bIB01 deploys on Ethereum, Base, BNB Chain, Polygon, Arbitrum, Gnosis, and Avalanche using the same contract address pattern that Backed uses across its product line.

bc3m-backed.title: Backed's EUR Govt Bond Tracker
bc3m-backed.text: bC3M is Backed's NAV-accreting tracker token for Amundi's short-dated Eurozone government bond UCITS ETF, KYC-gated and registered under Swiss DLT Act — one of the few EUR-pegged {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} tokens. bC3M is Backed Finance's EUR-denominated tokenised tracker certificate fully backed by the AMUNDI GOVIES 0-6 Months Euro Investment Grade UCITS ETF. The token is NAV-accreting in euros, giving Pharos one of the few EUR-pegged RWA assets backed by short-duration Eurozone government bonds — economically the EUR analogue of a {{term:treasury}}Treasury-bond{{/term}} tracker. Same Swiss DLT Act framework as bIB01, same KYC-gated primary issuance through Backed and KYC-gated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, same Uniswap / CoW secondary liquidity surfaces. Pharos tracks the Ethereum supply contract first; Backed also publishes the asset on Base, BNB Chain, Polygon, and Gnosis using its multi-chain deployment pattern.

ntbill-nest.title: Nest's On-Plume Treasury Vault
ntbill-nest.text: Nest Credit Treasury vault share on Plume routing into Superstate USTB/USCC and Janus Henderson JTRSY; NAV-accreting fund-of-funds-style token, not a par-redeemable dollar. nTBILL is Nest Credit's {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} vault on Plume: a vault share whose value tracks a curated book of Superstate USTB / USCC and Janus Henderson JTRSY positions, plus a small stablecoin liquidity buffer. The token is NAV-accreting and primary mint/{{term:redemption}}redeem{{/term}} runs through Nest at vault NAV. Reserves are sourced live from the Nest Credit positions API, the same adapter used by inALPHA. Pharos tracks nTBILL because it references a dollar base, but the token behaves like a tokenised {{term:money-market-fund}}fund-of-funds{{/term}} share rather than a par-redeemable stablecoin.

nbasis-nest.title: Nest's Basis-Trade Vault
nbasis-nest.text: Nest Credit basis-trade vault token combining tokenized T-bill collateral with perpetual shorts; NAV-accreting rather than $1-pegged, value drifts with funding-rate performance. nBASIS is Nest Credit's {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} strategy vault: tokenised {{term:treasury}}T-bill{{/term}} collateral combined with {{term:perpetual}}perpetual{{/term}} short positions, rebalanced by Nest. Closer in profile to Ethena USDe or Midas mRe7YIELD than to a par stablecoin -- the token's value drifts with {{term:funding-rate}}funding-rate{{/term}} performance rather than holding $1. Pharos lists it because the strategy references the dollar as its base and the Nest Credit positions API publishes live NAV, but the methodology treats nBASIS as a strategy vault with high collateral-quality risk and a NAV-token notice.

nopal-nest.title: Nest's BlackOpal Credit Vault
nopal-nest.text: Nest Credit vault token wrapping BlackOpal LiquidStone II tokenized private-credit positions plus a small liquidity buffer; NAV-accreting vault share, not a par-redeemable stablecoin. nOPAL is Nest Credit's BlackOpal LiquidStone II vault: tokenised private-credit positions plus a small {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} and stablecoin liquidity buffer. Like other Nest vaults, the token is NAV-accreting and primary access runs through Nest at vault NAV. Pharos flags nOPAL as a private-credit vault share rather than a par stablecoin; the high-risk reserve slice reflects the underlying LiquidStone II credit positions classified as {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-adjacent exposure.

nwisdom-nest.title: Nest's WisdomTree-Backed Vault
nwisdom-nest.text: Nest Credit vault share built around WisdomTree Connect tokenized fund exposure (xCRDYX) plus an nTBILL liquidity buffer; NAV-accreting tokenized fund share, not a par stablecoin. nWISDOM is Nest Credit's vault built around WisdomTree's tokenised fund shares (xCRDYX and related WisdomTree Connect products) with a small nTBILL and stablecoin liquidity buffer, classified as {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-adjacent vault exposure. Yield accretes through the underlying WisdomTree fund NAV; primary mint/{{term:redemption}}redeem{{/term}} runs through Nest at vault NAV. Pharos tracks it on the same live reserves pattern as inALPHA, with the understanding that the token is a vault share rather than a par stablecoin.

susdc-spark.title: Spark's USDC share class on the Sky savings rate
susdc-spark.text: an ERC-4626 vault that routes USDC through Spark's PSM into the Sky Savings Rate, with on-chain withdraw bounded by PSM liquidity. Spark Savings USDC (spUSDC) is the ERC-4626 V2 savings vault that gives USDC holders direct exposure to the Sky Savings Rate without first converting to USDS. Deposits are routed through Spark's {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} into Sky's savings module, and the share price appreciates against USDC as {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} yield accrues. The Ethereum vault holds roughly $937M of USDC at the V2 deployment address shared with Avalanche. Rate-setting depends on Sky governance, so spUSDC inherits Sky's centralized-dependent yield-setting risk on top of the underlying USDC issuer surface. {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is on-chain through the vault's withdraw path; final USDC liquidity depends on the PSM buffer.

susdt-spark.title: USDT-denominated Spark Savings vault on the Sky rate
susdt-spark.text: the USDT share class for the Sky Savings Rate, layered over the same Spark PSM and Sky savings module as spUSDC. Spark Savings USDT (spUSDT) is the ERC-4626 V2 savings vault that translates the Sky Savings Rate into a USDT share class. The Ethereum vault holds about $1.19B of USDT and accrues value via the share price; deposits route through Spark's {{term:psm}}PSM{{/term}} into Sky's savings module as a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} position. Holders inherit the USDT issuer surface (Tether), the Spark vault contract risk, and Sky governance's rate-setting authority. {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} is on-chain through standard ERC-4626 withdraw and depends on PSM-level USDT liquidity.

sgho-aave.title: Aave's non-slashable GHO savings module
sgho-aave.text:
Aave's non-slashable GHO yield product — 1:1 deposits, governance-set savings rate, no cooldown — separate from the slashable Umbrella stkGHO safety module.

Aave Savings GHO (sGHO) is the non-slashable GHO {{term:yield-bearing}}yield product{{/term}} offered alongside the slashable Umbrella stkGHO safety module. Depositors mint sGHO against GHO at a 1:1 conversion and receive GHO-denominated emissions at the Aave-governance-set savings rate. The contract holds approximately $267M of GHO and pays out without cooldown or slashing risk; it is distinct from the Umbrella stkGHO position that absorbs deficit events for the GHO market, and underneath sits GHO's own {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} collateral profile. Yield is governance-set, so emissions can move with Aave DAO decisions.

gtusdcp-gauntlet.title: Gauntlet's curated USDC MetaMorpho V2 vault
gtusdcp-gauntlet.text: gtUSDCp is the Gauntlet-curated MetaMorpho V2 USDC vault, an ERC-4626 wrapper compounding {{term:yield-bearing}}lending yield{{/term}} across permissioned Morpho Blue markets on Base and Ethereum. Gauntlet USDC Prime (gtUSDCp) is a MetaMorpho V2 vault on Morpho Blue curated by Gauntlet. The curator allocates USDC across permissioned Morpho markets backed by blue-chip crypto, {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}, and yield-bearing collateral, then keeps the vault's risk parameters live. The largest deployment is on Base ($352M), with a $101M Ethereum V2 deployment; together it ranks as one of the largest curated USDC vaults across MetaMorpho. Share price appreciates against USDC as borrower interest accrues; withdrawals depend on Morpho market liquidity and the curator's allocation discipline.

gtusdc-gauntlet.title: Gauntlet's conservative USDC MetaMorpho vault
gtusdc-gauntlet.text: gtUSDC is a Gauntlet-curated MetaMorpho V1 USDC vault, an ERC-4626 wrapper compounding {{term:yield-bearing}}lending yield{{/term}} across vetted Morpho Blue markets on Ethereum. Gauntlet USDC Prime V1 (gtUSDC) is the Ethereum-only V1 Morpho Prime vault curated by Gauntlet — a $145M MetaMorpho deployment across vetted USDC lending markets on Morpho Blue, distinct from the separately tracked Prime V2 vault (gtusdcp-gauntlet) at a different contract address. Share price appreciates against USDC as borrower interest accrues, with withdrawals dependent on borrower {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} flow and Morpho market depth. Tracking the V1 and V2 vaults as separate entries exists for the same reason Pharos tracks Steakhouse USDC and Steakhouse USDT separately — distinct curated portfolios warrant their own risk telemetry.

yvusdc-yearn.title: Yearn v3's aggregator USDC vault
yvusdc-yearn.text:
Canonical Yearn v3 USDC vault routing through Aave, Compound, Morpho, and Sky; ~$30M Ethereum AUM with queue-based withdrawals and centralized strategy selection.

yvUSDC-1 is the canonical Yearn v3 USDC vault: an ERC-4626 {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} share token whose price appreciates against USDC as Yearn's strategy allocator rotates underlying capital across whitelisted yield strategies (Aave, Compound, Morpho, Sky, and similar). The Ethereum vault holds about $30M of USDC. {{term:redemption}}Withdrawals{{/term}} route through Yearn v3's queue and depend on aggregate strategy liquidity; centralised strategy selection sits with Yearn governance.

aa-falconx-mev-capital.title: Senior tranche on MEV Capital's Falcon USDC strategy
aa-falconx-mev-capital.text: AA_FalconXUSDC is a senior {{term:overcollateralization}}senior tranche{{/term}} of a structured DeFi product — its yield comes from USDC lent into Falcon's USDf strategies, with junior tranches absorbing first losses. AA_FalconXUSDC is the senior (AA) tranche of a Pareto/Idle CDO over an MEV-Capital-curated Morpho vault routed into Falcon Finance's USDf strategies. The Ethereum tranche holds about $76M of USDC and accrues value against USDC as borrower interest flows in; junior tranches absorb losses first, but exit liquidity depends on USDf's mint/burn rails. The peg-like framing only holds while Falcon USDf maintains liquidity — sustained USDf stress can degrade {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} pricing even when the senior class is structurally protected.

vndc-jade-labs.title: Vietnam's most-trafficked VND stablecoin with weak attestation
vndc-jade-labs.text: VNDC is Jade Labs's Vietnamese dong stablecoin redeemable 1:1 via ONUS and VNDC Hub, with self-reported reserves and no independent attestation cadence. VNDC is a Vietnamese dong-pegged stablecoin issued by Jade Labs (the company behind ONUS Finance), the only credible on-chain VND instrument with material market presence. The issuer self-reports 1:1 fiat backing with VND {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} at Vietnamese banking partners and operates mint/redemption flows through those partners and the ONUS app, but no independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} cadence is published and aggregator-reported market cap has historically diverged from observable on-chain Polygon and BSC supply. Pharos lists VNDC across Polygon and BNB Smart Chain at zero decimals (the contracts mint whole-unit VNDC); the issuer's third ONUS-chain deployment is not in scope until that chain is tracked. The detail page carries an explicit attestation warning so users do not infer the reported $50M aggregate as fully verifiable.

mmxn-moneta-digital.title: Mexico's retail-focused MXN stablecoin with self-reported reserves
mmxn-moneta-digital.text: Mexico-issued retail MXN stablecoin with self-reported peso-bank backing and no institutional audit cadence; weaker attestation profile than MXNB-Juno, surfaced as an explicit caveat. Moneta Digital (MMXN) is a Mexican peso-pegged stablecoin issued by Moneta Digital, a Mexico-registered virtual asset entity targeting the US-Mexico remittance corridor and domestic crypto-peso liquidity. MMXN is multi-chain (Ethereum ERC-20, Tron TRC-20, with additional Polygon and BSC deployments per the issuer) and uses ERC20Mintable/Burnable/Pausable patterns that give the issuer discretionary supply control. Reserves are self-disclosed against MXN bank balances; unlike the already-tracked MXNB-Juno (operated under CNBV-licensed IFPE NVIO with formal quarterly {{term:attestation}}attestations{{/term}}), Moneta Digital does not publish an institutional audit cadence. Pharos tracks MMXN at roughly $1.4M circulating with several million USD of daily trading volume, surfacing the weaker-attestation gap as an explicit caveat on the detail page so users understand the comparison with regulated MXN issuers.

hkdr-rd-technologies.title: Missed the First Wave, Still in the Race
hkdr-rd-technologies.text: Pre-launch HKD stablecoin from RD Technologies; in HKMA sandbox but missed the April 2026 first license batch, H2 2026 candidate. HKDR is the HKD stablecoin from RD Technologies, a Hong Kong fintech founded by former HKMA chief executive Norman Chan. Its subsidiary RD InnoTech was in the first July 2024 cohort admitted to the HKMA stablecoin issuer sandbox — testing digital-asset trading rails and cross-border trade payments — and the firm has been positioning for licensing under the Stablecoins Ordinance that took effect August 1 2025. On 2026-04-10 the HKMA gazetted the first batch of stablecoin issuer licences (FRS01 and FRS02) to Anchorpoint and HSBC, with RD InnoTech notably absent from that cohort. RD remains a credible second-wave candidate — a recent Series A2 round and a memorandum of understanding with ZA Bank both point to a serious operational build-out — but the regulatory window has now shifted from binary first-batch outcome to a slower queue. Pharos keeps this entry pre-launch with a launching-soon phase; promote on licence issuance. The eventual product still routes through HKMA-mandated {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}, segregated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, and a regulated {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} window.

brd-volpon.title: Selic-Linked Yield, In a Token
brd-volpon.text: BRD is a pre-launch Brazilian real stablecoin from CF Inovacao, backed by Brazilian {{term:treasury}}Treasury bonds{{/term}} and structured to pass Selic-rate yield back to holders. BRD is a BRL stablecoin announced January 6 2026 by Tony Volpon, a former deputy governor of the Central Bank of Brazil, through his company CF Inovacao. The distinctive structural choice: BRD is backed by Brazilian National Treasury bonds and explicitly designed to pass the Selic-linked yield (currently around 15%) back to holders, rather than retaining it as issuer revenue. That is the same model Crown's BRLV already operates in institutional channels — Crown raised $13.5M from Paradigm in December 2025 — but BRD is positioning as the first to make {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-sharing{{/term}} the primary product framing rather than a niche feature. The competitive set in Brazilian BRL stablecoins is small but real: Transfero BRZ ($185M), BBRL ($51M), BRL1, plus cREAL on Celo. The harder gate is Brazilian regulation: BCB's FX-classification regime took effect February 2 2026 and final Consulta Publica 111 output is still pending, which is why Volpon has not published a launch date alongside the announcement.

krw1-bdacs.title: Korea's First Bank-Backed Won Stablecoin, Stuck in PoC
krw1-bdacs.text: BDACS/Woori KRW PoC on Avalanche with real-time banking-API reserve attestation; commercial gating awaits Korea's Digital Asset Basic Act. KRW1 is BDACS's KRW-backed stablecoin, developed with Woori Bank as the reserve custodian and launched on Avalanche in September 2025 — but in a proof-of-concept phase, not in public circulation. The structural advantages are real: real-time banking-API reserve attestation through Woori, KISA's endorsement of Avalanche for public-sector reliability, and a February 2026 Plume partnership that positions KRW1 as the Korean institutional settlement rail for tokenized RWAs (Plume hosts roughly $645M in tokenized assets). The commercial gating is Korea's still-pending Digital Asset Basic Act framework, where BDACS is explicitly trying to make KRW1 the technical standard. The strategic weakness is distribution — BDACS is a B2B custodian without a consumer app or retail footprint, which makes KRW1 likely to win on the institutional side and lose to bank-led or super-app issuers if Korea's eventual framework favours retail surfaces. Real-time banking-API {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} runs through Woori Bank {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, with KRW1 positioning itself as the settlement rail for Korean institutional {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} flows and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} routed through regulated banking channels.

rusd-revolut.title: The Cyprus Licence Was the Easy Part
rusd-revolut.text:
Pharos opens a placeholder for Revolut's expected USD stablecoin against the announced 'Crypto 2.0' direction; ticker, chain, and reserve model are still unannounced.

RUSD is the placeholder Pharos opens for Revolut's expected USD stablecoin, sister to the already-tracked RGBP. The legal substrate was assembled in 2025: Revolut Digital Assets Europe took a MiCA CASP licence from CySEC on October 23 2025, and Revolut's existing Bank-of-Lithuania EMI provides the e-money-token issuer foundation that MiCA Title IV requires. The Cyprus announcement also unveiled 'Crypto 2.0' with '1:1 conversion between stablecoins and USD' as a flagship feature — close enough to a product tease that EU counsel described a 2026 Revolut stablecoin as plausible. The harder questions are downstream: ticker, chain choice, reserve and {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} disclosure model, {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} mechanics, and how Revolut navigates the UK Bank of England's proposed restrictions on cross-group stablecoin issuance that already constrain RGBP. Pharos opens this entry against the announced USD direction; will trim if Revolut formally names a different first-issued variant.

brl-itau.title: Brazil's Biggest Bank Waits for the Rulebook
brl-itau.text: BRL-ITAU is a pre-launch stablecoin under evaluation by Brazil's largest private bank Itau Unibanco, with peg currency and design pending BCB regulation. Itau Unibanco — Brazil's largest private bank by assets — confirmed in April 2025 that it is evaluating its own stablecoin, with Head of Digital Assets Guto Antunes telling a Sao Paulo industry event the bank is 'always open to understanding whether it makes sense for our clients to have a stablecoin, even one in real, within Itau'. The peg-currency choice (BRL or USD) is explicitly undecided and gated on the final shape of Brazil's regulatory framework via BCB Consulta Publica 111, especially the open self-{{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} question that Antunes flagged as a major design constraint. Itau already participates in the DREX wholesale CBDC pilot, providing distribution-rail experience but also a competing institutional product that may shape final positioning; primary {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} would presumably run through Itau's bank network. Pharos opens the placeholder against BRL as the most likely first launch (Brazil retail base, BRL-denominated franchise) while documenting the USD option in editorial copy; retire/migrate if Itau formally names a USD-first variant.

usd-nubank.title: Stablecoins Strapped to the Credit Card
usd-nubank.text: a pre-launch Nubank dollar pilot anchored to credit-card rails, with own-issuance vs. third-party-integration still unresolved. Nubank's stablecoin pilot is structurally interesting because the entry point is not a wallet or a remittance corridor but the credit card. Vice-chair Roberto Campos Neto -- Brazil's central bank governor through 2024 -- announced at Meridian 2025 that Nubank would test dollar-pegged stablecoin payments on credit-card rails, framed inside a larger plan to tokenize deposits and issue credit against tokenized assets. Nubank already integrated USDC inside its app in 2023 and has 100M-plus customers across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia, which is the actual asset here: distribution. The unresolved product question is whether Nubank issues its own dollar stablecoin or routes through an existing one; Campos Neto's framing leaves both open, including the {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} architecture. Pharos opens the placeholder against the own-issuance interpretation; the entry will be retired if the pilot resolves as a USDC/PYUSD integration rather than a new Nubank-issued token.

moveusd-cfx.title: CFX's Solana Deposit Dollar
moveusd-cfx.text: CFX-issued tokenized-deposit dollar on Solana, ~$120M circulating against USD deposits, cash equivalents, and U.S. Treasuries; no independent reserve feed wired yet. MoveUSD is the largest clean coverage addition in this batch, with DefiLlama reporting roughly $120M in circulating supply and a live Solana price path. The token is best read as a CFX-issued dollar settlement instrument rather than a permissionless DeFi-native stablecoin: minting and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} run through the issuer, while the SPL mint gives Pharos a concrete on-chain supply anchor. Reserves are described as USD deposits, cash equivalents, and marketable U.S. {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} securities, but no independently audited reserve feed is wired into Pharos yet. The detail page carries a tokenized-deposit caveat so users do not confuse the high market cap with open retail redemption coverage.

hlusd-hela.title: HeLa's Native Runtime Dollar
hlusd-hela.text: Centralized USD stablecoin for the HeLa chain; CoinGecko-only coverage, no contract-level reserve telemetry yet. HLUSD is the native dollar stablecoin for the HeLa ecosystem, admitted through CoinGecko because the HeLa chain is not yet a supported Pharos contract platform. CoinGecko reports a positive price and market cap, which is enough for runtime coverage, but contract-level supply and issuer reserve telemetry remain outside the current model. The asset is therefore classified as a centralized-dependent RWA-backed USD coin with an explicit unsupported-chain notice. The unusually high trading volume relative to supply makes it useful coverage, but also a candidate for follow-up once HeLa chain support or better reserve documentation exists. Until the issuer publishes a verifiable {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} and discloses {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path remains the dominant unknown.

xmd-metal-dollar.title: A Stablecoin Basket on XPR Network
xmd-metal-dollar.text:
Metallicus's basket dollar wraps USDC, PYUSD, and Paxos-dollar exposure on XPR Network — convenient as an index, hard to verify outside CoinGecko.

Metal Dollar is a basket-backed dollar token on XPR Network, with public materials pointing to USDC, PYUSD, and Paxos-dollar components as the reserve set held in issuer {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}. Pharos admits it through CoinGecko's price and market-cap path because XPR Network is not currently supported for contract coverage. The structure gives XMD upstream exposure to centralized stablecoin issuers while leaving direct holder-control semantics hard to verify from Pharos' chain set, and no public {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} feed itemizes the basket weights. It is a useful basket-stablecoin addition, but reserve composition and redemption depth should be reviewed again before any dependency weights are made more granular.

vusd-virtue.title: IOTA-Backed CDP Dollar
vusd-virtue.text: Virtue USD is an IOTA-ecosystem {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin backed by IOTA and stIOTA positions, with high-risk collateral and IOTA not yet a Pharos-supported chain. Virtue USD is an {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} IOTA ecosystem stablecoin backed by IOTA and stIOTA positions, with {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} mechanics and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} as peg defense. CoinGecko resolves the IOTA object and reports a positive market cap, but IOTA itself is not yet a Pharos-supported chain, so the registry intentionally excludes contracts for now. That means Pharos can show price, market-cap, and risk metadata, while on-chain supply, mint/burn, and contract authority analysis remain future work. The collateral profile is high-risk compared with fiat-backed stablecoins because peg defense ultimately depends on volatile IOTA-family collateral and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} mechanics.

stusd-stoneyield.title: A Yield Wrapper Wearing a Dollar Label
stusd-stoneyield.text: a BNB Chain {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} wrapper over USDC routed through Venus-linked strategies, tracked as a managed NAV product. StoneYield USD is tracked as a BNB Chain yield-bearing stable wrapper, not as a plain fiat dollar. The BSC contract is verified through CoinGecko and the reserve model points to USDC and yield-bearing USDC strategy positions routed through StoneYield's managed protocol layer. That makes the token's stability depend on stablecoin collateral plus strategy execution and withdrawal liquidity, so Pharos marks it as both yield-bearing and a NAV token. Runtime price and market cap are available, but yield telemetry is currently static metadata rather than an integrated pool adapter.

lvusd-leverup.title: Monad Perps Collateral in Stablecoin Form
lvusd-leverup.text: Small Monad-based stable asset tied to LeverUp's perpetuals engine, not a cash-backed issuer dollar; redemption and reserve depth depend on a trading system rather than a bank balance sheet. LeverUp USD is a small Monad stablecoin tied to LeverUp's liquidity layer for perpetuals and margin trading. CoinGecko reports a live price and market cap, and the Monad contract is included because Pharos already has a Monad chain entry. The risk profile is not comparable to a cash-backed issuer coin: collateral and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} are tied to a trading engine that references USDC and MON, and public reserve depth is still thin. Pharos therefore treats lvUSD as a notice-heavy crypto-backed stable asset rather than a conventional dollar reserve token.

nusd-nexus.title: Legacy Synapse Bridge Liquidity
nusd-nexus.text: Legacy Synapse bridge-liquidity stable asset backed by a DAI/USDC/USDT pool; closer to bridge routing infrastructure than a standalone modern issuer, with inherited freezability and dependency risk. Nexus USD is a legacy Synapse {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}}-liquidity stable asset backed by a pool of DAI, USDC, and USDT. It is included because DefiLlama still returns both a current price and circulating supply, but the product model is closer to bridge routing infrastructure than to a standalone modern issuer. The upstream reserve basket gives NUSD inherited freezability and stablecoin dependency risk. Contract coverage is intentionally omitted until the active Synapse deployment set is freshly verified across chains.

brlm-mento.title: Mento's Brazilian Real Rail
brlm-mento.text: BRLm is Mento's oracle-priced Brazilian real on Celo, exchanged through FPMM swap routes against the diversified {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} Mento reserve mix. BRLm expands Mento coverage into Brazilian real-denominated settlement on Celo. Unlike the existing Mento {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} rows, this entry uses the reserve-wide Mento dashboard feed because the current CDP trove API only covers GBPm, JPYm, and CHFm. The reserve mix is diversified but still exposed to sUSDS, CELO, EURC, USDC, USDT, axlEUROC, stETH, and smaller assets, so Pharos classifies collateral quality as mixed rather than fiat-reserve grade. BRLm is small in absolute supply, but strategically useful because it adds another BRL rail from an already-modeled issuer family.

phpm-mento.title: PUSO Joins the PHP Set
phpm-mento.text:
Mento's Celo-native Philippine peso stablecoin uses the shared Mento reserve basket rather than PHP bank deposits, completing Pharos's regional PHP coverage.

PHPm, marketed by Mento as PUSO, is a Celo-based Philippine peso stablecoin with live DefiLlama price and circulating-supply coverage. It uses Mento's oracle-priced swap and reserve architecture rather than a bank-deposit PHP reserve, so the collateral stack is the same mixed Mento reserve basket used across the reserve-backed Mento family. Pharos already tracks other PHP-pegged issuers, making PHPm useful as an ecosystem-completion and regional-coverage addition. The live reserve feed is shared with the broader Mento reserve dashboard rather than a PHPm-specific {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}.

kesm-mento.title: First Kenyan Shilling Stablecoin Coverage
kesm-mento.text: First Kenyan shilling stable in Pharos; runs on Celo via Mento's reserve-backed FX mechanism, OTHER-tagged until KES becomes a first-class peg. KESm is the first Kenyan shilling-denominated stable asset in Pharos, admitted through DefiLlama's price and circulating-supply path. The token runs on Celo and uses the same Mento reserve-backed FX mechanism as the newer Mento local-currency suite. Because KES is not yet a first-class Pharos peg currency, the asset is grouped under OTHER until a broader peg-infrastructure update is justified. The reserve risk remains driven by the Mento mix, especially CELO exposure and upstream centralized stablecoins. Mechanically KESm is a {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}-style Mento FX stablecoin with {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} against the multi-asset reserve and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} via FPMM swaps at oracle-driven rates.

copm-mento.title: Colombian Peso Coverage via Celo
copm-mento.text: COPm is Mento's oracle-priced Colombian peso stablecoin on Celo; first COP reference on Pharos. COPm adds Colombian peso stablecoin coverage through Mento's Celo deployment. DefiLlama supplies the runtime price and circulating value, while the contract is verified from the Celo token-contract table. Pharos maps COP to OTHER for now because the peg enum does not yet include Colombian peso support. The addition is intentionally small-cap but strategically useful because it gives the dashboard a first COP reference before deciding whether a full COP peg tranche is worth building. The reserve relies on {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} across a mixed crypto and stablecoin basket and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through Mento reserve swaps.

cadm-mento.title: A Tiny CAD Rail from Mento
cadm-mento.text: CADm is Mento's oracle-priced CAD stablecoin on Celo, backed by the shared Mento reserve rather than Canadian bank reserves. CADm is Mento's Canadian dollar stable asset on Celo, added mainly for ecosystem completion rather than market size. It passes the DefiLlama runtime gate and uses a verified Celo contract, but circulating supply remains tiny compared with larger CAD stablecoin issuers already tracked by Pharos. The collateral story is Mento reserve exposure rather than Canadian-dollar bank reserves. That means resilience depends on Celo, Mento governance, and the mixed reserve basket behind the broader Mento system. The reserve relies on {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} across a basket of stablecoins and crypto, and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through Mento reserve swaps rather than fiat off-ramps.

audm-mento.title: Mento's AUD Completes Another Local Rail
audm-mento.text: AUDm is Mento's crypto-backed Australian dollar on Celo, minted by depositing USDm as Liquity-v2-style {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} collateral against the {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} Mento reserve mix. AUDm is the Mento Australian dollar asset on Celo, distinct from the already tracked Macropod AUDM despite the shared ticker style. It is admitted through DefiLlama and a verified Celo contract, with live reserve visibility through the shared Mento dashboard. The supply is small, so the value is mainly comparative: users can now see Mento's AUD rail beside larger AUD issuers and the rest of the Mento FX set. Reserves remain mixed and on-chain rather than an Australian-dollar banking stack.

ghsm-mento.title: Ghanaian Cedi Coverage, Grouped as Other
ghsm-mento.text: GHSm is Mento's Celo Ghanaian cedi stablecoin backed by a mixed reserve (sUSDS, CELO, EURC, USDC, stETH) — small-supply currency coverage rather than a market signal. GHSm brings Ghanaian cedi exposure into Pharos through Mento's Celo stablecoin suite. DefiLlama provides the runtime price and supply path, while CoinGecko's active slug resolves as cGHS rather than the stale DefiLlama gecko hint. Like KESm and COPm, GHSm is grouped under OTHER because GHS is not yet a first-class Pharos peg currency. It is very small, but it extends coverage into a currency region otherwise missing from the dashboard, with backing tied to Mento's shared {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} reserve and on-chain {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} flows.

zarm-mento.title: Mento's Smaller ZAR Stablecoin
zarm-mento.text:
Celo-issued ZAR stable from Mento's local-currency program, inheriting reserve risk from the shared Mento mix rather than ZAR bank collateral.

ZARm is a Celo-based South African rand stable asset from Mento minted {{term:cdp}}CDP-style{{/term}} against the Mento Reserve mix. Pharos already tracks a larger ZAR issuer, so ZARm is mainly an ecosystem-completion row that lets users compare Mento's local-currency model across regions. The token passes the DefiLlama price and supply gate and uses the verified Celo contract. Reserve quality is inherited from the shared Mento reserve mix rather than from rand-denominated bank collateral, so {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} risk is on the Mento basket, not the South African banking system.

wbrl-ripio.title: Ripio's Wrapped Brazilian Real
wbrl-ripio.text: WBRL is Ripio's wrapped Brazilian real stablecoin across six EVM chains — a second BRL rail from a Latin American issuer, with reserve transparency as the weak point. WBRL is part of Ripio's wFIAT suite: local-currency stablecoins issued across Ethereum, Base, World Chain, BNB Chain, Polygon, and Gnosis. It passes DefiLlama's price and circulating-supply gate and gives Pharos a second BRL rail from a Latin American issuer, alongside larger BRL assets already tracked. The contract address is consistent across supported EVM chains via {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} infrastructure, simplifying token discovery. The weak point is reserve transparency: Ripio describes local-currency {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} backing and a {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path, but no reliable per-token WBRL attestation was located during this pass.

wclp-ripio.title: First Chilean Peso Runtime Row
wclp-ripio.text: WCLP is Ripio's Chilean peso wFIAT token — Pharos's first CLP runtime asset, with conservative reserve metadata because public materials lack a per-token attestation feed. WCLP is Ripio's Chilean peso wFIAT token and gives Pharos its first CLP-denominated runtime asset. DefiLlama returns a live price and circulating value, while the same token address is deployed across the supported EVM set used by Ripio's suite via {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} infrastructure. CLP is grouped under OTHER until Pharos adds a first-class Chilean peso peg surface. Reserve metadata stays conservative because public materials describe the {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} backing model and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path but do not provide a per-token attestation feed.

wcop-ripio.title: Ripio's Colombian Peso wFIAT Token
wcop-ripio.text: WCOP is Ripio's Colombian peso wFIAT token with off-chain local-currency backing and multi-chain EVM issuance, overlapping with Mento COPm but using a different issuer model. WCOP is the Ripio wFIAT Colombian peso token, added through DefiLlama's price and supply coverage with verified supported-chain deployments. It overlaps thematically with Mento COPm but uses a different issuer model: off-chain local-currency {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} backing and multi-chain EVM issuance via {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} infrastructure rather than Celo's Mento reserve. COP is still grouped under OTHER pending broader peg-currency support. The main open gap is reserve evidence, since Ripio's public page does not provide a reliable per-token WCOP attestation or detailed {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} terms.

wpen-ripio.title: Peruvian Sol Coverage from Ripio
wpen-ripio.text:
Ripio's PEN-pegged wrapper extends Latam fiat coverage across six EVM chains, but per-token reserve attestation is missing.

WPEN adds Peruvian sol exposure to Pharos through Ripio's local-currency stablecoin suite. DefiLlama supplies the runtime price and circulating-supply path, and Ripio's same-address EVM deployment pattern lets Pharos track contracts on Ethereum, Base, World Chain, BNB Chain, Polygon, and Gnosis via {{term:bridge}}bridged{{/term}} routes. PEN is grouped under OTHER because it is not yet a first-class peg currency in the repo. Like the rest of the new Ripio rows, reserve transparency is the limiting factor: the backing model is described under issuer {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, but no per-token {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} feed was found to verify {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} capacity.

jaaa-janus-henderson-anemoy.title: AAA CLO Exposure as a Tokenized Fund
jaaa-janus-henderson-anemoy.text: NAV-accreting AAA CLO fund share via Anemoy/Centrifuge; permissioned, KYC-gated, not a $1 redeemable stablecoin. JAAA is not a dollar redeemable stablecoin in the usual sense: it is a NAV-accreting Janus Henderson AAA CLO fund share issued through Anemoy and Centrifuge rails. Pharos treats the Chainlink NAV feed as live reserve evidence, while the reserve-risk model stays conservative because even AAA CLO tranches are structured credit rather than cash or Treasury bills. The token has multi-chain contract coverage, but primary-market access remains permissioned and KYC-gated. The fund share is {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} structured-credit {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}, with Centrifuge {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and permissioned {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at NAV rather than open par exit.

acrdx-anemoy-apollo.title: Apollo Credit Through Anemoy
acrdx-anemoy-apollo.text: ACRDX is a permissioned, NAV-accreting share token from Anemoy and Centrifuge giving on-chain access to Apollo's diversified private credit strategy — not a par stablecoin, and not cash-like. ACRDX packages Apollo Diversified Credit Fund exposure into an Anemoy tokenized share class. The backing spans private corporate direct lending, asset-backed lending, performing credit, and opportunistic credit sleeves, so Pharos classifies the reserves as high-risk {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} credit rather than cash-like collateral. Chronicle proof-of-asset coverage provides useful NAV visibility, but {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} remains a permissioned fund process.

stac-securitize.title: CLO Fund Access on Securitize
stac-securitize.text:
A Securitize-issued BNY CLO fund token with NAV exposure to managed structured credit — not a $1-redemption stablecoin.

STAC is a Securitize-issued BNY CLO fund token with NAV-style exposure rather than a fixed dollar {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} promise. Its value depends on the fund's managed CLO portfolio and the Securitize primary-market process, which gives Pharos a clear centralized issuer and transfer-control profile with regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} underneath. Chronicle proof-of-asset coverage improves {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} transparency, but the {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} collateral risk remains structured credit.

hlscope-hamilton-lane.title: Hamilton Lane Private Credit Rail
hlscope-hamilton-lane.text: Tokenized senior secured private-credit fund priced at NAV; primary access permissioned, not an open-redemption $1 stablecoin. HLSCOPE tokenizes Hamilton Lane Senior Credit Opportunities Fund exposure through Securitize.
