The asset belongs in the NAV-token cohort: price should follow fund NAV, while subscriptions and redemptions are handled through permissioned fund infrastructure rather than open stablecoin liquidity. Reserve risk is high because the backing is private credit, not short-term cash instruments. This is an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} fund share rather than a par dollar — subscriptions and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} run through Securitize's permissioned {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} rail at NAV.

pc0000031-tradable.title: Private Credit Note, Not a Liquid Dollar
pc0000031-tradable.text: Yield-bearing private-credit note with CoinGecko price and market-cap coverage but no public APY or cashflow feed; intentionally kept out of live yield rankings, no redemption backstop assigned. Tradable PC0000031 is tracked as a {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} private-credit note ({{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} exposure) with CoinGecko price and market-cap coverage, but no reliable public APY or cashflow feed is wired. Pharos keeps it out of live yield rankings as an intentional gap and does not assign a {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} backstop because there is no public primary redemption route comparable to issuer stablecoin redemption.

pc0000033-tradable.title: Tradable Private Credit With Runtime Price
pc0000033-tradable.text: Tradable private-credit reference token admitted via runtime price and supply coverage; high-risk private-credit collateral with centralized issuer dependence and no public yield source. PC0000033 gives Pharos another Tradable private-credit reference point, admitted through runtime price and supply coverage rather than stablecoin-like liquidity. The collateral and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} profile are intentionally modeled as high-risk private credit with centralized issuer dependence, classified as {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-adjacent exposure. Yield remains a documented gap until a trustworthy public rate or cashflow source exists.

pc0000101-tradable.title: Contract-Priced Private Credit Exposure
pc0000101-tradable.text:
A NAV-style Tradable private-credit token priced from off-chain receivables rather than a $1 peg, with no published APY by design.

PC0000101 is a Tradable note whose economics come from off-chain private-credit exposure, not from a fixed $1 peg. The dashboard classifies it as a NAV-style yield-bearing {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} asset and preserves the lack of live APY as an intentional runtime gap. That avoids manufacturing yield from stale or contract-priced metadata.

pc0000089-tradable.title: Another Tradable Credit Note Under Watch
pc0000089-tradable.text:
A KYC-gated Tradable private-credit note carried at runtime price with no published yield row until reserve evidence exists.

PC0000089 follows the same treatment as the other Tradable note additions: runtime price coverage is enough to display the asset, but not enough to publish a yield row. Pharos records the credit collateral and centralized control profile as an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} exposure, while withholding live reserve and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}-backstop claims until public source evidence exists.

asusdf-astherus.title: Astherus Yield Wrapper Over USDF
asusdf-astherus.text: asUSDF is the staked, NAV-accreting wrapper of Aster's USDF, capturing yield from underlying {{term:delta-neutral}}delta-neutral{{/term}} and {{term:funding-rate}}funding-fee{{/term}} strategies on Binance/MirrorX. asUSDF is the yield-accruing Astherus wrapper around USDF, with a queue-style {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path rather than instant stablecoin conversion. The model now reflects the two-hour waiting period and a conservative partial capacity assumption because exits depend on downstream USDF liquidity. Reserve dependency is captured through the wrapped USDF exposure instead of a duplicate manual dependency entry.

mf-one-midas.title: Fasanara Strategy in Midas Form
mf-one-midas.text: Midas-wrapped Fasanara F-ONE strategy token, not a bank-reserve stablecoin; private-credit and digital-asset strategy risk with permissioned issuer redemption. mF-ONE is a Midas liquid-yield token tracking a Fasanara F-ONE strategy rather than a bank-reserve stablecoin, classified as {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-adjacent private-credit exposure. Chainlink NAV coverage gives Pharos a live valuation route, while reserves remain high-risk because the exposure is private-credit and digital-asset strategy risk. Primary liquidity depends on Midas permissioned mint and {{term:redemption}}redeem{{/term}} rails.

mglobal-midas-fasanara.title: Fasanara Global Without a Live NAV Adapter
mglobal-midas-fasanara.text: Midas-Fasanara strategy token modeled as high-risk centralized NAV-accreting strategy collateral; live reserve coverage is still waiting on a verified feed route. mGLOBAL adds another Midas-Fasanara strategy token to the dashboard, but without a verified live Chainlink NAV adapter in this pass. The asset is modeled as centralized-dependent, NAV-accreting, and high-risk {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-adjacent strategy collateral. It remains visible through market data while live reserve coverage waits for a verified feed route.

mhyper-midas.title: Hyperithm Strategy Token With NAVLink
mhyper-midas.text: Midas-wrapped Hyperithm market-neutral strategy token with a live Chainlink NAV feed; high-risk institutional strategy exposure, not a cash reserve. mHYPER wraps a Hyperithm-managed market-neutral stablecoin strategy through Midas. The checked-in metadata includes the Katana deployment and a Chainlink NAV feed, giving Pharos a live valuation route while still classifying the exposure as high-risk institutional strategy collateral. Holders rely on Midas issuer rails for primary {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}.

mmev-midas.title: MEV Capital Strategy in a Midas Wrapper
mmev-midas.text: Midas NAV token tied to MEV Capital DeFi strategy exposure with a live Chainlink NAV feed; tokenized strategy access, not a transactional stablecoin. mMEV is a Midas NAV token tied to MEV Capital DeFi strategy exposure. Pharos wires its Chainlink NAV feed for live reserve visibility but keeps the reserve-risk grade high because the underlying strategy is complex and not cash-like, classified as {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-adjacent strategy collateral. The token is best read as tokenized strategy access, not as a transactional stablecoin.

mapollo-midas.title: Apollo Crypto Strategy via Midas
mapollo-midas.text: Permissioned Midas NAV token tracking an Apollo Crypto managed yield strategy; treat the backing as high-risk digital-asset strategy exposure, not a cash reserve. mAPOLLO tracks an Apollo Crypto managed yield strategy through Midas liquid-yield rails, classified as {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-adjacent strategy exposure rather than a dollar reserve token. Chainlink NAV data supports live valuation, while the risk model treats the backing as high-risk digital-asset strategy exposure. As with the rest of the Midas strategy set, {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} depends on permissioned issuer infrastructure.

safo-spiko-usd.title: Spiko Smart Cash USD Share Class
safo-spiko-usd.text:
The USD share of Spiko/Amundi Smart Cash, using fully collateralized overnight total-return swaps — medium-risk RWA strategy exposure, not direct T-bills.

SAFO is the USD share class of Spiko / Amundi Smart Cash exposure using fully collateralized overnight total-return swaps. Pharos classifies the reserve as medium-risk {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} strategy exposure rather than direct {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} bills because the fund structure routes exposure through swap counterparties and collateral packages, with the underlying behaving more like a regulated {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}}. The primary market remains permissioned through Spiko rails, and the share price is supported by Spiko's regulated {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} stack rather than direct {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} at par.

spkcc-spiko.title: Spiko Cash and Carry Fund Share
spkcc-spiko.text:
A Spiko cash-and-carry fund share combining digital-asset basis trades with short-duration cash and Treasury collateral — yield-bearing by NAV, not pegged to $1.

SPKCC is a Spiko digital-asset cash-and-carry fund token, with Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, Base, Starknet, and Stellar deployments recorded. The reserve model is deliberately conservative because the strategy combines digital-asset {{term:basis-trade}}basis trades{{/term}} with short-duration cash and {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} collateral, structurally closer to a regulated {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} wrapped around a {{term:funding-rate}}funding-rate{{/term}} strategy under regulated {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. It is {{term:yield-bearing}}yield-bearing{{/term}} by NAV appreciation, not by a fixed stablecoin peg, and exposure to the strategy reflects {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-style fund mechanics.

eursafo-spiko.title: EUR Smart Cash Through Spiko
eursafo-spiko.text: EURSAFO is the euro share of Spiko/Amundi Smart Cash, a UCITS overnight-swap {{term:money-market-fund}}MMF{{/term}} authorized by the AMF — a fund token, not a bank-deposit reserve. EURSAFO is the euro share class of Spiko / Amundi Smart Cash exposure. The fund uses fully collateralized overnight total-return swaps with tier-1 bank counterparties, so Pharos treats the reserve as medium-risk {{term:rwa}}strategy{{/term}} exposure rather than a simple euro deposit reserve. KYC-gated Spiko fund rails control subscriptions and {{term:redemption}}redemptions{{/term}}.

eurspkcc-spiko.title: Euro Cash and Carry Fund Token
eurspkcc-spiko.text: EURSPKCC is the EUR share of Spiko's Cash & Carry FPS, blending crypto {{term:basis-trade}}basis-trade{{/term}} carry with short-duration {{term:treasury}}T-bills{{/term}} — a NAV share, not a 1:1 euro claim. EURSPKCC adds the euro-denominated Spiko cash-and-carry fund share, including the Stellar deployment verified in this pass. The asset accrues NAV from fund performance and does not target a rigid EUR 1 redemption profile. Pharos keeps the reserve-risk view high because the strategy includes digital-asset carry exposure.

uktbl-spiko.title: Spiko Treasury Bills Dollar Fund
uktbl-spiko.text: Spiko's AMF-authorized GBP money-market fund share token, NAV-based and gated through Spiko's transfer agent. UKTBL tracks Spiko's dollar {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}}-bill fund product rather than a direct stablecoin issuer reserve, structured as a regulated {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market fund{{/term}} share. The fund structure is regulated and NAV-based, with primary access through permissioned fund rails. Pharos treats the collateral as low-risk tokenized {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} exposure backed by {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}-style reporting but keeps the centralized issuer, {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} gating, and transfer-control assumptions explicit.

gbpsafo-spiko.title: GBP Smart Cash Share Class
gbpsafo-spiko.text: GBPSAFO is the GBP share of Spiko's UCITS Amundi Smart Cash {{term:money-market-fund}}MMF{{/term}} — a permissioned NAV share with overnight-swap exposure, not a retail GBP stablecoin. GBPSAFO extends Spiko Smart Cash coverage to a sterling-denominated share class. The reserve description follows the same fully collateralized overnight total-return swap structure as the USD and EUR SAFO classes, so the {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}} risk model is medium rather than pure cash. The token is best understood as a permissioned NAV share, not a retail GBP stablecoin.

eur0-usual.title: Usual's Euro Treasury Wrapper
eur0-usual.text: EUR0 is Usual's euro stablecoin minted from tokenized Eurozone T-bill collateral such as Spiko's EUTBL; centralized issuer rails. EUR0 is Usual's euro-denominated stable asset, admitted through CoinGecko market data and an Ethereum contract. The reserve thesis points to Spiko's euTBL tokenized {{term:treasury}}Treasury{{/term}} exposure rather than a simple euro bank-deposit account, so Pharos should read it as an {{term:rwa}}RWA{{/term}}-backed dependency token with centralized issuer rails. The supply is still small, but it gives the dashboard a useful euro reference from the Usual ecosystem. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} and backstop quality remain intentionally conservative until Usual-specific terms are reviewed. Spiko EUTBL is a tokenized {{term:money-market-fund}}money-market{{/term}}-style euro T-bill fund.

emxn-telcoin.title: Telcoin's Mexican Peso Cash Token
emxn-telcoin.text: eMXN is Telcoin's centralized MXN stablecoin on Polygon; reserves are issuer-reported with no public per-token feed yet. eMXN extends Telcoin's Digital Cash model from eUSD into Mexican peso settlement. CoinGecko supplies the runtime price and market-cap path, and the Polygon deployment gives Pharos a straightforward contract anchor. The issuer framing is bank-style payment infrastructure rather than a permissionless {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}}, so reserve confidence depends on Telcoin's off-chain controls and reporting. No public per-token reserve feed was found during the candidate pass. {{term:custody}}Custody{{/term}} sits with the issuer and {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} runs through Telcoin's wallet rails.

hchf-hedera-swiss-franc.title: Hedera's Small CHF Experiment
hchf-hedera-swiss-franc.text: Liquity-style CHF CDP minted from HBAR troves on Hedera; CoinGecko-only price coverage, supply data still thin. HCHF is a Swiss-franc stable asset on Hedera with CoinGecko price and market-cap coverage, while DefiLlama's row is not usable for live supply today. The candidate evidence is enough for static frontend metadata, but the collateral, governance, and redemption model still need a single-coin review before stronger report-card claims. Pharos should treat the entry as high-uncertainty CHF coverage rather than comparable to regulated fiat-backed franc issuers. As an HLiquity {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} variant, HCHF inherits HBAR-collateral {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} and Liquity-style {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} dynamics rather than any fiat {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}.

eurot-token-teknoloji.title: Token Teknoloji's Euro Token
eurot-token-teknoloji.text: EUROT is Token Teknoloji's Turkish 1:1 euro stablecoin backed by bank reserves at Ziraat Participation and Akbank, without machine-readable {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}}. EUROT is Token Teknoloji's euro-backed reserve token with Avalanche and Polygon contract coverage through CoinGecko. The issuer describes a 1:1 euro reserve model and publishes official token materials, but the candidate pass did not prove a machine-readable reserve or attestation feed. That makes EUROT useful for long-tail euro coverage while keeping reserve confidence and {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} transparency below larger MiCA-era issuers with recurring attestations.

mxne-real-mxn.title: Brale and Etherfuse's MXN Rail
mxne-real-mxn.text: Brale + Etherfuse MXN peso payment token on Base, Solana, and Stellar with issuer redemption; Base proxy-owner control flagged by CoinGecko and no live reserve feed proven in this pass. MXNe is a Mexican peso token associated with Brale and Etherfuse, with CoinGecko runtime coverage and deployments on Base, Solana, and Stellar. The public description points to 1:1 MXN backing under regulated {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} and issuer {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}}, so the model is closer to a fiat-reserve payment token than a crypto CDP. The main caveat is control risk: the Base contract has proxy-owner concerns in CoinGecko's token-risk metadata, and no live reserve feed -- nor a public independent {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} cadence -- was proven in this pass.

wmxn-ripio.title: Ripio's Missing MXN Wrapper
wmxn-ripio.text: wMXN completes Ripio's wFIAT set with a Mexican peso asset across the same EVM footprint as the rest of the suite, with reserve transparency the recurring weak point. wMXN completes the tracked Ripio wFIAT set with a Mexican peso asset deployed across the same EVM footprint as WBRL, WCLP, WCOP, and WPEN. DefiLlama provides the live price and circulating-supply path, while Ripio's official local-stablecoin page describes 1:1 local-currency {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}} backing and on/off-ramp {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} via {{term:bridge}}bridge{{/term}} infrastructure. As with the rest of the Ripio suite, the weak point is reserve transparency: public materials describe the backing model but do not expose a reliable per-token attestation feed.

jpyt-dephaser.title: A High-Risk Yen Synthetic
jpyt-dephaser.text: Algorithmic yen on Base/Optimism minted against locked USDT/USDC using an FX oracle; thin liquidity, high-dependency collateral. JPYT is Dephaser's yen-pegged token on Base and Optimism. CoinGecko describes the design as an algorithmic JPY stablecoin backed by locked USDT, so Pharos should treat the reserves as high-risk dependency collateral rather than a cash yen reserve. The runtime price and market-cap path are present, but the supply is small and the peg depends on Dephaser's mechanism, USDT collateral quality, and thin secondary liquidity. The mechanism is closer to {{term:algorithmic}}algorithmic{{/term}} FX synthesis than fiat backing, with {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} returning the locked USDT or USDC collateral rather than yen cash.

euro3-3a-dao.title: A Tiny Overcollateralized Euro CDP
euro3-3a-dao.text: EURO3 is 3A DAO's overcollateralized euro {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} stablecoin on Polygon and Linea, minted against crypto collateral in user-owned vaults. EURO3 is a 3A DAO euro stablecoin created through {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralized{{/term}} vault borrowing and burned when users repay or redeem against collateral. DefiLlama supplies the runtime price and circulating balance, with current activity split across Linea and Polygon, but there is no CoinGecko geckoId and supply is very small. The design gives Pharos a crypto-backed euro reference, while liquidity, oracle depth, and governance details remain the practical risk areas.

krwo-gimswap.title: GimSwap's KRW Voucher Token
krwo-gimswap.text: KRW-pegged stablecoin issued against Open Voucher KRW vouchers at 10,000:1 on Kaia and BNB Chain; CoinGecko flags unrestricted minting risk on BSC. KRWO is a Korean-won stable asset linked to GimSwap and Open Voucher, with CoinGecko coverage on Kaia and BNB Chain. The candidate pass points to KRW-backed issuance, but reserve and redemption evidence is still thinner than for regulated fiat issuers. CoinGecko's token-risk metadata flags unrestricted minting risk on BNB Chain, so Pharos should keep the control profile conservative until admin permissions and dilution controls are reviewed. The voucher-based issuance lacks third-party {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} and transparent {{term:custody}}custody{{/term}}, leaving the {{term:redemption}}redemption{{/term}} path entirely dependent on GimSwap's own voucher infrastructure.

xofm-mento.title: Mento's CFA Franc CDP
xofm-mento.text:
Mento's West African CFA franc CDP mints XOFm against USDm collateral on Celo, with FX-pair modeling still maturing on the reserve side.

XOFm brings Mento's local-currency {{term:cdp}}CDP{{/term}} model to the West African CFA franc on Celo. DefiLlama shows a live price and circulating supply, and the protocol description is clear: users deposit USDm into Mento troves and borrow XOFm against it, with {{term:overcollateralization}}overcollateralization{{/term}} buffers and {{term:liquidation}}liquidation{{/term}} mechanics enforcing peg discipline. Pharos now treats XOF as a first-class peg with a secondary daily FX reference, while reserve modeling stays conservative because the live Mento CDP adapter does not expose XOFm-specific trove rows yet.

xnk-kinka.title: Japanese Gold Bullion Token
xnk-kinka.text:
Kinka tokenizes one troy ounce of 99.99% Japanese gold per XNK, with Cardano- and Ethereum-issued supply against centralized issuer custody.

XNK represents one fine troy ounce equivalent of 99.99% Japanese-brand physical gold bullion held through Kinka's issuer and storage arrangements. The Cardano deployment is recorded alongside Ethereum, and the reserve model treats the backing as physical gold with centralized custody and issuer-controlled exchange terms. {{term:redemption}}Redemption{{/term}} into physical bars is possible only through the documented KYC process and size thresholds, with no public per-token {{term:attestation}}attestation{{/term}} cadence yet integrated.
